title: Stale test counts in REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md + README.md after 695-test jump
description: Round-1 explicitly jumped test totals from 481 to 695 and skip count from 11 to 10 (P14-008 and P14-044 land in HANDOFF.md/Todo.md), but two top-of-funnel docs still publish the old numbers. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md line 13 instructs the operator to verify `481 passed, 11 skipped` (will fail every time), line 20 says the tool count is `16 tools per HANDOFF.md` (HANDOFF.md no longer states 16 and the actual `[McpServerTool]` count is 22), and line 25 still says `doctor is expected to exit 1 off-Windows` even though README and P14-017 corrected this to exit 2 = PARTIAL. README.md line 5 still claims `481/492 tests passing (11 expected live-only skips)` — the round-1 P14-044 fix updated to 481/492, but the second wave that landed +214 tests never updated this badge.
recommendation: Update REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md line 13 to `695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed`; line 14 to drop the `plus the one Windows-only Credential Manager round-trip under Tests/Cli/` clause (the 10 skips are now all under `Tests/Bridge/` per HANDOFF.md:35); line 20 to `(22 tools per HANDOFF.md)` and add a one-liner reminder to count `[McpServerTool]` decorations under `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/` rather than a hard-coded number; line 25 to match README/P14-017 wording: `exit 2 off-Windows = PARTIAL (Windows-only probes skipped); exit 1 = a probe failed`. Update README.md line 5 to `695/705 tests passing (10 expected live-only skips), 0 failures, 0 warnings`.
rationale: REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md is the pre-commit verification gate — if the published expected number is wrong, the gate becomes a no-op the first time someone runs it and notices the mismatch. README is the public-facing status. Both bait operators into thinking the build is broken when it isn't.

verdict.reasoning: All five stale-doc claims verified by direct file read. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md line 13 literally reads `481 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed` while HANDOFF.md:11/35 publishes 695/10. Line 14 still references the Tests/Cli credential manager skip alongside an `11` total. Line 20 hard-codes `16 tools per HANDOFF.md` — actual `[McpServerTool]` count is 22 (confirmed via grep: 22 matches across 14 tool classes). Line 25 says `doctor is expected to exit 1 off-Windows` — DoctorCommand.cs:14-20 + 86-97 confirms the contract is exit 2 = PARTIAL (skipped probes, no reds) and exit 1 = a probe genuinely failed. README.md line 5 still reads `481/492 tests passing (11 expected live-only skips), 0 failures, 0 warnings` — P14-044 only bumped 469/480→481/492, missed the second wave to 695/705. P14-008, P14-017, P14-044 all touched related areas but none updated these specific lines: P14-008 rewrote the REGRESSION_CHECKLIST build/test sections using 481/11 (current state at that moment), P14-017 fixed the README doctor line only, P14-044 only updated the README badge to 481/492. So the finding is genuinely NEW post-Phase-14 churn. Refinement: the original recommendation says "drop the Tests/Cli credential manager round-trip clause — the 10 skips are now all under Tests/Bridge/" but that's WRONG. Verified by grep: there are 10 real `[Fact(Skip=...)]` decorators across 6 files, of which 9 are in Tests/Bridge/ and 1 is in Tests/Cli/AppIdStoreTests.cs:124 (the Credential Manager P/Invoke round-trip). HANDOFF.md:35 itself is also wrong on that point — it says "10 skips are `[Fact(Skip = "Requires real Lacerte SDK")]` across `Tests/Bridge/`" but one of them is the Windows-only Credential Manager test in Tests/Cli/ with a different skip reason. The corrected line 14 should keep the credential-manager mention but say `9 Bridge + 1 Cli = 10 total`. Also worth fixing HANDOFF.md:35 in the same sweep so the two source-of-truth docs agree.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Edit four lines in REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md plus one in README.md, and fix the matching wrong-claim in HANDOFF.md to keep the source-of-truth docs in lockstep:

1. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:13 — change `481 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed` → `695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed`.

2. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:14 — change to: `The 10 skips are the 9 `[Fact(Skip = "Requires real Lacerte SDK …")]` cases under `Tests/Bridge/` (Reader, Writer, Registration, CanUseNewApisProbe, LacerteAccessClient) plus the one Windows-only Credential Manager P/Invoke round-trip in `Tests/Cli/AppIdStoreTests.cs`.` (Do NOT drop the Cli clause as the original recommendation suggested — verified that AppIdStoreTests.cs:124 still carries `[Fact(Skip = "Windows-only — Credential Manager P/Invoke is exercised manually …")]`.)

3. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:20 — change `(16 tools per HANDOFF.md)` → `(22 tools today — count `[McpServerTool]`-decorated methods under `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/` rather than a hard-coded number, since this drifts every time a tool is added).`

4. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:25 — change `is expected to exit **1** off-Windows (no Lacerte install) — that's the documented behavior` → `is expected to exit **2** off-Windows = PARTIAL (Windows-only probes skipped, no real failures); exit 1 means a probe genuinely failed (e.g. AppID missing on a fresh checkout — run `lacerte-mcp register` to fix); exit 0 = all green (Windows + Lacerte install). Per DoctorCommand.cs:14-20.`

5. README.md:5 — change `481/492 tests passing (11 expected live-only skips), 0 failures, 0 warnings` → `695/705 tests passing (10 expected live-only skips), 0 failures, 0 warnings`.

6. (Bonus, same sweep) HANDOFF.md:35 — change `The 10 skips are `[Fact(Skip = "Requires real Lacerte SDK")]` across `Tests/Bridge/`.` → `The 10 skips are 9 `[Fact(Skip = "Requires real Lacerte SDK …")]` cases under `Tests/Bridge/` plus 1 Windows-only Credential Manager round-trip under `Tests/Cli/AppIdStoreTests.cs`.` HANDOFF.md:36 also still says `doctor → exit 1 off-Windows (expected)` — same fix as REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:25.

Do this as a single docs-only commit. No code touched, no build/test required, but follow with `& "$env:USERPROFILE\.dotnet\dotnet.exe" test …` to confirm 695/10/0 still holds at commit time.

title: ARCHITECTURE.md Invariant #7 + Configuration env table both stale after round-1
description: Two doc-consistency holes in ARCHITECTURE.md that round-1 missed: (1) Invariant #7 (line 78) still reads `The access map is consulted before every write` even though P14-002's recommendation explicitly called for tightening it to `consulted before every per-field write (WriteField)` and adding a DECISIONS entry naming WriteDetail + CreateClient as deliberate exceptions. P14-002 is checked off in Todo.md but neither edit happened. (2) The Configuration env-var table (lines 171-181) lists only 9 vars; README.md lines 87-101 now lists 12 (added `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT`, `LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE`, `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING` per P14-016/P14-033). Line 183 explicitly says `New env vars must be documented in both README.md and .env.example` — but ARCHITECTURE.md was excluded from the sync, and `.env.example` is missing `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING` and `LACERTE_SIM_EXPIRED` (both documented in README, both used by tests/code).
recommendation: (1) Edit ARCHITECTURE.md line 78 to: `**The access map is consulted before every per-field write.** `assertWritable(module, table, field, year)` runs inside `LacerteSessionManager.WriteField` before any COM call. Default-refuse on `Unknown` with `force:true` escape hatch. Detail-row writes and whole-row CreateClient are deliberately outside this gate — see DECISIONS.md "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate".` (2) Sync the ARCHITECTURE.md env-var table with README — add `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT`, `LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE`, `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING`. (3) Add `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING` and `LACERTE_SIM_EXPIRED` rows to `.env.example` so the README/.env.example/ARCHITECTURE.md trio stays in lock-step as the rule on line 183 requires.
rationale: Boundary Invariants are the load-bearing rules tools read first when adding write surfaces — an inaccurate Invariant #7 will mislead a future agent into thinking WriteDetail is gated when it isn't, or assuming the gate is broken and 'fixing' it. The env-var table drift is exactly what line 183 was written to prevent.

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED — three distinct doc-consistency gaps, all real, all sim-only fixable:

(1) P14-002 follow-through gap CONFIRMED. ARCHITECTURE.md line 78 still reads "The access map is consulted before every write" with no "per-field" qualifier. The Todo entry is checked off ([x]) but neither edit landed. DECISIONS.md section headers (grep ^##) show NO entry titled "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate" — the 15 dated entries cover bootstrap, stack, ODBC, AppID, status codes, access-map shape, sim store, two-mode parity, overlay semantic, SDK pin, WireLog, AutoReconnect, Pagination — nothing for the detail/whole-row carve-out. Per the P14-002 verdict (audit-findings.json:41) this was explicit deliverable: "Tighten Invariant #7 ... and add a DECISIONS.md entry titled 'Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate'." So Todo's checkmark misrepresents reality.

(2) ARCHITECTURE.md env-var table drift CONFIRMED. Lines 171-181 list 9 vars (APP_NAME, APP_ID, DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR, DATA_PATH, LIVE, SIMULATION, DEBUG_WIRE, DEBUG_LOG_PATH, SIM_EXPIRED). README lines 87-101 list 12 (those + DATA_ROOT + MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE + PARITY_RECORDING). No P14 task targeted ARCHITECTURE.md's env table; P14-016/P14-033 only updated README and .env.example. Line 183 of ARCHITECTURE.md itself says new env vars must be documented in both README and .env.example — silent on ARCHITECTURE.md's own table, but the divergence is exactly what an audit-target doc should not exhibit.

(3) .env.example partial gap. The audit claims both PARITY_RECORDING and SIM_EXPIRED are missing. CONFIRMED for SIM_EXPIRED (real gap — used by SimulationStore + tests, documented in README + ARCHITECTURE.md as "testing only", but absent from .env.example). PARTIALLY REFUTED for PARITY_RECORDING: P14-033's verdict (audit-findings.json:723) deliberately excluded it from .env.example ("parity recording is test-internal and would confuse operators"). So that subclaim is wrong by P14 design, but SIM_EXPIRED gap stands.

NOT a duplicate. P14-002 is checked off but unimplemented for the doc deliverables. P14-016/P14-033 covered README and .env.example only. P14-035 fixed the Module Boundaries Bridge row in ARCHITECTURE.md but not the env table. The finding catches genuine follow-through holes and a never-addressed gap.

Severity: medium-to-high. Boundary Invariants are load-bearing — an inaccurate Invariant #7 will mislead the next agent who reads it before adding a write surface. Env-table drift across three docs erodes the rule the docs themselves enforce.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-edit composite fix, all sim-only:

(1) ARCHITECTURE.md line 78 — replace the current "The access map is consulted before every write. assertWritable(module, table, field, year) runs in the tool layer (or session manager — pick one and be consistent) before any COM call. Default-refuse on Unknown with force:true escape hatch." with: "**The access map is consulted before every per-field write.** `assertWritable(module, table, field, year)` runs inside `LacerteSessionManager.WriteField` before any COM call. Default-refuse on `Unknown` with `force:true` escape hatch. Detail-row writes (`WriteDetail`) and whole-row `CreateClient` are deliberately outside this gate — see DECISIONS.md 'Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate'." Also drop the "(or session manager — pick one and be consistent)" parenthetical since the location is now decided (session manager).

(2) DECISIONS.md — add the dated entry P14-002's verdict already specified verbatim: title "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate", **Chosen** = these two paths bypass AssertWritable, **Why** = the map's `module|table|field` key shape (table = DATA-table number 1–7 with enumerable C{t}_{n} columns) cannot address per-client detail-file rows (no primary key, no enumerable column set) or whole-row CreateClient payloads, **Safety nets relied on instead** = `DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite` (Series/Code/StateAbbr/TSJ shape gates, line ~96) for details and `CreateClient`'s ClientID length check + SDK-side row validation for creates, **Affected paths** = `LacerteSessionManager.WriteDetail:681-752` and `LacerteSessionManager.CreateClient:758+`. Optionally drop a one-line `// No AssertWritable — see DECISIONS.md 'Detail-row + whole-row writes...'` at each call site.

(3) ARCHITECTURE.md env-var table (lines 171-181) — add the three rows missing relative to README: `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` (root scanned by `lacerte_list_datapaths`, default `C:\Lacerte`), `LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE` (forces file-based AppID store; auto-on off-Windows), `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING` (testing only — path to parity-recording JSON consumed by `BothModesData`). Then either (a) revise the line-183 rule to read "New env vars must be documented in README.md, .env.example, AND this table" so the rule names its own surface, or (b) consolidate by replacing the table with a single sentence pointing at README's `Environment variables (full reference)` section as the single source of truth and delete the duplicate table here entirely — the latter is preferable since it eliminates the drift surface permanently.

(4) .env.example — add a `LACERTE_SIM_EXPIRED=` row with a one-line comment ("Testing only: 1 simulates an expired 24h Intuit session for error-path tests"). Do NOT add `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING` — P14-033 deliberately excluded it as test-internal that would confuse operators (audit-findings.json:723), and that decision should be respected.

Skip the audit's framing that all four absences are equal — PARITY_RECORDING's absence from .env.example is by design.

title: Multiple DECISIONS.md entries owed for round-1 architectural additions
description: Round-1 added four load-bearing architectural choices to the codebase, but only three (WireLog redaction, AutoReconnect backoff, Pagination contract — P14-037) got dated DECISIONS.md entries. The missing entries: (1) P14-002 explicitly recommended a new DECISIONS.md entry titled "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate" — never added. (2) P14-004 introduced the canonical `try/finally + Marshal.ReleaseComObject` COM-lifetime pattern as a project-wide invariant for every dynamic dispatch site in Writer/Reader — no decision entry explains the pattern, so a future bridge wrapper added without it will silently leak. (3) P14-005 replaced the unsynchronized idempotency cache with `ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock(key, payload, body)` using per-key `SemaphoreSlim` — no decision entry pins the lock-scope rationale or the constants (`MaxIdempotencyEntries`, `IdempotencyTtl`). (4) P14-050 added `Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs` as a new architectural layer that fires *before* WireLog + AcquireWriter on every dynamic dispatch path — material enough to warrant ordering rationale (a future contributor adding a new bridge method has no doc telling them to call it first).
recommendation: Append four dated 2026-05-30 entries to DECISIONS.md, each ~15-25 lines following the existing Chosen/Why/Alternatives/Downstream shape: (1) `Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate` — name WriteDetail (line ~681) and CreateClient (line ~758), explain the map's M|T|F key shape can't address detail rows or whole-row creates, point at DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite + CreateClientTools 8-char/regex/TaxType gates as the actual safety nets. (2) `COM lifetime: try/finally + Marshal.ReleaseComObject on every dynamic dispatch` — cite Writer.cs/Reader.cs as the canonical pattern, point at CanUseNewApisProbe.cs:96-103 as the original template, mark any new bridge call site missing the pattern as a CI-failable lint candidate. (3) `Idempotency cache: per-key SemaphoreSlim + 24h TTL + 10k entry cap` — cite ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock, explain why per-key beats global lock + why TTL+cap eviction is lazy/opportunistic. (4) `Bridge input validation layer fires before WireLog + COM dispatch` — explain ordering rationale (no PII in log file from rejected calls, no COM allocation for trivially-bad inputs), list the four call sites that currently route through it, mark as the canonical entry point for any new dynamic bridge method.
rationale: DECISIONS.md is the audit trail that prevents the next agent from re-debating settled architectural questions. The CLAUDE.md operating-system section explicitly tells agents to read DECISIONS.md when their task touches a previously-debated area — silent landings undermine that workflow.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading DECISIONS.md (276 lines, only 14 entries — none cover any of the four claimed gaps) and cross-referencing the Phase-14 code that landed.

CONFIRMED — all four entries are missing:
1. **P14-002 carve-out** — `LacerteSessionManager.cs:792-793` and `:881-882` literally contain comments saying `// P14-002 — no AssertWritable here; see DECISIONS.md "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate"`. That DECISIONS.md entry **does not exist** — grep for "Detail-row|access-map gate" returns zero matches in DECISIONS.md. The code now points readers at a non-existent doc. Additionally, P14-002's accepted recommendation said to tighten ARCHITECTURE.md Invariant #7 to "consulted before every per-field write (WriteField)" — line 78 still reads "consulted before every write." So P14-002 is a TWO-part half-fix (broken doc reference + spec wording still misleading).
2. **P14-004 COM lifetime pattern** — Writer.cs/Reader.cs now follow the try/finally + `Marshal.ReleaseComObject` pattern (confirmed in code), but no DECISIONS.md entry pins this as the project-wide invariant. A future contributor adding a bridge method has nothing to point them at it.
3. **P14-005 per-key SemaphoreSlim** — `LacerteSessionManager.cs:105-106, 115, 1317-1376` confirms the `_idempotencyLocks` ConcurrentDictionary, `ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock<T>`, `IdempotencyTtl = 24h`, and the 10k cap landed. No DECISIONS.md entry pins the lock-scope rationale or the constants.
4. **P14-050 BridgeInputValidation** — `Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs` exists (confirmed via `ls Bridge/`). No DECISIONS.md entry explains why it must fire before WireLog + AcquireWriter on every dynamic-dispatch path.

NOT a duplicate of P14-037 — that task explicitly covered only WireLog/AutoReconnect/Pagination (the three entries that did land). The four entries this finding flags are different subsystems, all Phase-14 additions.

NOT a duplicate of P14-002/P14-004/P14-005/P14-050 themselves — those tasks shipped the code/comments but skipped the doc entries the originals' Do-instructions either explicitly required (P14-002) or implicitly required (P14-004 fix introduces a project-wide invariant; P14-005 fix introduces new constants; P14-050 introduces a new architectural layer). The Phase-14 work was completed minus this documentation tail.

Pure docs edit, sim-friendly, no Windows/Lacerte dependency. Highest-value among the four: the P14-002 broken reference in code comments is actively misleading — a reader who follows the pointer will conclude the operating-system is broken or that they're looking at stale code.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Append four dated 2026-05-30 entries to DECISIONS.md (Chosen/Why/Alternatives/Downstream shape, ~15-25 lines each), and fix the two collateral half-fixes in P14-002:

(1) **"Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate"** — Cite `LacerteSessionManager.WriteDetail` (~line 780+) and `CreateClient` (~line 870+), explain the map's `{module}|{table}|{field}` key shape cannot address detail rows (no primary key, no enumerable field set) or whole-row creates (multi-field atomic). Point at the actual safety nets: `DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite` (series/code/stateAbbr/tsj gates) for details, and `CreateClientTools` 8-char ClientID cap + `^[A-Z0-9]+$` regex + TaxType-Module match for creates. **Also fix the two collateral half-fixes**: (a) tighten `ARCHITECTURE.md:78` Invariant #7 to read "consulted before every per-field write (`WriteField`); detail-row and whole-row writes have separate client-side gates — see DECISIONS.md 'Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate'"; (b) verify the in-code comments at `LacerteSessionManager.cs:792-793, 881-882` now point at an entry that actually exists.

(2) **"COM lifetime: try/finally + Marshal.ReleaseComObject on every dynamic dispatch"** — Cite `Writer.cs` (4 sites) and `Reader.cs` (1 site) as the post-P14-004 canonical pattern, point at `CanUseNewApisProbe.cs:96-103` as the original template, mark any new bridge call site missing the pattern as a future lint candidate. Reject the cached-instance alternative (would change lifecycle semantics; per-call release is correct for static utility classes).

(3) **"Idempotency cache: per-key SemaphoreSlim + 24h TTL + 10k entry cap"** — Cite `LacerteSessionManager.ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock` (line 1317), explain why per-key beats one global lock (parallel different keys remain concurrent; only same-key callers serialize), why TTL+cap eviction is lazy/opportunistic (no timer, no background thread, scrubber runs only when the cap is hit on a store), and why the semaphore is intentionally never removed from the dictionary on release (cheap memory leak vs. a recreate-race trap). Constants live in code, not env — tuning them silently changes the contract.

(4) **"Bridge input validation layer fires before WireLog + COM dispatch"** — Cite `Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs` as a new architectural layer introduced by P14-050. Explain the ordering rationale: (a) no rejected-call PII reaches the log file, (b) no COM RCW allocation for trivially-bad inputs (control chars, oversized strings, non-primitive JSON values), (c) the validation message is the operator-actionable surface, not a deep stack trace. List the four call sites that currently route through it. Mark as the canonical entry point for any new dynamic bridge method; new methods that skip it bypass the security gate silently.

Verify the fix end-to-end by grepping `DECISIONS.md "Detail-row` and confirming the code-comment pointer in `LacerteSessionManager.cs:792` now resolves to a real entry. Pure markdown edits, no test or build changes — `dotnet build` should remain green at 695 passing.

title: LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR documented but never read by any code
description: README.md line 92, ARCHITECTURE.md line 175, and .env.example line 9 all advertise LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR=2024 as a 'recommended' env var that supplies a default year when a tool call omits one. The constructor of LacerteSessionManager reads LACERTE_SIMULATION, LACERTE_LIVE, and LACERTE_APP_NAME but NEVER reads LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR. The only fallback Register() and CreateClient gates use is `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` (line 191/220), so any operator who follows the documentation and sets LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR=2024 silently has it ignored. The two references in StatusCodes.cs (lines 149/233) are remediation strings only — they tell the operator to set the var that the code does not consult. A non-numeric value would also be accepted with no error because the var is never parsed.
recommendation: Either (a) wire LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR into the constructor: parse with int.TryParse, validate >= 2018, store as a field, and have RequireContextOrFallback() / Register() / CreateClient prefer it over DateTime.UtcNow.Year; OR (b) remove all references from README/.env.example/ARCHITECTURE/StatusCodes remediation and add an explicit DECISIONS.md entry that the year always comes from lacerte_set_context. Add a unit test + a doctor probe that warns 'LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR set but currently unused' or confirms it is honored.
rationale: This is the most operator-visible config drift in the project: the documented surface lies about what code actually does. A user who carefully reads the env vars and sets a default year will be confused when tools still demand year on every set-context call, or when CreateClient timestamps a 2026 return because DateTime.UtcNow won. The disconnect was missed by every round-1 lens because none of them cross-referenced documented env vars against code reads.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by direct evidence. `grep LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR` across the entire tree produces 8 hits — all in docs (.env.example:9, ARCHITECTURE.md:175, README.md:60+92), error-mapping research (docs/research/agents/05-error-mapping.md), and StatusCodes.cs:149/233 remediation strings. Zero hits in any executable code path. Confirmed by enumerating every `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable` call: the only env vars read are LACERTE_SIMULATION, LACERTE_LIVE, LACERTE_APP_NAME, LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE, APPDATA, LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE, LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH, LACERTE_DATA_PATH (DoctorCommand only), LACERTE_SIM_EXPIRED, LACERTE_DATA_ROOT, LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING. LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR is conspicuously absent. The bug is also self-documented: LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 217-219 carry the comment "otherwise fall back to the env-default-year (Phase 11 task), otherwise current calendar year as a last-resort lower bound" — a known unimplemented Phase 11 task that Phase 14 missed. Compounding the docs lie: README:92 claims the var supplies a "Default year used when `lacerte_set_context` omits one" — but SessionTools.cs:71 declares `int taxYear` as a non-nullable mandatory parameter, so the documented behavior is impossible. Phase 14 didn't catch this: P14-016 (missing-from-docs vars) and P14-033 (DATA_ROOT/PARITY/FORCE_FILE_STORE) address the inverse problem (vars read by code but not documented); P14-062 hit the exact same pattern for LACERTE_DSN (documented but never read by code) but did not look at the other env vars. So this is a new, real, in-session-fixable, operator-visible config drift bug.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Wire LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR end-to-end (option (a) in the original — cleaner than deleting because there are 3+ real fallback sites that currently use `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` as a degraded default). Concrete steps, all sim-safe:

1. **Parse + store in ctor.** In `LacerteSessionManager.cs:127-157`, after `_appName = TryGet(...)`, add:
   ```csharp
   var rawYear = TryGet(resolved, "LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR");
   if (rawYear != null) {
       if (!int.TryParse(rawYear, NumberStyles.Integer, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, out var y) || y < 2018) {
           throw new InvalidOperationException($"LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR='{rawYear}' invalid; must be integer >= 2018.");
       }
       _defaultTaxYear = y;
   }
   ```
   Store as `private readonly int? _defaultTaxYear`. Fail-loud at startup (not silent on bad value) per Boundary Invariant on config.

2. **Prefer it over `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` at all fallback sites.** Replace `Context?.Year ?? DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` with `Context?.Year ?? _defaultTaxYear ?? DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` at:
   - `Register()` line 191 (taxYearArg for WireLog)
   - `Register()` line 220 (taxYear for `_bridge.Register`)
   - Any `CreateClient` gate that uses UtcNow.Year as a degraded default (verify by grepping `UtcNow.Year` in LacerteSessionManager.cs)

3. **Update `lacerte_set_context` to honor the default when omitted.** Change `int taxYear` to `int? taxYear = null` in `SessionTools.cs:71`, then `var resolvedYear = taxYear ?? _session.DefaultTaxYear ?? throw new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.InValidTaxYear, new { reason = "taxYear required when LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR unset" });`. This is what the README already promises.

4. **Expose via SessionStatus + doctor.** Add `defaultTaxYear` to the SessionStatus response and a Doctor probe row: `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR set to YYYY (default for set_context)` or `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR unset (set_context will require explicit year)`. Doctor probe is the cure for silent ignored-config.

5. **Tests** (all sim-safe, in `SessionManagerTests.cs` + `SessionToolsTests.cs`):
   - Env-parse: valid (2024), invalid ("abc"), too-low (2017), null/unset
   - Register WireLog payload reflects the env default when Context is null
   - `lacerte_set_context` with omitted year + env set → uses env
   - `lacerte_set_context` with omitted year + env unset → throws InValidTaxYear (with operator-actionable reason)
   - `lacerte_set_context` with explicit year always wins over env

6. **DECISIONS.md entry**: dated, "LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR honored as `set_context.taxYear` default and as the Register fallback over calendar-year." Cite that the calendar-year fallback would silently file 2026 returns on TY24 boxes.

Do NOT take option (b) (delete from docs) — the explicit "Phase 11 task" code comment plus the multiple `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.Year` fallback sites mean the operator actually needs this var; deleting it would leave the year-fallback path stuck on calendar year forever.

title: LACERTE_APP_ID env var documented but ignored; only Credential Manager / file is read
description: .env.example line 6 instructs the operator to set LACERTE_APP_ID=00000000-... and warns 'do NOT change AppID after first registration'. Bridge/Registration.cs:GetStoredAppId() and Cli/Storage/AppIdStore.cs ONLY read from Windows Credential Manager (target 'lacerte-mcp') or the JSON file at %APPDATA%/lacerte-mcp/config.json. There is no code path that consults the LACERTE_APP_ID env var. A new operator who follows the .env.example will be told their AppID is not persisted (doctor: AppID GUID FAIL) and Register() will throw AppNotRegistered (synthetic) even though the env var is explicitly set. There is no documented precedence rule (env vs Credential Manager vs file) because env-var support does not exist at all.
recommendation: Pick a path: either (a) add env-var support in AppIdStore.Get() / Registration.GetStoredAppId() with documented precedence (env > Credential Manager > file), validate that the env value is a parseable Guid, and add a doctor probe that surfaces which backend is supplying the AppID; OR (b) delete LACERTE_APP_ID from .env.example and replace it with a comment saying 'AppID is minted by `lacerte-mcp register` into Windows Credential Manager — never set via env'. Whichever path is chosen, update DECISIONS.md so future contributors do not re-introduce the documentation.
rationale: The .env.example is the literal first-contact onboarding artifact and it documents a non-existent code path. Round-1 lenses checked Credential Manager behavior but did not audit env-var docs vs code reality. The operator who fills out the template gets a confusing AppID-not-persisted state with no diagnostic that explains why their setting was ignored.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three claims directly. (1) `.env.example` lines 4-6 still document `LACERTE_APP_ID=00000000-...` with a stern "do NOT change AppID after first registration" comment, strongly implying the env var is read at runtime. (2) `AppIdStore.Get()` (LacertMCP.Cli/Storage/AppIdStore.cs:101-112) and `Registration.GetStoredAppId()` (LacertMCP.Server/Bridge/Registration.cs:117-128) read ONLY from Windows Credential Manager (target `lacerte-mcp`) with a JSON-file fallback at `%APPDATA%/lacerte-mcp/config.json`. Neither consults `LACERTE_APP_ID`. Grep of the whole repo confirms `LACERTE_APP_ID` appears only in `.env.example`, `README.md`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` — never in any C# file. (3) `StatusCommand.cs:51` does read `LACERTE_APP_NAME` from env, but never `LACERTE_APP_ID`. README.md:94 and ARCHITECTURE.md:174 already correctly label `LACERTE_APP_ID` as "runtime read-only — source of truth is Credential Manager", so the docs are inconsistent: README/ARCHITECTURE warn it's ignored, .env.example treats it as a real knob. Phase-14 audit findings P14-016 and P14-033 cover the README env-var table (missing `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT`, `LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE`, `LACERTE_PARITY_RECORDING`) and P14-033 did mirror those into .env.example (lines 27-32 confirm), but neither addressed the misleading `LACERTE_APP_ID` line. New, real, actionable, pure docs fix — no Windows/Lacerte needed. Following ARCHITECTURE.md:180 ("new env vars must be documented in both README.md and .env.example"), the fix must keep .env.example consistent with the README/ARCHITECTURE wording.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Take option (b) — do NOT add env-var support. Adding an env > CredMan > file precedence chain would (i) break Boundary Invariant #8 (Registration happens ONCE at startup from a single source of truth), (ii) re-open an AppID-leak surface that DECISIONS.md (2026-05-30 "AppID GUID in Windows Credential Manager") explicitly closed by moving the GUID out of files/env, and (iii) invent a new contract for a one-operator personal tool. Concrete edit to `.env.example` lines 4-6: replace the two `LACERTE_APP_*` lines with a single comment block matching the README/ARCHITECTURE wording: `# Identity registered with Lacerte. AppName is read at runtime (default: LacerteMCP).` then `LACERTE_APP_NAME=LacerteMCP` then a separate comment: `# AppID is NOT set here. The GUID is minted by 'lacerte-mcp register' into Windows Credential Manager (target=lacerte-mcp, account=app-id). Off-Windows or with LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE=1 it falls back to %APPDATA%/lacerte-mcp/config.json. See DECISIONS.md 2026-05-30 for rationale.` Remove the `LACERTE_APP_ID=00000000-...` line entirely so no operator pastes a zero-GUID and wonders why register still complains. Cross-check: README.md:94 already states this; no edit there needed. Optionally add a one-line DECISIONS.md entry dated today: "`.env.example` does not include `LACERTE_APP_ID` — the GUID is never read from env to preserve a single source of truth (CredMan, file-fallback only)." No code change, no test change required.

title: WireLog.Redact nukes the actionable "reason" key in every error envelope
description: P14-018 added "reason" and "rawError" to WireLog._sensitiveKeys to scrub COM-echoed taxpayer data, and P14-019 made WrapToolHandler.SerializeError run the same Redact pass on the wire envelope. The two fixes collide. Almost every structured throw in the codebase puts the actionable diagnostic in context["reason"]: "Series is required.", "dbf must match the DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF shape...", "appId length 130 exceeds 128-char cap.", "No AppID minted. Run `lacerte-mcp register` first.", "Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint.", etc. — see BridgeInputValidation.cs (10+ throws), DetailsTools.cs:146/165/177/189/203, CreateClientTools.cs:76/89/100/111, LacerteSessionManager.cs:213/365/661/742/1009/1357, FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:206/211/215/220, every Bridge/* throw. Test WrapToolHandlerRedactionTests.Run_ErrorContext_RedactsReasonKey explicitly asserts the value becomes "***". Net effect: the LLM consuming an error sees `{"statusName":"DetailWriteInvalid","userMessage":"...client-side validation...","remediation":"Fix the failed field per the validation message","context":{"field":"series","reason":"***"}}` — "per the validation message" is the very message that was just scrubbed.
recommendation: Treat error envelopes as a different redaction class from disk-log records. Either (a) remove "reason" and "rawError" from WireLog._sensitiveKeys and instead add a separate value-shape regex inside WrapToolHandler.SerializeError that scrubs SSN/EIN/phone/email patterns from "reason" / "rawError" string values — preserving the structured diagnostic prefix; or (b) split the redaction surface: WireLog.RedactForDisk keeps the bare-key alternation (disk PII risk) and WireLog.RedactForWire scrubs only definite-PII keys and runs a regex pass over reason/rawError values. Add a regression test asserting that BridgeInputValidation.ValidateDbfName("BAD;",...) produces an error envelope whose reason still contains the literal phrase "DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF".
rationale: Highest-traffic LLM-actionability hole in the project. The audit's existing P14-018/P14-019 fixes were each correct in isolation but compose into a regression that makes every structured error message useless to the LLM. There's no point listing remediations like "Fix the failed field per the validation message" when the validation message has been replaced with three asterisks.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading source. (1) WireLog.cs:109 explicitly adds "rawError" and "reason" to _sensitiveKeys via P14-018, so RedactNode replaces them with JsonValue.Create("***") wholesale (line 318). (2) WrapToolHandler.cs:94 (SerializeError) runs WireLog.Redact on the serialized envelope JSON per P14-019. (3) WrapToolHandlerRedactionTests.cs:82-99 (Run_ErrorContext_RedactsReasonKey) explicitly asserts the literal "555-66-7777" disappears from a reason value of "Late-bound COM call failed: SSN 555-66-7777" — i.e. the test ENSHRINES the over-redaction. (4) The throw sites that use ["reason"] as the actionable diagnostic key are pervasive and verified: Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs has 12+ such throws (lines 117/136/159/170/183/206/318/343/365/396/427/476), Tools/CreateClientTools.cs has 8+ (lines 76/89/100/111/128/139/150/172), Tools/DetailsTools.cs has 4 (146/165/177/189/203), Schema/FieldAccessMapLoader.cs has 5 (206/211/215/220/228), and every Bridge/Reader+Writer+Registration/CanUseNewApisProbe path. (5) The error envelope shape includes `remediation: "Fix the failed field per the validation message"` while the validation message — which lives in context.reason — has been blanked. The two Phase-14 fixes were each correct in isolation but compose into a functional regression on the LLM-actionability surface, which is the project's primary purpose (an MCP server consumed by an LLM). Not a duplicate: no Phase-14 task addresses the wire-vs-disk asymmetry of WHAT keys to redact (only the "where to redact" gap). Fully implementable off-Windows: pure WireLog.cs + WrapToolHandler.cs + new test, all unit-testable in sim.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Split the redaction surface into two callers so disk-log redaction (paranoid) and wire-envelope redaction (LLM-actionable) diverge cleanly:

1) In src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs, remove "rawError" and "reason" from _sensitiveKeys (line 109) AND from the _redactRegex alternation (line 137). These were the only two non-PII-shaped keys in the set — every other entry is a definite-PII column name. WireLog.Record path is unaffected for genuine PII keys; it loses key-name redaction of reason/rawError on the disk log, which is OK because the actionable-diagnostic strings written by the codebase don't contain raw PII (verified by spot-reading 30+ throw sites — they say things like "DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF" and "appId length 130 exceeds 128-char cap.").

2) Add a new public method WireLog.ScrubPiiValues(string) that runs a value-shape regex pass over a JSON document, replacing matches in any string value (not key) with "***". Cover SSN (^\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}$ and unanchored), EIN (^\d{2}-\d{7}$), US phone (10-11 digits with separators), email (RFC-5322 simplified), and DOB formats (M/D/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD). This is the same defense the finding's option (b) describes but as a value-pattern scrubber rather than a key-name scrubber, so structured diagnostics survive while literal PII embedded in a COM ex.Message gets blanked.

3) In src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs, change both Redact calls (lines 61 and 94) to a composition: `WireLog.ScrubPiiValues(WireLog.Redact(json))`. Order matters — Redact runs first to nuke definite-PII columns (TaxpayerSSN, EmailID, etc.) by key, then ScrubPiiValues catches any PII-shaped values that leaked through reason/rawError.

4) Replace the misnamed test WrapToolHandlerRedactionTests.Run_ErrorContext_RedactsReasonKey with two new tests:
   (a) Run_ErrorContext_PreservesReasonDiagnosticPrefix — throw with context.reason = "dbf must match the DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF shape (uppercase ASCII alphanumerics + single dot, <= 16 chars)." and assert the envelope JSON CONTAINS the literal substring "DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF". This is the regression sentinel the finding asks for.
   (b) Run_ErrorContext_ScrubsPiiEmbeddedInReason — throw with context.reason = "COM call failed: SSN 555-66-7777" and assert (i) the SSN substring is gone, AND (ii) the substring "COM call failed:" survives. This proves the new value-pattern scrubber works without nuking the diagnostic prefix.

5) Audit BridgeInputValidation.cs's 12+ reason strings (lines 117/136/159/170/183/206/318/343/365/396/427/476) to confirm none embeds raw user input that could be PII-shaped. Currently all of them embed only lengths, char codes, and field NAMES (not values), so the new pipeline preserves all of them intact while still catching anything a future maintainer adds.

This restores the wire envelope's LLM-actionability without re-opening the disk-log PII hole P14-018 was trying to plug — disk records still go through the original Redact-only path via WireLog.WriteRecord, which is unchanged.

title: BridgeInputValidation throws AppNotRegistered for unrelated appId-length/charset failures
description: ValidateAppId raises LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.AppNotRegistered = 9006) when the appId exceeds 128 chars or contains COM-unsafe characters. AppNotRegistered's StatusInfo says "Any tool other than lacerte_register was called before a successful Register() landed" with remediation "Run lacerte_register once to grant consent and sign in." Neither is true: the operator DID register, the AppID just has bad shape. An LLM following the remediation will re-run lacerte_register (which is idempotent and succeeds), then retry the same call, get the same error, loop. The correct synthetic code does not exist — there is no AppIdInvalid 9xxx slot.
recommendation: Add a new synthetic code SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidAppId = 9103 (auth-lifecycle range) with userMessage "The persisted AppID is malformed or oversized — registration storage is corrupt." and remediation "Run `lacerte-mcp unregister` to clear the bad AppID, then `lacerte-mcp register` to mint a fresh GUID." Update BridgeInputValidation.ValidateAppId both throw-sites to use it. Update WrapToolHandlerTests/SyntheticStatusCodesTests with the new entry. Keep the context dict's ["reason"] explanation (after fixing finding #1) so the LLM has the precise charcode/length.
rationale: Misclassified errors send LLMs into infinite retry loops. "Run lacerte_register again" is the canonical wrong remediation for any bridge-layer validation issue that happens to throw 9006. Synthetic codes only buy actionability when each code corresponds to one cause + one remedy.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs lines 109-138 and SyntheticStatusCodes.cs lines 110-114. ValidateAppId throws SyntheticStatusCodes.AppNotRegistered (9006) for both length-exceeded and unsafe-char failures, but 9006's StatusInfo unambiguously says the operator never registered, with remediation "Run lacerte_register once to grant consent and sign in." For a malformed appId that's already persisted (or passed through from env per the file comment lines 68-71), running lacerte_register either no-ops (idempotent) or re-mints the GUID without clearing the bad source, so an LLM following the remediation can loop. The misclassification is cemented in tests at BridgeInputValidationTests.cs:146 and :423 — both assert ex.StatusCode == AppNotRegistered for bad-shape appIds — so the broken UX is part of the regression contract right now, not just an oversight. Not a Phase-14 duplicate: P14-050 introduced BridgeInputValidation but its refined recommendation focused on what to validate, never on which status code to emit. No other Phase-14 finding touched the appId-status-code mapping. Slot 9103 is free: P14-064's refined recommendation explicitly dropped the "9103 for idempotency cache eviction" idea, and the as-shipped code leaves 9103 unallocated (only 9101 ReAuthRequired and 9102 IdempotencyConflict exist in the 9100-9199 auth-lifecycle range). UnregisterCommand.cs exists in src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/ (confirmed via Glob), so the proposed remediation chain is real. Sim-only and trivial: add one StatusTable entry, swap the two throw sites in ValidateAppId, update the two test assertions plus a SyntheticStatusCodesTests row. No Windows/Lacerte dependency.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `public const int InvalidAppId = 9103;` in SyntheticStatusCodes.cs (9100-9199 auth-lifecycle range — confirmed free since P14-064 dropped its 9103 idea) with a StatusInfo entry: name "InvalidAppId", Severity.Error, userMessage "The supplied AppID is malformed or oversized (failed bridge-boundary shape check before COM dispatch).", remediation "If the AppID came from registration storage, run `lacerte-mcp unregister` then `lacerte-mcp register` to mint a fresh GUID. If it came from a LACERTE_APPID env var, fix or unset that env var." (broader than the original "storage is corrupt" wording because the file comments at BridgeInputValidation.cs:68-71 explicitly note operators can pass appId through from env). Swap both throw sites in ValidateAppId (lines 109 and 128) from `SyntheticStatusCodes.AppNotRegistered` to `SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidAppId`, keeping the existing context dict (op/field/length/maxLength/index/charCode/reason) unchanged. Update BridgeInputValidationTests.cs:146 and :423 to assert InvalidAppId instead of AppNotRegistered. Add one row to SyntheticStatusCodesTests verifying StatusTable[InvalidAppId] returns the expected name + remediation. Sanity-check that nothing else in the codebase asserts on or branches on 9006 specifically (Grep for AppNotRegistered — there are 4 hits, all already enumerated; only the 2 in BridgeInputValidationTests need updating, plus any in WrapToolHandlerTests if it tests the wrapped envelope shape for this code).

title: Bulk-update flow forces N tool calls; no batched write API exists
description: REQUIREMENTS §1.2 calls out bulk-updates (mailing addresses, EF flags, preparer assignments) as a first-class operator scenario, and the WorkflowPrompts.cs `lacerte_bulk_field_update` prompt explicitly walks the LLM through `lacerte_field_write` invoked once per client. There is no `lacerte_field_write_bulk` / `lacerte_field_write_many` tool, no array-of-clients overload, and no session-level helper that streams the writes. For a firm with hundreds of clients the model must issue N MCP round-trips, each going through WrapToolHandler+JSON serialize+idempotency hash+access-map probe+wire call. The `lacerte_bulk_field_update` prompt even tells the model to STOP on first error, so a single network glitch in client 50/300 leaves the batch in a half-applied state with no resume primitive. There is no progress event, no streaming response, no transactional batch — the operator's primary write workflow has zero throughput optimization.
recommendation: Add `LacerteFieldWriteBulk(int table, string field, IList<{clientNumber, value}> targets, bool dryRun, string idempotencyKeyPrefix)` that loops the writes inside one tool call, returns a structured `{succeeded[], failed[{clientNumber, statusCode, userMessage}], skipped[]}` envelope, and supports continue-on-error vs stop-on-error. Suffix each per-row idempotency key with the clientNumber so a retry of the whole batch replays cleanly. The session-side body can reuse the existing `WriteField` chokepoint (so access-map / read-only / lock semantics stay one-source-of-truth) — only the tool surface and per-row error-aggregation are new. Add at least one FullFlowTests case that bulk-updates 5 sim clients and asserts {succeeded:5, failed:0}; add another that injects a failure on row 3 and asserts the response carries succeeded:2 + failed:1 + skipped:2 (or succeeded:4 + failed:1 in continue mode).
rationale: This is the highest-volume real-world flow in REQUIREMENTS. Today it costs ~5x the round-trips it needs and has no atomic-batch recovery story; the existing prompt is a workaround that papers over the missing primitive.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. FieldWriteTools.cs exposes only the single-target `LacerteFieldWrite` (one (clientNumber, field, value) per call). There is no `LacerteFieldWriteBulk`, `LacerteFieldWriteMany`, or array-of-clients overload anywhere in src/ (grep across LacertMCP.Server/Cli/Tests returned zero matches for Bulk/Many/Batch write APIs). The lacerte_bulk_field_update MCP prompt (WorkflowPrompts.cs:156-213) literally instructs the model to loop `lacerte_field_write` one-client-at-a-time with `STOP on first failure` — confirming the finding's claim that the prompt is a workaround for a missing primitive. REQUIREMENTS.md line 12 lists "Bulk-updating fields across many clients (mailing addresses, EF flags, preparer assignments)" as the operator's #2 scenario, so this is squarely on the product critical path. Phase-14 ships 71 tasks (P14-001..P14-071) — none introduces a batched write API; if anything, P14-005 (per-key idempotency lock), P14-042 (per-write payload hash), P14-043 (per-op undo), and P14-064 (constant-time key compare) all amortize across N round-trips and would directly benefit from a single bulk entrypoint. Fully sim-implementable off-Windows: the proposed bulk wrapper just loops the existing `WriteField` chokepoint (lines 640-778), which already encapsulates context check, DATA6/7 read-only gate (P14-054), idempotency lock+replay, AssertWritable, WireLog, dry-run snapshot/restore, and TY21+ branching — so the bulk tool inherits every existing invariant for free and only adds per-row error aggregation. Useful: today a 300-client mailing-address change is 300 MCP round-trips × (JSON serialize + WrapToolHandler + idempotency hash + access-map probe + log line) plus the LLM's per-call token overhead, with no resume primitive when a transient COM error trips row 50/300. The finder's "5x round-trips" understates it — it's N→1. The recommendation is sound; minor tightening below.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `LacerteFieldWriteBulk` in a new `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/FieldWriteBulkTools.cs` that loops the existing `LacerteSessionManager.WriteField` chokepoint inside a single tool call. Signature: `(int table, string field, IList<BulkWriteTarget> targets, bool dryRun = false, bool continueOnError = false, string? idempotencyKeyPrefix = null, int? maxParallel = 1)` where `BulkWriteTarget = { string clientNumber, object? value, int? subClientID, string? stateAbbrev }`. Loop body MUST go through `WriteField` (do NOT reach past it into `ApplySimFieldWrite` directly) so DATA6/7 block, AssertWritable, WireLog, dry-run undo, and the P14-005 per-key idempotency lock all stay one-source-of-truth. Per-row idempotency key shape: `$"{idempotencyKeyPrefix ?? \"bulk\"}-{row.clientNumber}"` — matches the convention already documented in WorkflowPrompts.cs:188/192 so the lacerte_bulk_field_update prompt can be simplified to call the new tool directly. Response envelope: `{ table, field, dryRun, total, succeeded:[{clientNumber, statusCode}], failed:[{clientNumber, statusCode, syntheticCode?, userMessage, errorContext}], skipped:[{clientNumber, reason:\"stop-on-error\"}] }` — keep `statusCode` so existing TAPIStatus mapping helpers stay reusable. Default `continueOnError=false` matches the existing prompt's safety posture; `maxParallel=1` default avoids cross-key idempotency-lock contention (raising it later is a follow-up). Tests in `FieldWriteBulkToolsTests.cs` (NOT FullFlowTests — that file is reserved for end-to-end shape): (a) happy-path bulk-update of 5 sim clients asserts `{total:5, succeeded:5, failed:0, skipped:0}`; (b) inject a failure on row 3 by writing to a read-only field for one client and assert stop-on-error yields `{succeeded:2, failed:1, skipped:2}`; (c) re-run same payload in continue-on-error and assert `{succeeded:4, failed:1, skipped:0}`; (d) replay-safety: invoke twice with same `idempotencyKeyPrefix` and assert second call returns cached statusCodes per row (no double-write — extend SimulationStore write counter to assert this). After landing, update WorkflowPrompts.cs `BulkFieldUpdate` to recommend `lacerte_field_write_bulk` as the primary path and demote the per-row loop to a "fallback if you need finer control" note; add README Tools-table row and an ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md Phase-14 entry.

title: Detail read has no Series/Code filter; SqlTemplates push-down dead code
description: `lacerte_detail_read` returns the FULL per-client detail file — every W-2 row, every interest row, every dependent row interleaved. Detail files for active returns routinely run to hundreds or thousands of rows; the model has to pull all of them just to find W-2 rows (Series=11) or interest rows (Series=12). `SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries(client, series)` and `DetailByCode(client, code)` exist and emit valid push-down SQL but are referenced ONLY in unit tests (`SqlTemplatesTests.cs:286, 293`). The session manager's `ReadDetail` has no series/code parameter, and the tool exposes no filter at all. The detail-review flow in REQUIREMENTS §1.5 ("pull tax-detail context into review chats") therefore forces an overfetch + client-side filter on every call, which the model frequently won't do — it will just paginate aimlessly or summarize the wrong rows. No pagination is exposed either: unlike `lacerte_table_read` / `lacerte_client_list`, `LacerteDetailRead` returns count+rows with no limit/offset.
recommendation: Add `series` (int?) and `code` (int?) optional parameters to `LacerteDetailRead` and a corresponding `ReadDetail(clientNumber, series?, code?)` overload on the session manager. In live mode dispatch to `SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries` / `DetailByCode` when set; in sim filter the in-memory `List<DetailRow>` by the numeric-string Series/Code invariant (already enforced by `DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite`, so the int.Parse is safe). Also add `limit`/`offset` pagination matching `LacerteTableRead`'s shape. This wires the existing dead push-down code, gives the detail-review flow first-class filtering, and removes the overfetch tax. Add one round-trip test: seed 20 detail rows across series 11/12/14, assert `ReadDetail(clientNumber, series: 11)` returns only Series==11 rows in both sim and live legs.
rationale: Existing dead code in SqlTemplates proves the design intent was filtered reads. The detail-review operator flow is asymptotically broken without it, and the wire SQL is already written and tested.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified directly against source. The gap is real and the prior 71 Phase-14 fixes did NOT close it:

1. CONFIRMED — DEAD CODE: `SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries(client, series)` (SqlTemplates.cs:249-253) and `DetailByCode(client, code)` (264-268) exist and emit valid push-down SQL (`where Series = {series}` / `where Code = {code}`), but Grep across `src/` shows they are referenced only in `SqlTemplatesTests.cs`, `SeedData.cs` (as constants), `SqlTemplates.cs` (definition), and `DetailsTools.cs` (in xmldoc comments — NOT in any call). No production caller invokes them. The session manager doesn't even import them.

2. CONFIRMED — MISSING FILTER PARAM: `LacerteSessionManager.ReadDetail(string clientNumber)` at lines 574-587 takes no filter, no limit, no offset. The sim path (line 582) returns `module.Details[clientNumber].ToList()` — the FULL detail file for the client.

3. CONFIRMED — TOOL HAS NO FILTER: `DetailsTools.LacerteDetailRead` (DetailsTools.cs:63-78) takes only `clientNumber` and returns `{clientNumber, count, rows}` — no series/code, no limit/offset. The `[Description]` literally says "No filtering — returns the full ordered list."

4. CONFIRMED — SIM ALREADY HAS FILTER CAPABILITY: `SimulationStore.ReadDetail(dataPath, year, module, clientNumber, Predicate<DetailRow>? filter = null)` at SimulationStore.cs:409 already accepts a predicate AND is tested (`SimulationStoreTests.ReadDetail_WithFilter_NarrowsResults` at line 362 uses `r => r.Series == SeedData.SeriesIds.Wages`). So the lower layer is wired — only the session-manager → tool wiring is missing.

5. CONFIRMED — NO PHASE-14 DUPE: Searched audit-findings.json + Todo.md Phase 14 (P14-001 through P14-071). Closest hits:
   - P14-014 (ListClients pagination push-down) — fixes ClientsTools/Data1, says nothing about Detail.
   - P14-055 (Series/Code numeric column type alignment) — landed via "lighter-fix path" keeping Series/Code as `string` on the wire and using regex validation to ensure the strings are numeric-parseable. The xmldoc at DetailsTools.cs:23 and SqlTemplates.cs:238-247 explicitly acknowledges this prepares the ground for filter wiring but does NOT do the wiring.
   - No P14 task mentions adding series/code filter params, paginating detail-read, or activating DetailBySeries/DetailByCode.

6. REQUIREMENTS §1.5 context (detail-review chats): the operator flow is meant to pull "tax-detail context into review chats" — without push-down, a Schedule B review for a high-net-worth client pulls every W-2/dependent/state-apportionment row alongside the interest rows the model actually needs.

The fix is fully off-Windows actionable — sim path is the `Predicate<DetailRow>` filter already wired in SimulationStore; live path is dispatching to existing SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries/DetailByCode (which Phase 9 will execute via the ODBC reader the moment that ships). Sim tests cover both filter and non-filter paths today.

Severity calibration: the finding says "high" — I'd call it medium-high. It's a latent perf + flow problem rather than a correctness bug, but it activates the moment the operator uses the detail-review prompt on a real return.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Wire the existing push-down through three layers. Sim-only, off-Windows actionable, ~80 lines + 2 tests.

(1) **LacerteSessionManager.ReadDetail overload** — add `ReadDetail(string clientNumber, int? series, int? code, int? limit, int? offset)` that:
   - Sim path: builds a `Predicate<DetailRow>` (`r => (series == null || int.Parse(r.Series) == series) && (code == null || int.Parse(r.Code) == code)`), forwards to existing `SimulationStore.ReadDetail(dataPath, year, module, clientNumber, predicate)` (already exists at SimulationStore.cs:409, already tested). int.Parse is safe because `DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite` (P14-055) guarantees Series matches `^\d+$` and Code matches `^-?\d+$` on every sim write, AND the seed fixture (P14-055) uses numeric-string Series IDs.
   - Apply `.Skip(offset ?? 0).Take(limit ?? Pagination.MaxLimit)` AFTER filtering so the (filtered total, page) shape matches `LacerteTableRead`.
   - Live path (Phase 9): dispatch to `SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries(client, series.Value)` when only series set, `DetailByCode` when only code set, `DetailAll` when neither; if BOTH set, fall back to `DetailAll` + in-memory filter (LacerteDSII doesn't compose AND well — document this constraint in xmldoc).
   - Keep the existing single-arg `ReadDetail(string clientNumber)` as an unfiltered delegating wrapper so existing tests/callers don't churn.

(2) **DetailsTools.LacerteDetailRead** — add four optional params with `[Description]`:
   - `series` (int?) — "Optional Series filter (e.g. 11=W-2, 12=Interest, 13=Dividends, 14=Dependents). Push-down via SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries in live."
   - `code` (int?) — "Optional Code filter."
   - `limit` (int? = 100) + `offset` (int? = 0) — mirror `LacerteTableRead`'s shape exactly (Pagination.Page envelope).
   - Update the existing tool [Description] from "No filtering" to "Optional Series/Code push-down + offset/limit pagination."
   - Return shape: `{clientNumber, rows, total, hasMore, nextOffset}` to match `LacerteTableRead` (the current `{clientNumber, count, rows}` is a one-off shape that itself disagrees with the rest of the read tools — fold this fix in).

(3) **Tests** (both legs of parity):
   - `DetailsToolsTests`: assert calling `LacerteDetailRead("1001", series: 11)` returns only rows where `Series == "11"` (BROW seed has 2 Wages + 1 Dep; expect 2). Use SeedData.SeriesIds.Wages constant from P14-055.
   - `LacerteSessionManagerTests`: round-trip test seeding 20 rows across Series 11/12/14 via WriteDetail, then `ReadDetail(clientNumber, series: 11)` asserts only Series=="11" subset returned.
   - `SqlTemplatesTests`: already covers DetailBySeries/DetailByCode SQL rendering — no new test there, but bump description to drop the "currently unreferenced" tone.

(4) **README tool table**: update the `lacerte_detail_read` row to list the new optional params + cross-reference Series ID table.

Skip the "add a separate `lacerte_detail_read_by_series` tool" route — overloading the existing tool's params keeps the discoverable surface narrow and matches how `LacerteTableRead` exposes optional filters.

Do NOT touch DetailRow.Series/Code types — P14-055 explicitly chose the lighter-fix path (string on the wire + numeric-string invariant). Reopening that decision is out of scope; the int.Parse in the new overload is safe under the P14-055 invariant.

title: EF status review has no since-date filter; pulls full roster every time
description: REQUIREMENTS §1.4 ("Watching e-file status across the firm") is the canonical poll-for-changes workflow, but `lacerte_ef_status` takes ZERO parameters: no `sinceStatusDate`, no `statusFilter` ("Rejected" / "Pending"), no `clientNumber`, no pagination. The `EfStatusJoin` SQL template at SqlTemplates.cs:208-213 unconditionally joins ALL EFilings to ALL EFStatuses for the module. A firm with 500 returns transmitted over six weeks gets 500 rows back every poll — the model then has to filter client-side. The `lacerte_review_ef_status` prompt explicitly tells the model to bucket by Status and flag rows older than 72h, which is exactly the work a SQL WHERE clause should be doing. There is also no `lacerte_ef_status_for(clientNumber)` for single-client drill-down; the prompt's Step 4 says "call lacerte_detail_read for each ClientId" — wrong tool for the job, and detail-read doesn't carry e-file status fields.
recommendation: Extend `LacerteEfStatus(string? sinceStatusDate = null, string? statusFilter = null, string? clientNumber = null, int limit = 100, int offset = 0)`. Mirror in `LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus(...)` and add a parameterized `EfStatusJoinFiltered(sinceDate, status, client)` template that appends `where s.EFStatusDate >= ? and s.EFStatus = ? and ci.C1_0 = ?` as needed. Sim path filters the in-memory join result by the same predicates. Add pagination on the result. Update `WorkflowPrompts.ReviewEfStatus` to call `lacerte_ef_status` with the filter set per bucket (one call for `Rejected`, one with `sinceStatusDate=now-72h` for stale) instead of pulling everything and grouping in-memory. Add a parity test asserting the `sinceStatusDate` filter returns the same shape in sim and live.
rationale: Polling for new EF status changes is the named flow #4. The current API is O(firm-size) per poll with no incremental delta — it scales linearly with the entire e-file history forever, not with what changed since last poll.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against source. EFileTools.cs:23 confirms `LacerteEfStatus()` takes zero parameters. LacerteSessionManager.cs:594-617 confirms `ReadEFStatus()` LINQ-joins the full EFilings × EFStatuses cross-product with no predicate. SqlTemplates.cs:208-213 (post-P14-021 rewrite) confirms the EfStatusJoin SELECT has no WHERE clause. WorkflowPrompts.cs:127-130 confirms the prompt tells the model to bucket Rejected/Pending and flag rows older than 72h client-side — exactly the work a WHERE should do. REQUIREMENTS.md line 14 confirms this is named workflow #4 ("Watching e-file status across the firm"). Phase-14 audit findings searched: P14-021 only fixed the column-projection sim/live parity (added EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId aliases), not filtering. P14-014/F13 retrofitted pagination on ListClients and TableRead but explicitly did NOT touch EFileTools — line 80 of Todo confirms EFileTools shipped at Phase-5 #49 and has not been re-touched since. Fix is pure sim + SQL-template work, no Windows or live SDK dependency: extend the session signature, add a parameterized SQL template, filter the sim LINQ join, plug into the existing Pagination.Page<T>, rewrite the prompt to push the filters server-side, add parity tests via the existing RoundTripTests harness. Severity is appropriate: per-poll O(firm × history) growth on the canonical poll workflow is a real scalability bug, not bikeshedding.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Extend the EF-status surface with server-side filters + pagination, reusing the Phase-14 plumbing:

1) **Tool signature** — `EFileTools.LacerteEfStatus(string? sinceStatusDate = null, string? statusFilter = null, string? clientNumber = null, int? limit = null, int? offset = null)`. Parameter contracts: `sinceStatusDate` is an ISO-8601 date (`yyyy-MM-dd`) parsed via `DateTime.TryParseExact(..., CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...)` — reject anything else with `LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidArgument, ...)`; `statusFilter` validated case-insensitively against the documented set `{Rejected, Pending, Transmitted, Accepted}` (any other string also rejected — keeps sim/live parity tight); `clientNumber` validated via existing `SqlTemplates.ValidateClient`. No new tool needed — single-client drill-down is just `clientNumber=...`.

2) **Session manager** — `LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus(DateTime? sinceStatusDate, string? statusFilter, string? clientNumber, int limit, int offset)` filters the in-memory LINQ join (`Where(... s.StatusDate >= since && s.Status == statusFilter && f.ClientId == clientNumber)`) and returns a `Pagination.Page<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,object?>>` so the envelope matches ListClients/TableRead (rows + total + limit + offset + hasMore + nextOffset). Update WireLog.Record args so the filter values appear in the wire log (the existing PII redaction will catch the clientNumber if needed).

3) **SQL template** — Add `SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoinFiltered(bool hasSince, bool hasStatus, bool hasClient)` that returns the existing SELECT + the appropriate `WHERE` clauses with `?` placeholders. Critical: use `OdbcParameter` binding in the (not-yet-wired) Reader path, not string interpolation — P14-048 already established this codebase has had ODBC-delimiter injection bugs, and `clientNumber` arrives from operator input. Add `SqlTemplatesTests` rows asserting each combination of present/absent filters produces the expected WHERE shape and that the SELECT projection still matches the sim contract column-for-column.

4) **Prompt** — Rewrite `WorkflowPrompts.ReviewEfStatus` Step 2 to make two filtered `lacerte_ef_status` calls: one with `statusFilter="Rejected"`, one with `sinceStatusDate={now-72h, formatted yyyy-MM-dd}` for the stale-Pending sweep, instead of pulling everything and grouping in-memory. Step 4's "call `lacerte_detail_read` for each ClientId" is wrong tool — replace with `lacerte_client_read(clientNumber)` for context plus a follow-up `lacerte_ef_status(clientNumber=...)` for the per-client history drill-down.

5) **Tests** — Add to existing `LacertMCP.Tests/Parity/RoundTripTests.cs` (harness already shipped Phase-12 #81): theory rows covering (a) `sinceStatusDate` filter excludes older rows, (b) `statusFilter="Rejected"` returns only rejected rows, (c) `clientNumber=` returns rows for one client, (d) pagination `limit=2,offset=1` returns the right slice and `hasMore` flag, (e) invalid `statusFilter="Bogus"` throws InvalidArgument in BOTH legs (sim + recorded-live). Seed `SimulationStore.Seed` with at least 6 EFStatuses across 3 clients + 2 statuses + 2 dates so the filters actually have something to discriminate (current fixture is too sparse for filter tests).

6) **README + ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA** — Update the `lacerte_ef_status` tool row to reflect the new params + paginated envelope. The Prompts table row for `lacerte_review_ef_status` should note the rewritten Step 2 flow.

title: No write-then-read round-trip test or test-only access-map override
description: The FullFlowTests Step 5 comment is explicit: "WriteField with a force-bypass (access map is empty in v1)" and asserts a 9012 UnknownFieldAccess instead of asserting the write landed and the read sees it. WriteParityTests likewise only asserts rejection codes — none of the 695 tests writes a value to C1_1 and then reads C1_1 back to confirm the operator sees what they wrote. The v1 base access maps ship empty, so the access-map gate fails closed on every writable-field probe; there is no fixture-injection hook to seed a known-writable field for the test suite. The hidden risk: the entire happy-path write→sim store→read path has no integration coverage. If `SimulationStore.ApplySimFieldWrite` corrupted the field-name casing, or `CloneRow` dropped a key, or the sim's `Fields` dict mutated under a snapshot, no test would catch it. The operator's #1 trust question — "if I write X did it actually land?" — has no automated verification in either mode.
recommendation: Add a test-only seam: either (a) `AccessMapMutationCollection` (already exists at `src/LacertMCP.Tests/AccessMapMutationCollection.cs` — wire it in) lets tests inject `{module=I, table=1, field=C1_1, access=ReadWrite}` before driving the write, or (b) add `FieldAccessMapLoader.AddOverrideForTests(...)` that the existing `AccessMapMutation` fixture uses. Then add a `FullFlow_WriteThenRead_RoundTrips` test: register → SetContext → Write field C1_1="NewFirstName" → Read same client → Assert row["C1_1"]=="NewFirstName" in both sim and live legs. Add the symmetric DetailRoundTrip: Write detail row → Read detail rows → assert the new row is present at the expected index with all 11 fields intact. This closes the operator's trust gap and makes regressions in CloneRow / Fields-dict mutation immediately visible.
rationale: Round-1 P14-021 covered the read-parity harness shape but every write test asserts a rejection code. The most important property of any write tool — what you wrote is what you'll read — is unverified.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading the cited files. FullFlowTests step 5 explicitly asserts UnknownFieldAccess (9012) rather than a real write success. WriteParityTests asserts rejection codes only (read-only gate, context gate, access-gate-first fail-closed, C{t}_0 ExposedForRead, unknown-field). The seam already exists — AccessMapTestFixture (src/LacertMCP.Tests/Tools/AccessMapTestFixture.cs:28) injects I|1|C1_15=ReadWrite — and FieldWriteToolsTests + UpdateReturnToolsTests both already USE it for happy-path tests, but those happy-path tests assert only the response envelope (success==true, statusCode==1), never doing the subsequent ReadClient to confirm the value landed. The DryRun tests do read before/after but assert origValue==afterValue (i.e., no change). SimulationStoreTests.cs:295-317 explicitly comments "the store-mutation portion of the happy path is exercised in SimulateCreateClient_HappyPath_RoundTripsThroughProcessQuery" — a phantom reference; that test does not exist for fields. For WriteDetail, there is no test anywhere that writes a row via session/store and then reads it back via ReadDetail to assert presence. Phase-14 grep (P14-021 read parity SQL, P14-024 access-map branches, P14-025 UpdateReturn tool tests, P14-028 WriteDetail lock, P14-030 sim CreateClient gates, P14-054 DATA6/7 block) does not cover write-then-read positive assertion. The audit's claim that fixture-injection has no hook is slightly inaccurate (AccessMapTestFixture exists), but the core gap — no test asserts "write X then read X" — is real and load-bearing for operator trust.

title: Idempotency per-key SemaphoreSlim map leaks unbounded across process lifetime
description: ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock does GetOrAdd into _idempotencyLocks for every distinct idempotency key and NEVER removes the SemaphoreSlim. The cache-entry side has TTL + cap-based eviction (P14-013/P14-064), but the LOCK side has no eviction at all — the matching SemaphoreSlim stays in _idempotencyLocks forever. The comment at lines 1313-1316 hand-waves this as 'cheap to leak (one SemaphoreSlim per unique key)' but on a 7-day run with thousands of writes each carrying a unique key (the only way idempotency actually works) this map grows linearly with total write count, NOT with active inflight writes. Each SemaphoreSlim is a 200+ byte managed object plus a kernel semaphore handle, so 100k unique keys = ~20 MB + 100k kernel handles. Dispose at process exit eventually frees them, but for the 24h/7d steady state this is real leak pressure.
recommendation: After releasing the semaphore in the finally block, attempt removal: if (sem.CurrentCount == 1 && _idempotencyLocks.TryRemove(key, out var sameSem) && !ReferenceEquals(sameSem, sem)) { _idempotencyLocks.TryAdd(key, sameSem); } — the ReferenceEquals dance handles the rare TOCTOU where a concurrent caller already replaced it. Alternatively, piggyback on the cache eviction path: whenever StoreIdempotent evicts an entry by key, also TryRemove that key from _idempotencyLocks (and Dispose the semaphore). The lock map should never outlive its cache entry.
rationale: Phase 14 task P14-005 added the per-key lock to close the TOCTOU race but explicitly chose not to clean up. That's defensible for short sessions but invalidates the cap-based eviction guarantee for long-running operators — the leak channel that audit-finding P14-013 was supposed to close just moved from the cache to the lock map. Reviewer asked specifically about this in the prompt ('Lock leakage: per-key SemaphoreSlims in the idempotency map — what cleans them up?'); the answer today is 'nothing.'

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED. The leak channel is real: `_idempotencyLocks.GetOrAdd` at line 1324 has no matching removal; only `Dispose()` (line 1465) cleans up — at process exit. The comment at lines 1313-1316 explicitly acknowledges the leak as accepted ("cheap to leak"). P14-005 (the task that introduced the lock map) chose this trade-off deliberately to avoid TOCTOU on the self-remove path; P14-013 and P14-064 only bound the CACHE side, not the LOCK side — so the finder's central claim (cap-based eviction guarantee invalidated by the lock map) is accurate. NOT a duplicate: no Phase-14 task addresses lock-map eviction.

However, severity is overstated. (a) For a single-operator personal tool (CLAUDE.md), a 7-day session accumulating 100k unique idempotency keys is unrealistic — operators supply keys for risky writes (e-file submission), not bulk field writes. (b) The "100k kernel handles" claim is wrong: SemaphoreSlim only allocates a Win32 semaphore handle if `AvailableWaitHandle` is accessed; the lock path here uses only `WaitAsync`/`Release`, so no kernel handle is created. Real cost is ~200 B/key of managed memory — call it 2 MB at 10k keys, matching the cache cap.

The recommendation's `sem.CurrentCount == 1` self-remove dance is genuinely racy (a concurrent thread about to call `WaitAsync` on the snapshot reference could lose its semaphore mid-flight) and was correctly rejected by the prior audit. The piggyback-on-cache-eviction approach is the right one — when StoreIdempotent's prune loop removes a cache entry, also remove + dispose the matching lock. Even that has a small race (another thread could be holding the lock during eviction), but it's bounded: worst case is one more execution of the body without idempotency replay, which is observationally equivalent to a cache miss.

Fix is small, sim-only, off-Windows actionable, and restores the invariant "lock map size ≤ cache map size" — i.e., P14-013's cap genuinely bounds the leak channel.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Make the lock map a strict subset of the cache map. Three small, coordinated edits in `LacerteSessionManager.cs`:

(1) Add a private helper `private void EvictIdempotencyEntry(string key)` that does `if (_idempotencyCache.TryRemove(key, out _) && _idempotencyLocks.TryRemove(key, out var sem)) sem.Dispose();`. 

(2) Replace the two TryRemove calls in `StoreIdempotent`'s prune loop (lines 1381 and 1392) with `EvictIdempotencyEntry(kv.Key)` and `EvictIdempotencyEntry(oldestKey)` respectively. Also replace the TTL-miss eviction in `TryReplayIdempotent` (line 1346) with the helper.

(3) Update the comment block at lines 1311-1316 to reflect the new invariant: "The semaphore is removed alongside its cache entry by EvictIdempotencyEntry, so the lock map is bounded by IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries (10k) just like the cache. A concurrent waiter may briefly hold a since-evicted semaphore — bounded race, worst case is one extra body execution (observationally equivalent to a cache miss)."

Skip the proposed `sem.CurrentCount == 1` self-remove dance — the prior audit correctly rejected it as racy. Skip the kernel-handle alarm — `SemaphoreSlim` allocates a Win32 handle only on `AvailableWaitHandle` access, which this code never uses; the leak is managed memory only.

Add one sim-only xUnit test: write 10_005 entries with unique idempotency keys, assert `_idempotencyLocks.Count <= 10_000` after the over-cap prune fires (use reflection on the private field, mirroring the pattern any existing cache-cap test uses for `_idempotencyCache`). If no such existing test exists, drop the assertion and rely on the cache-cap test as the canary — the helper makes the two counts move together.

title: No CancellationToken plumbing — tools cannot honor MCP cancel notifications
description: A repo-wide grep for `CancellationToken` finds zero matches in the Server project. Every [McpServerTool] method has the signature `Task<string> LacerteX(...)` with no CancellationToken parameter. The MCP spec defines a `notifications/cancelled` message the client (e.g. Claude Desktop) sends to abort an in-flight tool call; the SDK plumbs a token down to handlers that accept one, but our tools opt out by never declaring it. WrapToolHandler.Run also takes a parameterless Func<Task<object>>. As a result, a paged ListClients over 50k rows, a slow ODBC scan, or a hung COM Register cannot be cancelled — the client gives up, but the server keeps the COM apartment / ODBC connection busy until the underlying call returns.
recommendation: Add `CancellationToken cancellationToken = default` as the trailing parameter on every [McpServerTool] method (the SDK injects it automatically when present), thread it through WrapToolHandler.Run(Func<CancellationToken,Task<object>>, CancellationToken), and forward to LacerteSessionManager methods (ListClients, ReadTable, WriteField, etc.). Inside the sim path, check `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` between expensive steps (LINQ materialization, idempotency-lock acquisition); inside the live bridge, pass to AutoReconnect / ODBC. Wrap OperationCanceledException in WrapToolHandler as a structured `{success:false, statusCode:9xxx Cancelled, ...}` rather than letting it bubble as an Error(0) wrapped exception.
rationale: MCP protocol compliance — long-running tools that can't be cancelled hold COM/ODBC handles and force the user to wait or restart the server. The audit's round-1 covered idempotency locks but not cooperative cancellation; this is a fresh hole that affects every tool method.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by grep: zero occurrences of `CancellationToken` anywhere in the LacertMCP repo (not just Server). Sampled ClientsTools.LacerteClientList (signature `Task<string> LacerteClientList(string?, int, int)` — no CT) and WrapToolHandler.Run (signature `Run(Func<Task<object>>)` — also no CT).
