Checked all 71 Phase-14 task IDs in Todo.md and audit-findings.json — none of P14-001 through P14-071 touch cancellation, OperationCanceledException, or `notifications/cancelled`. The closest neighbors (P14-005 idempotency lock race, P14-013 idempotency cache eviction, F12 AutoReconnect) are about retry/idempotency, not cooperative cancel. The ModelContextProtocol C# SDK does inject CancellationToken into tool handlers when the method signature declares a trailing CT parameter — this is the documented mechanism, so the fix is to opt in. Sim-only verifiable: write an xUnit test that calls LacerteClientList with an already-cancelled CTS and asserts OperationCanceledException (or a 9xxx envelope) — no Windows/Lacerte/ODBC needed. The audit's framing of operational impact (paged 50k-row ListClients, slow ODBC scan, hung COM Register holding the apartment) is accurate given the existing chokepoints in LacerteSessionManager. One nit on the original recommendation: wrapping OCE as a synthetic 9xxx envelope is debatable — MCP semantics suggest the SDK should suppress the response when the client already sent `notifications/cancelled`, so letting OCE propagate from the handler (the SDK then chooses whether to emit a result) is the cleaner default; the 9xxx envelope only matters for tool-initiated timeouts. Worth refining.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Three-tier rollout, all sim-verifiable: (1) Add `CancellationToken ct = default` as the trailing parameter on every `[McpServerTool]` method across the 15 Tools/*.cs files (ClientsTools, TablesTools, DetailsTools, FieldWriteTools, UpdateReturnTools, CreateClientTools, EFileTools, FormsTools, StatesTools, StatusTools, SubclientsTools, SessionTools, HealthTools, MetadataTools, Internal/FieldWriteCore) — the SDK injects it automatically on signature match. (2) Change `WrapToolHandler.Run` to overload-or-replace with `Run(Func<CancellationToken, Task<object>> handler, CancellationToken ct)`; rethrow `OperationCanceledException` directly (do NOT wrap as a 9xxx envelope — MCP spec wants the canceled tool to NOT emit a response when the client already sent `notifications/cancelled`; the SDK suppresses the result on bubbled OCE). Keep the existing LacerteSDKError/Exception catches unchanged. (3) Thread `ct` into `LacerteSessionManager` async chokepoints — `ListClients`, `ReadClient`, `ReadTable`, `ReadDetail`, `ReadEFStatus`, `WriteField`, `WriteDetail`, `CreateClient`, `Register`, `CanUseNewApis` — and add `ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()` (a) before idempotency-lock acquisition, (b) inside the SimulationStore LINQ paths between filter/sort/page steps, (c) before each `_bridge.<method>` call (so AutoReconnect retries also abort). For the live ODBC path, pass `ct` to `OdbcCommand.ExecuteReaderAsync(ct)` once Phase 4 #39 lands; for now a pre-call check suffices. Tests (sim-only, ~6 facts): (a) cancel-before-call → OCE; (b) cancel mid-LINQ via a yield-point assertion on a fake store with 10k rows; (c) cancel during idempotency-lock contention (use the existing lock seam); (d) WrapToolHandler propagates OCE without wrapping; (e) regression: non-cancelled path still returns the envelope shape unchanged. New synthetic status code (e.g., 9013 `OperationCancelled`) only needed if tool-internal timeout work lands — explicitly defer.

title: AutoReconnect retries are silent — `log` parameter never passed
description: Every one of the five `AutoReconnect.WithRetry`/`WithRetrySync` call sites in `LacerteSessionManager` passes the operation but omits the optional `ILogger? log` parameter. `AutoReconnect.cs` only emits its `LogWarning("Transient COM/RPC failure on attempt {Attempt}/{Max}; retrying in {DelayMs}ms.", …)` if that logger is non-null (see AutoReconnect.cs:71-74 and :111-114). So when production hits the exact failure mode this code was added to handle — a flaky RPC server, a busy-message-filter, a midnight COM disconnect — the operator sees ZERO log evidence that the wire just retried 3 times over 1750ms. The only forensic trail is `ex.Data["AutoReconnect.Attempts"]` on the FINAL throw, and only if the call exhausts all retries. A retry-that-succeeded-on-attempt-2 is completely invisible. This is the single biggest observability hole introduced by Phase 14 — the resilience layer that landed in F12 has no telemetry surface.
recommendation: Either (a) inject an `ILoggerFactory` into `LacerteSessionManager` and create a category logger that all five call sites pass to `AutoReconnect`, or — cheaper — (b) inside `AutoReconnect.WithRetry`/`WithRetrySync` ALWAYS emit a `WireLog.RecordSync("AutoReconnect.retry", new { attempt, hresult = ex.HResult.ToString("X8"), delayMs }, …)` in addition to the optional `log?.LogWarning` so the existing wire log captures every retry deterministically. Option (b) avoids touching every call site and keeps retries in the same log stream as the wrapped op. Also add a `WireLog.RecordSync("AutoReconnect.exhausted", new { attempts, finalHresult })` at the rethrow point so the audit log distinguishes "failed first try" from "failed after 3 retries".
rationale: Without this, when an operator reports "Lacerte calls felt slow tonight" you have no way to know if it was 1 happy-path call or 4 silent retries against a transient RPC failure. The retry feature exists but has no observability.

verdict.reasoning: VERIFIED. All 5 call sites at LacerteSessionManager.cs:223, 434, 719, 838, 940 invoke AutoReconnect.WithRetry/WithRetrySync without the optional `log` parameter (default ILogger? log = null in AutoReconnect.cs:55, 95). The retry warning at AutoReconnect.cs:71-74 and :111-114 is `log?.LogWarning(...)` — null-guarded, so nothing is emitted. The retry metadata stamped onto ex.Data["AutoReconnect.Attempts"/"Exhausted"] (AutoReconnect.cs:83-84, 121-122) is read ONLY by AutoReconnectTests.cs, never by production code. The outer WireLog wrapper (e.g. Register at line 192, CanUseNewApis at line 432, WriteField at the WriteField chain) does record one op-level entry, BUT WireLog's error capture at WireLog.cs:165-169 only serializes ex.GetType().FullName + ex.Message — the .Data dictionary is dropped on the floor. Net effect, exactly as the finding claims: (a) a 2nd-attempt success is INVISIBLE in the wire log (only elevated durationMs hints at it), and (b) an exhausted-after-3-retries failure is OBSERVATIONALLY INDISTINGUISHABLE from a 1st-attempt failure in the log stream. Phase-14 has one related task — P14-023 — but that adds unit tests for IsTransient HRESULT coverage, not telemetry. P14-037 is docs-only (DECISIONS.md entry). No Phase-14 task wires retry observability. Fix is pure C# in Server/Resilience + a sim-only xUnit test, no Windows/Lacerte needed. Recommendation option (b) is the right pick for this single-operator project (no DI container exists today; injecting ILoggerFactory through LacerteSessionManager would ripple through every test fixture). Also worth bundling a tiny WireLog.cs fix to capture ex.Data alongside type/message so exhausted-retry attribution shows up in the same log line.

title: WireLog file grows unbounded — no rotation, no size cap, no eviction
description: The log file path is `lacerte-YYYYMMDD.log` (FilenameForToday()), opened in `FileMode.Append` with no size check. A single high-volume day — e.g. an operator doing a 5000-client batch update with `LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1` and each `WriteField` recording ~300 bytes of args+result — produces a 1-2 GB daily log. There is NO size cap, NO compaction, NO `*.log.1`/`.log.2` rolling, NO oldest-file deletion. The `_openWriters` dict only closes the prior writer at date rollover (line 475-482). On a 30-day continuous session the `logs/` directory will accumulate 30 files of unbounded size with zero pruning. title: Idempotency cache hits/misses/conflicts/evictions are never logged
description: `TryReplayIdempotent` returns a cached result without writing any log line, `StoreIdempotent` evicts entries silently, and `IdempotencyConflict (9102)` throws a structured error but produces no separate audit entry. The Phase-14 idempotency-cache rework added TTL eviction (line 1344-1348), size-cap pruning (line 1374-1395), and per-key semaphore locking (line 1317-1334) — none of which emit telemetry. From the log perspective: when a tool call's WireLog.Record entry shows `durationMs=2` and `result=Success`, the operator cannot tell whether that was a genuine cached replay (no wire side effect) or whether the work actually ran. When 9102 fires the WireLog entry shows it as an error — but the operator can't see WHICH prior key/payload caused the conflict (only the colliding new fingerprint). And when the size cap evicts an entry, a subsequent same-key replay will silently turn into a real re-execute, which violates the idempotency contract operators are relying on. The cache is the strongest correctness guarantee the system makes, and it's invisible.
recommendation: Inside `TryReplayIdempotent`: on a hit emit `WireLog.RecordSync("Idempotency.hit", new { key, ageMs = (now - entry.CreatedAt).TotalMilliseconds }, …)`. On a TTL-expiry miss emit `"Idempotency.expired"`. On a fingerprint mismatch attach the cached `entry.CreatedAt` to the 9102 exception's context dict so the operator sees BOTH timestamps. Inside `StoreIdempotent`: when an eviction loop runs, emit one `"Idempotency.evicted"` line with `{ cacheSize, droppedKey, droppedCreatedAt }`. None of these are PII (the key is operator-supplied; the fingerprint is a base64 SHA-256). Without this, the eviction-after-cap-pressure failure mode — a duplicate detail-row write surviving 24h cache but evicted by 10001st entry — looks identical in logs to a clean first-time write.
rationale: Idempotency is the contract the LLM client most depends on for safety. Today an evicted-then-replayed key silently produces a double-write that no log can detect after the fact.

The outer WireLog.Record("WriteField", ...) wrapper sits INSIDE the ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock body but AFTER the TryReplayIdempotent check (see WriteField line 668-689: cache check at 677, WireLog.Record at 689). When TryReplayIdempotent hits, `return cached` (line 679) bypasses WireLog.Record entirely — so a cache hit produces NO log line whatsoever, not "a line that's indistinguishable from a real call" as the finding describes. From an operator's view a successful cached replay is invisible in the log (no op entry at all), which is even worse for the audit story.

Three concrete event paths today have no telemetry:
1. Cache hit (line 677-680) — silent, no log line at all
2. TTL expiry treated as miss (line 1344-1348) — silent eviction; the subsequent re-execute looks like a fresh first-time call
3. Size-cap pruning (line 1374-1395) — silent drop of expired entries + oldest-by-CreatedAt
4. 9102 IdempotencyConflict (line 1359) — the structured error carries `idempotencyKey` and `reason` but NOT the existing entry's CreatedAt, so the operator can't compare timestamps to know how long ago the conflicting key was first used.

Tests can use the existing WireLogSessionIntegrationTests pattern (reflection-poke `WireLog.EnableForTests` + temp-dir log inspection) — same approach as the existing WireLog test surface confirmed at WireLog.cs line 66-69.

    new { key, ageMs = (DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - entry.CreatedAt).TotalMilliseconds },
    () => null);
```

var data = new Dictionary<string, object?>

    new { cacheSize = _idempotencyCache.Count, expiredDropped = expiredCount,

    () => null);
```

title: Over-redaction in WrapToolHandler breaks operator diagnostics and read tools
description: P14-018/P14-019 wired WrapToolHandler.Run to call WireLog.Redact on BOTH the success envelope (line 61) and the error envelope (line 94). WireLog._sensitiveKeys (Logging/WireLog.cs:89-110) includes "reason", "Description", "FirstName", "LastName", "MiddleName", "City", "ZipCode", "Zip", "Address1", "Address2". Net effect: (a) every error context's "reason" — including validator messages like "dataPath is required" or "ClientID must match ^[A-Z0-9]+$" or "Pre-TY21 live writes require a ClientNumber → row-number lookup" — gets replaced with "***". (b) every successful LacerteDetailRead response gets DetailRow.Description fields wiped (e.g. "ACME Industries W-2" → "***"), breaking the tool's primary value to the LLM. (c) any future tool that returns a row containing a column literally named City/Zip/Description loses that data. Tests (DetailsToolsTests) only assert count/success, not the actual Description payload, so the regression is silent. The audit verdict for P14-019 explicitly asked for rawError+reason redaction without analyzing whether "reason" is also a critical diagnostic key — it's both.
recommendation: Split the redaction policy: SUCCESS envelopes should NOT be redacted whole-tree (read tools legitimately return Description/City/Zip/Address/Name data — that's the operator's data, not a leak to a third party). Only WIRE-LOG records (disk) need the broad redaction. For error envelopes, drop "reason" from _sensitiveKeys and instead redact ONLY the SDK-echo path (rawError + a new explicit "sdkEcho" or "rawComMessage" key) — keep "reason" as operator-facing diagnostic. Alternative: introduce two keysets, _diskRedactionKeys (broad) and _wireRedactionKeys (narrow: SSN/EIN/Bank/Email/Phone/SSN-codes only), and have WrapToolHandler use the narrow set while WriteRecord uses the broad set. Add tests that assert LacerteDetailRead returns the actual Description string for at least one seeded row, and that a synthetic 9201 BridgeUnavailable error context preserves its operator-facing reason.
rationale: This is a functional regression introduced by the Phase-14 fix that touches every operator-visible error and every detail-row read. It currently masquerades as "hardening" but actually destroys the value of the operator-facing surface. No PII protection is gained for legitimate reads of the operator's OWN tax data — the LLM the operator is talking to IS the consumer of that data.

CONFIRMED — finding is a real, silent regression introduced by P14-018+P14-019.

Same problem applies prospectively to any tool returning rows with literal property names City/Zip/Description/FirstName/LastName — e.g. CreateClient response echo, ListClients responses, sub-client reads, state-info reads. The current fix breaks legitimate reads of the operator's OWN tax data — there's no PII protection benefit because the LLM IS the operator's consumer.

title: ODBC row results bypass WireLog redaction (column-name keyed)
description: LacerteDsnReader.Query wraps `ExecuteReader` in `WireLog.RecordSync` with the SQL as args and the materialized row list as the result. The dict overload (line 69-82) keys rows by raw ODBC column names — i.e. Lacerte field codes like `C1_15`, `C1_14`, `C1_71`. WireLog.Redact's JsonNode walker only redacts when the JSON KEY is in `_sensitiveKeys` (`SSN`, `TaxpayerSSN`, etc.). The PII-field-code SecondPass (`ScrubFieldValuePairs`) only fires on the literal `{field: '<code>', value: <secret>}` shape used by WriteField — it does NOT fire on `{C1_15: '111-22-3333'}`. So a `select * from [DATA1-Client Info]` result containing SSNs lands verbatim in the wire log when `LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1`. P14-018's expansion never closed this hole because the round-1 author was focused on write-side payloads.
recommendation: Add a third redaction pass to WireLog.Redact: when a JsonObject key matches the C{t}_NN PII-code regex (against `_piiFieldCodes`), replace the value wholesale. Concretely, in RedactNode, after the `_sensitiveKeys.Contains(name)` branch, add `if (_piiFieldCodes.Contains(name)) { obj[name] = JsonValue.Create('***'); continue; }`. Add a WireLogRedactionTests case asserting `{"C1_15":"111-22-3333"}` redacts to `{"C1_15":"***"}`. Also add a parity test for an ODBC-shaped result dict (column names as keys).
rationale: ODBC reads are the dominant data path (Boundary Invariant #6: 99% of reads are ODBC). A debug wire log for a single `client_list` call would contain every taxpayer SSN/DOB/bank account in the install, keyed by column code that the current redactor cannot recognize.

title: Error context leaks SDK-echoed PII as substrings of message fields
description: OdbcErrorMapper.Map stuffs the raw ODBC driver message into `context["odbcMessage"] = message`. WrapToolHandler then writes the context to the MCP wire envelope and runs WireLog.Redact on the serialized JSON. But Redact only matches the SHAPE `"Key":"value"` — it does not scrub PII embedded as a SUBSTRING of a value. The Lacerte/FoxPro ODBC driver historically echoes the failing SQL and offending literal into its error message (e.g. `Syntax error near 'TaxpayerSSN = 111-22-3333'` or `Field C1_15 value '123-45-6789' rejected`). That message rides into `odbcMessage`, `reason` (which IS in `_sensitiveKeys` so the key gets stripped — but the SUBSTRING in `odbcMessage` does not), and `rawError`. Same pattern in WrapToolHandler line 74 (`rawError = ex.Message`) and Registration.cs / Writer.cs catch blocks that put `ex.Message` into a non-sensitive context key (`reason`).
recommendation: Three options, pick one: (a) Add a `RedactSubstrings` post-pass in WireLog.Redact that runs SSN/EIN/phone/email regexes (`\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b`, `\b\d{9}\b`, `\b\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}\b`, email regex) against the SERIALIZED JSON string and replaces matches with `***`. (b) Stop echoing raw SDK exception messages into context — keep only the SQLSTATE + caller's `sql` (which already passed `SqlTemplates.ValidateClient`/`ValidateColumn` gates). (c) Truncate `odbcMessage` and `rawError` to the first 80 chars + ellipsis (the driver typically puts the error category first, sensitive data second). Option (a) is the safest defense-in-depth; (b) is the cleanest architecturally; (c) is the cheapest. Land (a) plus a test that asserts `{"odbcMessage":"SSN 111-22-3333 invalid"}` redacts the SSN substring.
rationale: Round-1 P14-018 explicitly punted on this with `// Defer the full key-name DENYlist refactor`. The substring-leak surface is real — any ODBC syntax/constraint error during a write probe will dump the rejected value into the wire envelope and the disk log.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed real, narrower than claimed, and not addressed by Phase-14.

Code verification:
- OdbcErrorMapper.cs:46-50 puts the raw driver text under key `odbcMessage`. That key is NOT in WireLog._sensitiveKeys (Logging/WireLog.cs:89-110) and not in the fallback regex alternation (line 137). The walker therefore leaves the value verbatim — substring PII would survive into both the MCP wire envelope (via WrapToolHandler.SerializeError → WireLog.Redact post-P14-019) and the disk log.
- A second, smaller leak: WireLog's own catch blocks (WireLog.cs:165-169 and 197-202) build `{"type": ..., "message": ex.Message}` under the `error` slot. Key `message` is also missing from `_sensitiveKeys`, so an OdbcException wrapped by Record() drops its raw text to disk.

The audit overstates the surface in two ways:
- `reason` IS already in `_sensitiveKeys` (line 109), so all Bridge/Registration/Writer/Reader catch sites that put `ex.Message` under `reason` get wholesale-scrubbed by both wire and disk paths. The "Same pattern in WrapToolHandler line 74 (rawError) and Registration.cs / Writer.cs catch blocks that put ex.Message into a non-sensitive context key (reason)" sentence is wrong on both counts: `rawError` and `reason` are both in `_sensitiveKeys` and get wiped wholesale.
- `sql` (also written by LacerteDsnReader.cs:114-117 alongside `odbcMessage`) only carries SqlTemplates-built strings — user input is gated through `ValidateClient` (^[A-Z0-9]{1,8}$) and `ValidateColumn`, so PII can't be inlined there.

Net: real but narrow — the only remaining leak vector is `odbcMessage` and WireLog's internal `error.message` key. Phase-14 P14-018 ("expand redaction key list") and P14-019 ("apply Redact to wire envelope") landed but neither added these two keys. No Phase-14 task references `odbcMessage` or substring scrubbing (verified by grep over Todo.md and audit-findings.json).

Fully off-Windows actionable: one-file change in WireLog.cs plus a 2-line unit test in WireLogTests.cs.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Smallest fix that closes the leak and matches the project's existing redaction pattern:

1) Add two keys to WireLog._sensitiveKeys (Logging/WireLog.cs:89-110):
   - `"odbcMessage"` — the raw driver text echoed by OdbcErrorMapper.cs:49.
   - `"message"` — only used in WireLog's own internal catch blocks (lines 168, 200) where it carries `ex.Message`. The risk of over-redacting is low because production code that wants to log a benign string under "message" is not a pattern in this codebase (verified via grep — only the two WireLog internal sites use the bare "message" key).

2) Mirror the additions in the fallback regex alternation (_redactRegex at line 137) so malformed-JSON inputs are covered too.

3) Add 2 tests to WireLogTests.cs:
   - `Redact_OdbcMessage_WipesEntireValue` — `{"odbcMessage":"Syntax error near 'TaxpayerSSN = 111-22-3333'"}` → value becomes `"***"`.
   - `Record_OdbcExceptionInWork_RedactsInnerErrorMessage` — wrap a synthetic OdbcException whose ex.Message contains `"SSN 111-22-3333 invalid"`, assert the on-disk line has no `"111-22-3333"` substring.

Deliberately rejecting option (a) from the original finding (substring regex post-pass on serialized JSON): it over-redacts and reproduces the well-known "phone number false positives in account IDs" trap; the project already uses a key-name allowlist pattern (P14-018) and this fix extends it consistently. Deliberately rejecting option (b) (drop odbcMessage entirely): SQLSTATE alone loses debug value during live troubleshooting — keep the key but scrub the value, same posture as `rawError`/`reason`.

Skip OdbcErrorMapper.cs changes entirely — the fix lives in WireLog where the rest of the redaction policy is centralized. ~10 LOC + 2 tests, one commit.

title: LacerteAccessClient.CreateClient bypasses BridgeInputValidation entirely
description: Round-1 P14-050 introduced BridgeInputValidation as the defense-in-depth gate at every dynamic COM dispatch — but only Writer.WriteToDBFDatabase / UpdateTaxReturn / WriteDetail and Reader.ReadFromDBFData call it. LacerteAccessClient.CreateClient (lines 206-252) directly dispatches `clientList.SetDataPath(dataPath)` + `clientList.IClient(taxType, clientID, emailID, firstName, lastName)` + `client.CreateClient()` through `dynamic com` with ZERO bridge-boundary checks. CreateClientTools validates ClientID shape and TaxType, but the firstName / lastName / emailID strings — which the spec marks as required CreateClient inputs and which are operator-supplied free-form — are forwarded unvalidated. No length cap (could be megabytes), no NUL/control-char rejection (a `"Smith\0; DROP"` literal silently truncates inside the COM marshaller, exactly the case BridgeInputValidation.EnsureSafeText was built to prevent), and no AppId / dataPath check at the bridge boundary. The skip-test at LacerteAccessClientTests.cs:135 only asserts BridgeUnavailable off-Windows, so the validation hole is invisible to the suite.
recommendation: Add `ValidateCreateClientArgs(appId, dataPath, clientID, taxType, firstName, lastName, emailID)` to BridgeInputValidation that calls ValidateAppId, ValidateDataPath, ValidateClientNumber(clientID, ...), and EnsureSafeText on firstName/lastName/emailID (with ShortStringMaxLength for names and 254 for email per RFC 5321 — or DescriptionMaxLength as a safe upper bound). Optionally narrow emailID with a `@` presence check. Call from LacerteAccessClient.CreateClient BEFORE the dynamic dispatch, mirroring the pattern in Writer.cs:41/94/156. Add a unit test that asserts a control-char in firstName throws DetailWriteInvalid before any COM call is attempted.
rationale: The audit listed Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs as a 'newly-introduced surface' to scrutinize. The round-1 task closed Writer/Reader but left the CreateClient COM path open. Since CreateClient is the only path that mutates DATA1 wholesale (no per-field access map covers it — DECISIONS.md 'Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate'), the bridge boundary is the LAST gate before the SDK marshaller. P14-050's stated invariant ('a future caller that bypasses the tool layer still cannot push a curly-brace / NUL / oversize string into the late-bound COM marshaller') is provably not honored here.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading the cited files. LacerteAccessClient.cs:206-252 dispatches `clientList.SetDataPath(dataPath)` + `clientList.IClient(taxType, clientID, emailID, firstName, lastName)` + `client.CreateClient()` through `dynamic com` with zero BridgeInputValidation calls — the file does not import BridgeInputValidation and the method body has no pre-flight guard. Confirmed via Grep: BridgeInputValidation is called from exactly 4 sites — Reader.cs:43 (ReadFromDBFData), Writer.cs:41 (WriteToDBFDatabase), Writer.cs:94 (UpdateTaxReturn), Writer.cs:156 (WriteDetail). CreateClient is missing. NOT a Phase-14 duplicate: HANDOFF.md line 61 explicitly lists those four methods as the P14-050 scope, omitting CreateClient; Todo.md P14-050 (line 408-411) names only Writer.UpdateTaxReturn and Writer.WriteDetail; no other P14-xxx task touches the create path's bridge-boundary validation. Tool-layer fallback is weak: CreateClientTools.cs:121-152 only does `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` on firstName/lastName/emailID — no length cap, no control-char/NUL rejection, no appId/dataPath check. The finding's NUL-truncation concern is real: the SDK uses C-string marshalling and "Smith\0; DROP" will silently truncate to "Smith" before reaching the DBF. Actionable off-Windows because the throw fires BEFORE the dynamic dispatch (mirrors Writer.cs pattern). The original recommendation is correct; I tightened the test asserts and added an explicit pre-flight insertion point + op label so the implementer can pattern-match exactly.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `BridgeInputValidation.ValidateCreateClientArgs(string appId, string dataPath, string clientID, string taxType, string? firstName, string? lastName, string? emailID)` to Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs alongside the existing composite validators. Implementation: `const string op = "CreateClient"; ValidateAppId(appId, op); ValidateDataPath(dataPath, op); ValidateClientNumber(clientID, op); EnsureSafeText(taxType, op, "taxType", ShortStringMaxLength); EnsureSafeText(firstName, op, "firstName", ShortStringMaxLength); EnsureSafeText(lastName, op, "lastName", ShortStringMaxLength); EnsureSafeText(emailID, op, "emailID", 254);` — emailID gets the RFC 5321 254-char cap rather than ShortStringMaxLength. Do NOT add an `@` presence check (operators may legitimately have legacy non-RFC IDs in DATA1; the spec doesn't require RFC compliance). Wire it from LacerteAccessClient.CreateClient inside the WireLog lambda BUT BEFORE the `dynamic com = _comInstance!;` line at LacerteAccessClient.cs:226 — mirror the Writer.cs:41/94/156 placement (validation -> WireLog -> dispatch is the wrong order; Writer puts validation inside the outer method body before WireLog, which is the pattern to follow for consistency — verify by checking Writer.cs:41 then mirror). Add unit test `BridgeInputValidationTests.ValidateCreateClientArgs_RejectsNulInFirstName` that builds a string with `\0` mid-value and asserts `LacerteSDKError` with `StatusCode == SyntheticStatusCodes.DetailWriteInvalid` and `Context["field"] == "firstName"`, plus one negative test per arg (appId-too-long, dataPath-control-char, clientID-with-semicolon, oversize-email). Then add an `LacerteAccessClientTests.CreateClient_RejectsControlCharBeforeBridgeUnavailable` test that calls CreateClient with `firstName="bob\0"` off-Windows and asserts it throws DetailWriteInvalid (NOT BridgeUnavailable) — proves the check fires before EnsureLive(). Update HANDOFF.md "Files added / changed" line 61 to add ", LacerteAccessClient.CreateClient" to the validator-callers list.

title: No concurrency tests for new ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock SemaphoreSlim
description: Phase-14 task P14-005 added ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1317, gating same-key writes through a per-key SemaphoreSlim to close a TOCTOU race between TryReplayIdempotent and StoreIdempotent. The only idempotency tests are sequential (WriteField_SameKey_SamePayload_DoesNotReexecute and WriteField_SameKey_DifferentPayload_ThrowsIdempotencyConflict). A grep for 'ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock|_idempotencyLocks|concurrent.*idempotency' across LacertMCP.Tests returns zero matches. The whole point of the new lock — that 100 threads firing the same idempotencyKey produce one execution + 99 cached replays (or 1 success + 99 IdempotencyConflicts on payload divergence), never 100 executions — has no regression coverage. A future refactor that drops the SemaphoreSlim wrap would not fail any test.
recommendation: Add a Parallel.For(0, 50, ...) test that drives the same idempotency key with identical payload through WriteDetail and asserts only ONE row was actually appended (mirror the pattern in SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests.WriteDetail_ParallelAppend_DoesNotLoseRows). Add a second test with divergent payloads asserting exactly one Success + N-1 IdempotencyConflict exceptions. Both should fail today if the SemaphoreSlim is removed.
rationale: P14-005 is one of the riskier round-1 correctness fixes (concurrency + double-execution money path). Shipping it with zero concurrent test coverage means any future regression silently re-opens the race.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by code+test inspection. (1) LacerteSessionManager.cs:1317 ships ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock with the per-key SemaphoreSlim wrapping the (TryReplay -> body -> Store) triple — this is the P14-005 production fix. (2) The only idempotency tests live in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs:262-310 and are strictly sequential — WriteField_SameKey_SamePayload_DoesNotReexecute and WriteField_SameKey_DifferentPayload_ThrowsIdempotencyConflict. (3) Grep across LacertMCP.Tests for `ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock|_idempotencyLocks|concurrent.*idempotency` returns ZERO matches; grep for `Task.WhenAll|Parallel.For` returns only SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests.cs (P14-028, list locking, unrelated to idempotency). (4) Critically, the P14-005 refinedRecommendation in audit-findings.json line 107 EXPLICITLY required: "Add one sim-only xUnit test in `LacerteSessionManagerTests` that uses `Task.WhenAll` to fire N=20 concurrent WriteDetail calls with the same idempotencyKey + identical payload, then asserts `ReadDetail("1001").Count` only grew by 1" — that test was never written. P14-005 shipped a half-fix: production code landed, test coverage omitted. This is precisely a "quality of the 71 new fixes — half-fixes, weak tests" hole the meta-audit was asked to find. Fully sim-actionable (SimulationStore + LacerteSessionManager only, no Windows/COM/ODBC dependency). The companion BROW seed already exists in NewSimManagerWithContext (used by the sequential tests), so the new test is a 30-line addition.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Add two xUnit facts to `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs` directly after line 310, satisfying the P14-005 task body that was checked off without test coverage:

(1) `WriteDetail_SameKey_SamePayload_Concurrent_AppendsExactlyOnce` — `var mgr = NewSimManagerWithContext(); var row = new DetailRow("Wages", "", "1", "", "", "", "W2", "T", "", 5000.0, "concurrent"); var beforeCount = (await mgr.ReadDetail("1001")).Count; var tasks = Enumerable.Range(0, 50).Select(_ => mgr.WriteDetail("1001", row, idempotencyKey: "kpar1")).ToArray(); var results = await Task.WhenAll(tasks); Assert.All(results, r => Assert.Equal(StatusCodes.Success, r)); var afterCount = (await mgr.ReadDetail("1001")).Count; Assert.Equal(beforeCount + 1, afterCount);` — fails today if the SemaphoreSlim wrap is removed (TOCTOU race lets 2+ appends slip through).

(2) `WriteDetail_SameKey_DivergentPayload_Concurrent_OneSuccessRestConflict` — 50 tasks split into two payload variants sharing one idempotencyKey, gather via `Task.WhenAll` of `Task<(int? status, Exception? ex)>` wrappers, then assert exactly one (or more, since the winning payload also short-circuit-replays) `StatusCodes.Success` AND that every non-success result is a `LacerteSDKError` with `SyntheticStatusCodes.IdempotencyConflict`. Concretely: `Assert.Contains(results, r => r.status == StatusCodes.Success); Assert.All(results.Where(r => r.ex != null), r => Assert.Equal(SyntheticStatusCodes.IdempotencyConflict, ((LacerteSDKError)r.ex!).StatusCode));` and assert `afterCount - beforeCount == 1` (only the winner's payload actually appended).

Place both in a new `[Fact]` pair under a `// Idempotency cache — concurrent state machine` section comment. No new helpers, no SimulationStore changes, no fixture work — uses the existing `NewSimManagerWithContext()` factory and the BROW seed at client 1001. Mirror the locking-test docstring style from `SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests` (cite P14-005 in the XML comment). Both tests must FAIL if `await sem.WaitAsync()` / `sem.Release()` at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1325/1332 is commented out — that's the canary signal the test exists to enforce.

title: Stale TODO/FIXME comments persist after round-1 cleanup wave
description: Round-1 HANDOFF.md line 20 claims `stale Stream A TODO comments cleared`, but several remain. (1) `SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:64-71` still carries `// TODO: drop once all call sites use the 9200-range names` + the `BridgeUnavailableLegacy=9010 / SimulationOnlyLegacy=9011` aliases tied to non-existent `Stream 4`. (2) `SeedData.cs:99` `// TODO: expand to 5-15 per client per task #17` — task #17 is checked off in Todo.md (Phase 2). (3) `LacerteSessionManager.cs:1285-1290` quotes the deleted Stream A TODO inline in a comment block that resurrects the very text round-1 said it removed. (4) `HealthTools.cs:33-35` `// TODO (Phase 9): surface live SDK HRESULT via _session.HealthProbe()` — P14-001 noted this in its rationale but the TODO never got converted to an issue reference. (5) `SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs:31,49` references `Stream B's parallel Tools tests` — a workflow-internal stream concept that has no meaning in the shipped codebase.
recommendation: Three concrete fixes: (1) Either delete the `BridgeUnavailableLegacy`/`SimulationOnlyLegacy` aliases entirely (grep for callers first — they're already documented as not referenced) OR rewrite the comment to drop `Stream 4` and replace with `v0.2 alias removal — see Todo.md follow-up entries`. (2) Delete the `// TODO: expand to 5-15` in SeedData.cs:99 (task #17 is done — if more rows are wanted, file a new follow-up). (3) Rewrite the `LacerteSessionManager.cs:1285-1290` comment to drop the resurrected TODO text — just state the current design (`Per-operation undo closures replace the whole-module snapshot/restore — see P14-043/P14-070`). (4) For `HealthTools.cs:33` and the test Stream B references, replace `Stream A/B/4` with concrete artifact references (a follow-up ID, a Phase number) or delete if the work is closed.
rationale: HANDOFF.md asserts these were cleared. Future agents grep for TODO to find loose ends, and stale comments either trigger re-work or get treated as noise — eroding the signal value of every other TODO in the tree. This directly contradicts the HANDOFF claim.

verdict.reasoning:
All five cited locations verified:

(1) SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:64 references "Stream 4" (workflow-internal term, not a real codebase concept), and lines 69-71 declare BridgeUnavailableLegacy=9010 + SimulationOnlyLegacy=9011 with a TODO at line 69 and self-referential note at line 170. Grep confirms ZERO external callers for either constant — only the StatusTable entry references them — so deletion is mechanically safe.

(2) SeedData.cs:99 confirmed `// TODO: expand to 5-15 per client per task #17.` — Todo.md line 37 (task #17) is `[x]` complete (Phase 2). The TODO is a stale "remember to come back" with the trail going nowhere.

(3) LacerteSessionManager.cs:1285-1290: The P14-070 verdict (audit-findings.json line 1537) said "delete the two stale TODO comments and replace them with a one-line note that explains the current design choice (not a deferred promise)." But the comment that landed (lines 1279-1290) literally reads `...and resolves the stale "TODO Stream A" pointing at SimulationStore.Snapshot/Restore (task #23 completed...)`. That's an 8-line history-of-the-old-comment block, not the focused 1-2-line current-design statement the verdict prescribed. So this is a half-fix of P14-070, not a re-surfacing of a separate issue.

(4) HealthTools.cs:33-35: `// TODO (Phase 9): surface live SDK HRESULT via _session.HealthProbe()` is still present. P14-001 wrapped the handler in WrapToolHandler and made mode dynamic but left the TODO untouched. The remediation is either a tracked follow-up ID or deletion of the speculative TODO.

(5) SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs:31 + 49: Two `Stream B's parallel Tools tests` references in comments. "Stream B" is a workflow-internal scaffolding concept with no codebase meaning. Confusing for future readers grepping for cluster names.

Phase-14 audit check: only P14-070 touched any of this (just the two LacerteSessionManager.cs Stream A TODOs); the four other classes of stale markers (SyntheticStatusCodes Stream 4 + Legacy aliases, SeedData task #17, HealthTools Phase 9 TODO, test Stream B refs) were NOT in audit-findings.json. The HANDOFF.md line 20 claim "stale Stream A TODO comments cleared" only covers the LacerteSessionManager half (and even there only partially).

Severity is correctly low/medium — these are documentation-quality issues, not behavior bugs. But the finding accurately identifies a class of cleanup the round-1 cleanup wave undersold. Fix is pure comment-edit + dead-const-removal, fully off-Windows actionable, ~5 minutes of work.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Five concrete edits, all comment/dead-code only, no test changes needed:

(1) **SyntheticStatusCodes.cs** — Delete lines 60-71 (the "Renumbered from agent 05..." comment block + the two `BridgeUnavailableLegacy`/`SimulationOnlyLegacy` const declarations) AND lines 170-181 (the two StatusTable alias entries + "See TODO above" comment). Grep confirms zero external callers. Replace the deleted block with a one-line comment: `// 9201/9202 are the canonical bridge-range codes (DECISIONS.md 2026-05-30 "Synthetic statusCode range").` Also delete the trailing comma after the BridgeUnavailable/SimulationOnly entries if needed to keep the dictionary literal valid.

(2) **SeedData.cs:99** — Delete the line `// TODO: expand to 5-15 per client per task #17.` (task #17 is closed). The existing "2-3 rows is enough" comment on the prior line stands alone.

(3) **LacerteSessionManager.cs:1279-1290** — This is a P14-070 half-fix follow-through. Replace the 11-line "TODO Stream A" history block with the focused version that P14-070's verdict actually prescribed: `// Per-call deep clone of only the active module — cheaper than // SimulationStore.Snapshot/Restore (which clones every module) and sufficient // because dry-run writes only touch the active context's module. See // P14-043/P14-070 for the prior whole-module snapshot removal.` Drop the resurrected "stale TODO Stream A pointing at" sentence.

(4) **HealthTools.cs:33-35** — Either (a) delete the `// TODO (Phase 9)` block since Phase 9 is closed and live HealthProbe wiring is a Windows-gated follow-up that should live in Todo.md, not as a TODO, OR (b) rewrite to `// HealthProbe live HRESULT surfacing is Windows-gated — tracked as follow-up Fxx in Todo.md.` (Pick a follow-up ID or add one.)

(5) **SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs:31 + 49** — Replace both `Stream B's parallel Tools tests` references with `the Tools/* tests that mutate the same FieldAccessMapLoader cache via AccessMapTestFixture`. The race condition the comment describes is real; just drop the workflow-internal "Stream B" label.

Net diff: ~25 lines deleted, ~6 lines added, zero behavior change, zero test impact. Confirms the HANDOFF.md "stale Stream A TODO comments cleared" claim end-to-end.

title: HANDOFF.md test-landing breakdown doesn't sum to 695 + double-counts numbers
description: The `Test landing breakdown (current)` block under `### Test landing breakdown (current)` does not arithmetically reconcile to the claimed 695 total. Adding the explicit numbers: Errors 53 + Schema (19+29+4+12=64) + Session/SimulationStore 47 + Session/LacerteSessionManager ~34 + Odbc ~95 + Bridge (38+62+~6+10=~116) + Tools ~90 + Cli ~25 + Logging/Resilience/Pagination/Prompts ~40 + Parity/Integration ~50 = ~614 (well short of 695). The Schema row also double-counts: `19 + 29 + 4 + 12 = 64` — the original Phase-1 schema count (per Todo.md task #15: `53 status-code tests + 19 schema tests`) was 19, so the 29+4+12 must already cover the new FieldAccessMap coverage tests, but presenting `19 + 29 + 4 + 12` reads as if all four are additive, inflating that bucket. The `Bridge ... = ~116` adds the 10 *skipped* tests into the passing total, which contradicts line 104's `695 passing + 10 skipped = 705`. Net effect: the breakdown looks authoritative but doesn't audit.
recommendation: Either drop the breakdown entirely (replace with a one-liner pointing the operator at `dotnet test --list-tests` for a per-class count, which won't drift) or recompute from scratch by running `dotnet test --list-tests` and grouping by namespace prefix once. If kept, fix Bridge to read `38 + 62 + ~6 = ~106 (+ 10 skipped)` so skip count isn't conflated with pass count, and add a final `... ≈ 695` line that actually sums to the claimed total. The maintenance cost of keeping the breakdown accurate across audits has already been demonstrated to exceed its value — recommend removal.
rationale: HANDOFF.md is the doc the next agent reads first via `/pickup`. A breakdown that doesn't sum to the total either erodes trust in the rest of HANDOFF or sends the agent on a wild-goose chase looking for the missing tests. The drift will only get worse as more tests land.

verdict.reasoning: Verified arithmetic: the bucket sums 53+64+47+34+95+116+90+25+40+50 = 614, which is 81 short of the claimed 695. The Bridge line (38+62+~6+10 skipped = ~116) is the clearest concrete defect — it folds 10 skipped tests into the passing-total column while line 104 explicitly separates passing (695) from skipped (10). The schema-row sub-arithmetic (19+29+4+12=64) does compute correctly, but the presentation is misleading because the Phase-1 schema bucket was 19 and only Phase-14 additions are the other 45; mixing them as four equal addends without labeling makes the bucket look inflated. No Phase-14 task in audit-findings.json or Todo.md addresses HANDOFF.md test-breakdown reconciliation — closest related findings are about README test counts (different file). The finding is in-session actionable (docs-only edit, no Windows needed) and useful because HANDOFF is the first file /pickup loads; a breakdown that visibly doesn't tie out either sends the next agent on a false hunt or erodes confidence in the rest of the doc.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace the per-bucket breakdown in HANDOFF.md lines 92-103 with a single line: `- See per-namespace counts via `dotnet test --list-tests` (totals: 695 passing + 10 skipped = 705, 0 failures, 0 warnings).` Rationale: the breakdown drifts on every test landing, has now visibly failed to reconcile (sums to 614, not 695), and conflates skipped tests into the passing total in the Bridge row. If the operator wants the breakdown kept, the minimal fix is: (a) split Bridge into `Bridge: 38 + 62 + ~6 = ~106 (+ 10 skipped)` so skips don't inflate the passing column, (b) re-tally every bucket against `dotnet test --list-tests | Group-Object` output and adjust the ~estimates until the explicit sum equals 695, and (c) append `Sum: 695` on its own line so future drift is self-evident. Recommendation: pick option 1 (remove); the maintenance cost has now demonstrably exceeded the value across two consecutive audits.

title: README tool table still describes lacerte_health as returning hardcoded sim string after P14-001 fix
description: README.md line 143 still describes `lacerte_health` as `Health probe. Returns "reachable (sim)" in sim mode.` — but P14-001 explicitly landed a fix that changed the response from a raw `reachable (sim)` string to a structured `{ mode, status }` envelope wrapped in `WrapToolHandler` (verified in `HealthTools.cs:36-40`). The Description attribute on the C# method now reads `Health probe. Returns a structured { mode, status } envelope reporting the active session mode (simulation/live) and reachability` — completely different from the README. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md line 92 also still refers to the count `15 Phase 5 read tools plus lacerte_health` without describing the new shape, and the universal-truth rule (`Tools (Phase 5 — Read)` table description must match `[Description]` attribute) is silently violated.
recommendation: Edit README.md line 143 to: `| lacerte_health | Health probe. Returns a structured { mode, status } envelope (Phase 9 will surface the live SDK HRESULT via _session.HealthProbe()). | 0 |`. Same edit pattern applies to any external doc that quotes the old description — grep for `reachable (sim)` across the repo and update the (3) hits in Todo.md/.todo-phase14-addendum.md (which are audit-finding rationale and are correctly preserved as historical) versus README.md (which is forward-facing and must reflect current behavior).
rationale: README is the user-facing tool contract; an LLM agent reading the table will form a different expectation than what the tool returns, leading to brittle prompt engineering. This is also a direct symptom of a P14 fix that landed in code without a corresponding doc sweep.

title: status always emits JSON — no human-readable format for interactive use
description: StatusCommand.Run unconditionally serializes the snapshot as JSON. The CLI help text says 'Print registration state, AppID (masked), mode, and storage backend' — nothing about it being JSON. An operator typing `lacerte-mcp status` in an interactive PowerShell gets a wall of JSON they must visually parse. The brief asked about `status --json vs default` but the polarity is inverted: there is no default human format, JSON is the only format. The roundtable pattern (humans get a table, scripts get --json) is the standard CLI shape — see `doctor` and `tools` which both lead with the human view.
recommendation: Default to a 6-line human view (e.g. `Registered: yes / AppID: a1b2c3d4-****... / Mode: simulation / Backend: file (/home/.../config.json) / Platform: Win32NT / Build: 0.1.0`) and gate the JSON behind a new `--json` flag. Keep the existing JSON shape so scripts that already consume it just need `--json`. Update the command description string to clarify the default format. Add one assertion in StatusCommandTests that the default output does NOT start with `{`.

Backcompat impact is minor and bounded — the smoke.ps1 script only checks status's exit code (not its output), and the README's one-line "JSON snapshot" callout can be updated in the same diff. title: doctor has no --json output — asymmetric with status and tools
description: `status` (JSON) and `tools --json` both emit machine-parseable output for CI/scripts. `doctor` emits only a human table — its exit code conveys 0/1/2 but the structured probe results (name, status, detail, remediation) are lost to scripts. A CI pipeline that wants to fail-fast with a useful error message has to grep stdout. The HANDOFF.md `scripts/smoke.ps1` already invokes doctor; once it grows into a fuller smoke check, the consumer needs the structured form.
recommendation: Add a `--json` option to DoctorCommand.Build() and an overload `Run(TextWriter, bool asJson)` that serializes `IList<ProbeResult>` (plus the computed exit code) as a JSON object. Use the same camelCase serializer convention `ToolsCommand` uses. Add one DoctorCommandTests assertion: `doctor --json` output is a parseable JSON object with `probes[]` and `exitCode` keys. ProbeStatus enum should serialize as its string name not int.
rationale: Of the three diagnostic verbs (status, tools, doctor), only doctor lacks a machine format despite being the most valuable for CI/smoke. Adding it is ~20 lines and harmonizes the contract.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real and new. DoctorCommand.cs (verified at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/DoctorCommand.cs) exposes only `Run(TextWriter)` — no --json option, no JSON serialization branch. Compare with StatusCommand (line 67: JsonSerializer.Serialize default-on) and ToolsCommand (line 47-50, 81-93: --json option emitting camelCase JSON). The asymmetry is real. Phase-14 grep over Todo.md and audit-findings.json: P14-017 fixed a doctor exit-code doc bug; P14-046 added `tools --json` and `unregister` verbs but explicitly did not extend doctor; P14-071 made ComputeExitCode pure/testable but added no JSON path. No Phase-14 task ships --json on doctor. The use-case is concrete: scripts/smoke.ps1 (lines 57-60) currently accepts any of exits 0/1/2 as "OK" because it has no way to read which probes specifically failed — once smoke grows into a real CI gate it must parse structured output. Implementation is ~20 lines, pure CLI, fully off-Windows-doable. One refinement: the original recommendation correctly calls out ProbeStatus enum serialization — CamelCase naming policy affects property names only, not enum values, so an explicit JsonStringEnumConverter is required to avoid emitting Status as the integer 0/1/2/3.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add a `--json` option to DoctorCommand.Build() and an overload `Run(TextWriter, bool asJson)`. Concrete shape — match StatusCommand+ToolsCommand conventions exactly so all three diagnostic verbs share one JSON contract: (1) Build(): add `var jsonOpt = new Option<bool>("--json", () => false, "Emit machine-parseable JSON instead of the human table."); cmd.AddOption(jsonOpt);` and pull it in the SetHandler the same way ToolsCommand does. (2) New overload `public static int Run(TextWriter writer, bool asJson)` — keep the existing `Run(TextWriter)` as `=> Run(writer, asJson: false)` to avoid breaking the existing DoctorCommandTests call sites. (3) When asJson: build `var payload = new { exitCode = exit, probes = results.Select(r => new { name = r.Name, status = r.Status, detail = r.Detail, remediation = r.Remediation }) };` then `JsonSerializer.Serialize(payload, new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true, PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase, DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull, Converters = { new JsonStringEnumConverter(JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase) } })`. CRITICAL: add the `JsonStringEnumConverter` — `PropertyNamingPolicy` does NOT apply to enum values, so without it ProbeStatus serializes as the int 0/1/2/3 instead of "pass"/"warn"/"fail"/"skipped". (4) Compute the exit code BEFORE serializing so it appears in the JSON payload AND still returns from Run. (5) Add three DoctorCommandTests: `Doctor_Json_EmitsParseableObject` (round-trips through JsonDocument, asserts `exitCode` and `probes` keys exist), `Doctor_Json_StatusSerializesAsString` (assert `probes[0].status` is a JsonValueKind.String, not Number — guards the enum-converter), and `Doctor_Json_ExitCodeMatchesReturnedInt` (the int Run() returns equals the `exitCode` field in stdout). (6) Bonus low-cost win: update scripts/smoke.ps1 line 60 to invoke `doctor --json` and use ConvertFrom-Json to grep for fail probes instead of swallowing exit 1 silently — that closes the loop the finding's rationale points at.

title: register/login Phase-9 stubs return exit 0 — silent no-op masquerades as success
description: InvokeLiveRegister (and the analogous block in LoginCommand line 61-71) prints `[stub] Lacerte SDK bridge not yet wired into the CLI (Phase 9 task #63)` and returns 0. On a real operator box that has Windows + the SDK installed, `lacerte-mcp register` will (a) mint a GUID, (b) print the stub message, and (c) exit 0. To any wrapping script or `if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)` check, this looks like a successful registration when in fact no Intuit consent ceremony has happened. The 24h ticket will never refresh, the AppID is unusable, and the operator finds out only when the first tool call returns NotSignedIn (9101).
recommendation: Return exit code 3 (or a documented dedicated 'not-implemented' code) from both stubs and print to stderr instead of stdout. Update the message to explicitly say 'Registration not yet wired; until Phase 9 ships, the AppID is minted but the Intuit handshake will not run — first MCP tool call will return NotSignedIn until you re-run after the upgrade.' Add an assertion test that the non-Win32NT stub still returns 0 (intentional cross-platform behaviour) but the Win32NT stub returns the new non-zero code.
rationale: An operator following the README quick-start on a Windows box will hit this silent no-op and discover it only when tools start failing hours later. Round-1 added the Phase-9 stub comments but kept exit 0; treating an explicit not-yet-implemented branch as success is a classic exit-code anti-pattern.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed by direct read. RegisterCommand.cs:91-106 InvokeLiveRegister: the Win32NT branch (line 100-105) prints "[stub] Lacerte SDK bridge not yet wired into the CLI (Phase 9 task #63)" to stdout and `return 0`. LoginCommand.cs:61-71 has the analogous structure: Win32NT branch (line 67-71) writes "[stub] Lacerte SDK bridge not yet wired" to stdout and `return 0`. Both stubs run on a real Windows operator box — `PlatformID.Win32NT` matches any Windows OS, not just "Windows + SDK wired" — so an operator following README line 115 (`lacerte-mcp register --app-name ... --tax-year 2024`) on the target machine will get exit 0 with no consent ceremony, no ITPRegistration call, and a 24h ticket that will never refresh. Cron-driven `lacerte-mcp login` will silently succeed forever. The threat is acute: README line 117 promises "calls ITPRegistration.Register() and prints the GUID for backup" — that promise is unfulfilled on the same Windows box the docs target.

Not a Phase-14 duplicate. P14-065 (lines 1412-1427 of audit-findings.json) addressed AppID GUID masking in stdout — it left the exit-code semantics untouched. The other "exit code" findings in audit-findings.json are about DoctorCommand (lines 355-371, 1543-1559), not register/login. Phase-14 Todo entries #70 and #71 confirm the stub is documented as deferred, but they don't address the silent-success exit code. The new AppIdMaskingTests.cs covers GUID leak but not exit code.

Actionable in this sim-only dev env: pure C# change to return non-zero on the Win32NT stub path, plus xUnit tests that pin both exit code and stderr-vs-stdout routing. Tests already use IsolatedAppIdScope + APPDATA redirection (see AppIdMaskingTests pattern); no Windows/Lacerte SDK needed because the Win32NT branch is reached on this dev box (PowerShell on Win32NT). For the off-Windows branch, can use Bash-side execution or skip-on-Windows attribute.

title: field-access discover stub message is misleading about why it fails
description: `discover` always prints `Bulk introspection requires live SDK + Windows. See follow-up F5 in Todo.md for the introspection script roadmap.` and exits 2. An operator on a Windows + live SDK box reading this message reasonably concludes 'I have those, so this should work — let me check my env'. But the truth is the command is unimplemented at all — `F5` is the roadmap, not a flag. The message conflates 'requires X' (which would be a routing/gate problem) with 'not built yet' (a feature gap). Operators will waste time toggling LACERTE_LIVE / checking the SDK install before reading the source. Exit code 2 is also wrong per the documented contract (exit 2 = skipped because environment inapplicable; this is not environment-dependent — it's unimplemented everywhere).
recommendation: Rewrite the message: 'Bulk field-access introspection is not yet implemented (tracked as follow-up F5 in Todo.md — needs live-SDK write-probing). For now, populate the access map by hand with `lacerte-mcp field-access set` or by editing the JSON shards under Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/.' Exit with code 3 (not-implemented) instead of 2 — reserve 2 for environment-skip cases the way doctor uses it. Add a single test that locks the exit code and the substring 'not yet implemented'.
rationale: Misleading error messages cost operator time. The exit-code semantics inconsistency (this exits 2 for 'not implemented', doctor exits 2 for 'skipped — wrong OS') is the specific case the brief asked about: 'does it tell the operator to run on the live box?' — the answer today is yes, but that answer is a lie because it wouldn't work even on the live box.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading FieldAccessCommand.cs lines 215-227 (the cited stub) and DoctorCommand.cs lines 20/61/107 (the canonical exit-code contract). DoctorCommand explicitly defines the exit-code semantics as `Exit 2 — at least one skipped (probe inapplicable on this OS)` — i.e., environment-skip. `field-access discover` returns 2 for "not implemented at all," which collides with that contract — even on Windows + live SDK + LACERTE_LIVE=1 the command wouldn't work. The audit finding's "operator wastes time toggling env / checking SDK install" is a plausible failure mode given the message literally says "requires live SDK + Windows."

The finding is also sharper than the original author realized: F5 is NO LONGER a roadmap item — Todo.md line 164 confirms `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper/` already shipped as a net48 x64 console project, and HANDOFF.md "Next Task" #3 tells operators to run `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe --module I --table 1` directly.
