title: LACERTE_LIVE=1 AND LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 silently picks Simulation with no warning
description: The mode resolution `Mode = (!sim && live && onWindows) ? Live : Simulation` makes LACERTE_SIMULATION the trump card. The precedence IS documented in ARCHITECTURE.md and tested, but when an operator sets both env vars expecting live, the server starts in Simulation mode and emits no log warning, no doctor probe, and no entry in lacerte_session_status that explains why live did not engage. The same silent fallback fires when LACERTE_LIVE=1 is set on non-Windows — the OS check in the same expression flips to Sim with no diagnostic. The first symptom the operator sees is that ListClients returns canned seed data instead of their real Lacerte fixtures, which they may not immediately spot.
recommendation: On construction, if (live==1 && sim==1) or (live==1 && !onWindows), write a single ILogger.LogWarning at startup that names the conflict and the chosen mode. Add a 'Mode resolution' line item to the SessionStatusSnapshot output so the operator can see the reason (e.g. `reason = 'LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 overrode LACERTE_LIVE=1'`). Add a doctor probe 'Mode' that prints Live/Sim plus the reason for the choice, FAIL if both flags conflict (since this is almost certainly a config bug).
rationale: Mode selection is the single most important config decision in the project; a silent fallback to Sim against operator intent is a personal-tool footgun. Round-1 covered precedence correctness with a unit test but did not audit the operator-feedback gap when the precedence fires against intent.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs:131-135. The expression `Mode = (!sim && live && onWindows) ? Live : Simulation` silently picks Simulation in two operator-surprising cases: (a) both LACERTE_LIVE=1 AND LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 set (sim trumps live with no signal), and (b) LACERTE_LIVE=1 set off-Windows (OS check flips to Sim with no signal). No `ILogger.LogWarning` / `WireLog` call fires at construction; SessionStatusSnapshot.cs only carries `Mode` (no resolution reason), and DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes (verified all 7 probes — Build version / Windows version / x64 / .NET 4.8 / ODBC DSN / SDK install / LACERTE_DATA_PATH / AppID) has no Mode probe at all. Searched audit-findings.json end-to-end for "LACERTE_LIVE", "LACERTE_SIMULATION", "mode resolution", "conflict", "both flags" — Phase-14 covered precedence-correctness via a unit test and EditionDetection warning-once, but never added the conflict-warning + status-reason surface this finding asks for. The fix is pure sim-only: WireLog.RecordSync at ctor + a new `ModeResolutionReason` field on SessionStatusSnapshot + a Mode probe in DoctorCommand. All three touch files Phase-14 already modified, so the patch slots cleanly. Severity "medium" is honest for a single-operator personal tool — the symptom (ListClients returns seed data) IS discoverable, but on an LLM-driven loop a confused operator could spend real time before noticing, and the cost-vs-fix ratio is excellent (~30 LOC + 2 unit tests). The original recommendation is well-scoped; I tightened the call-sites and pinned the error-code choice for the doctor Fail leg.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three coordinated changes, all sim-actionable in-session:

(1) `LacerteSessionManager` ctor (after line 135): if `live && sim` OR `live && !onWindows`, emit ONE warning via the existing logging surface — `WireLog.RecordSync<object?>("ModeResolution", new { resolved = Mode.ToString(), liveRequested = live, simRequested = sim, onWindows }, () => null!)` is consistent with the EditionDetection pattern already established at line 340. Also stash the reason on a new private field `_modeResolutionReason` (string, one of: `"both LACERTE_LIVE=1 and LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 set — LACERTE_SIMULATION won"`, `"LACERTE_LIVE=1 requested but not on Windows — fell back to Simulation"`, or `null` when the resolution was unambiguous).

(2) `SessionStatusSnapshot.cs`: add an optional `string? ModeResolutionReason = null` positional record field (mirrors the existing optional BuildVersion / Edition pattern at line 29-34 — additive, no breaking change). Wire it from `LacerteSessionManager.SessionStatus()` so `lacerte-mcp status` JSON surfaces the reason whenever it's non-null. Add a SessionToolsTests fact pinning the field appears when both env flags are set.

(3) `DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes()`: add probe #8 "Mode resolution" that re-reads LACERTE_LIVE / LACERTE_SIMULATION env vars + onWindows and reports Pass ("Live" or "Simulation — unambiguous"), Warn ("Simulation — LACERTE_LIVE=1 requested but not on Windows"), or **Fail** ("conflict — both LACERTE_LIVE=1 and LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 set; refusing to guess") with the remediation "Unset one of LACERTE_LIVE / LACERTE_SIMULATION." Fail (not Warn) is correct for the both-set case per the finding's rationale — it's almost certainly a config bug and `DoctorCommand.ComputeExitCode` already promotes Fail to exit-1 (verified at line 119). Add a DoctorCommandTests fact using the public `ComputeExitCode(IList<ProbeResult>)` seam introduced by P14-071 to pin both-set → exit 1.

Skip emitting via `ILogger` — this project uses WireLog as the canonical structured-logging surface (no Microsoft.Extensions.Logging dependency in LacertMCP.Server.csproj), and forcing one in would be inconsistent with every other diagnostic emission in the codebase.

title: Doctor command does not probe operating mode, AppID validity, or live readiness
description: RunAllProbes covers build version, Windows, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, Lacerte SDK install dir, LACERTE_DATA_PATH presence, and AppID persisted. It does NOT probe: (a) what mode the server WOULD start in (LACERTE_LIVE/LACERTE_SIMULATION resolution); (b) whether the persisted AppID is a parseable Guid (Get() returns null on parse failure, indistinguishable from 'not set'); (c) whether the COM ProgID `LacerteSDK_Access.TPRegistration` resolves (would catch a half-installed SDK); (d) whether the LACERTE_DATA_PATH value (when set) actually exists on disk and is a directory; (e) LACERTE_DATA_ROOT validity; (f) Schema/FieldAccessMap shard presence (an operator with a corrupt build dir gets 'Unknown' field-access for every write with no probe explaining why). The probe set documented in the XML doc (lines 22-27) is the full set actually run — which means the operator's first-touch troubleshooting tool is silent on the most likely failure modes.
recommendation: Add probes (priority order): (1) Mode resolution probe — read both env flags + OS, print the resolved mode and FAIL/WARN on conflict (per finding #3); (2) ProgID probe — `Type.GetTypeFromProgID("LacerteSDK_Access.TPRegistration") != null`, FAIL with 'register the SDK COM server' remediation; (3) LACERTE_DATA_PATH directory-exists probe (currently it only checks the env var is set, not that the path resolves); (4) FieldAccessMap base shards probe — enumerate Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json next to the assembly, FAIL if zero present; (5) AppID parse probe — distinguish 'not persisted' from 'persisted but malformed'.
rationale: Doctor is the only place the project tells the operator what is wrong before they hit a tool call. The current probe set documents prerequisites but skips the most common live-mode failure modes (mode resolution, COM ProgID, FieldAccessMap copy-to-output). Round-1 added the exit-code unit test and the BuildVersion probe but did not expand the probe surface.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/DoctorCommand.cs (lines 124-234) and AppIdStore.cs. All 5+ claimed gaps confirmed:

(a) Mode resolution — RunAllProbes never reads LACERTE_LIVE/LACERTE_SIMULATION. LacerteSessionManager.cs:131-135 shows the resolution logic — setting BOTH env vars silently resolves to Simulation (sim wins via `!sim && live`), and there is NO doctor surface explaining this. Operator who sets LACERTE_LIVE=1 on Windows but leaves a stale LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 from a prior shell will silently get sim mode with no doctor signal.

(b) ProgID probe — DoctorCommand only checks the SDK install directory (lines 315-338), never that `LacerteSDK_Access.TPRegistration` or `LacerteSDK_Access.LacerteAccess` ProgIDs actually resolve. A half-registered MSI (files present, COM regsvr32 not applied) passes the doctor and explodes at the first tool call. Bridge/LacerteAccessClient.cs uses `Type.GetTypeFromProgID` — same call would work as a probe.

(c) LACERTE_DATA_PATH dir-exists — lines 199-212 only test `string.IsNullOrEmpty(dataPath)`; never `Directory.Exists(dataPath)`. A typo'd path passes as `Pass`.

(d) FieldAccessMap shards — AppIdStore's neighbor `Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json` ships as Content (Todo line 30, F5 dumper), but if MSBuild's CopyToOutputDirectory loses them, FieldAccessMapLoader silently returns Unknown. No probe enumerates `Path.Combine(AssemblyDirectory, "Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json")`.

(e) AppID parse — AppIdStore.Get() at line 107 (`Guid.TryParse` → null) and line 162 (file path `Guid.TryParse` → null) both return null indistinguishably for "absent" vs "corrupt". Doctor message "not persisted" misleads the operator who DID run register.

(f) LACERTE_DATA_ROOT — code references it (per grep hit in 17 files including PathValidation.cs, Registration.cs, FieldAccessMapLoader.cs) but doctor never probes it.

Phase-14 dupe check: P14-071 added ComputeExitCode tests only. The "0. Build version" probe at line 132 is the only P14 probe-surface change (P14-040). P14-017 fixed a doc string about doctor exit codes. NONE of the 71 Phase-14 items expanded the probe set — the audit-findings.json doctor hits (1543, 1551, 998) are about exit-code tests, README accuracy, and 'doctor does not probe live connectivity' (1001 — that's rationale text for unrelated CLI cleanup, not a landed probe).

Actionable off-Windows: all 6 probes are testable in sim — Directory.Exists is OS-agnostic; Type.GetTypeFromProgID returns null off-Windows so the probe must Skip not Fail there; mode-resolution and AppID-parse are pure env/parse logic. ProbeResult + ComputeExitCode shape already supports adding entries without test churn (DoctorCommandTests is parameterized on counts, not names).

Useful: doctor is the SOLE first-touch troubleshooter; these are the highest-yield additions per failure-mode-frequency. Not bikeshedding.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Add six probes to DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes (priority order — first three are the highest-yield):

(1) "Operating mode" probe — read LACERTE_LIVE + LACERTE_SIMULATION + onWindows. Mirror the resolution logic in LacerteSessionManager.cs:131-135 EXACTLY (consider extracting to a shared `SessionMode.Resolve(IEnvironment)` helper to guarantee parity). Emit Pass with detail "resolved: Simulation (off-Windows default)" / "resolved: Live (LACERTE_LIVE=1 on Windows)" / etc. Emit Warn when BOTH flags are 1 (sim wins silently) or when LACERTE_LIVE=1 off-Windows (will fall back to sim). Always Pass — this probe is informational; failure is a separate concern.

(2) "Lacerte COM ProgID" probe — `Type.GetTypeFromProgID("LacerteSDK_Access.TPRegistration") != null` AND `LacerteSDK_Access.LacerteAccess`. Skipped off-Windows (Type.GetTypeFromProgID returns null off-Windows too, so naive call would mis-Fail). Fail with remediation "SDK files present but COM not registered; re-run the 64-bit Lacerte SDK MSI as Administrator (or `regsvr32 LacerteSDK_Access.dll` from the install dir)."

(3) "LACERTE_DATA_PATH resolves" probe — only when LACERTE_DATA_PATH is set, add a second probe checking `Directory.Exists(dataPath)`. Fail with "path does not exist on disk: {dataPath}; correct the env var or run `lacerte_set_context` with a valid path." Keep the existing "env set" Warn probe separate.

(4) "FieldAccessMap base shards" probe — enumerate `Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Schema", "FieldAccessMap", "base", "*.json")`. Pass with count when ≥9 (one per module). Fail with "0 base shards found; build dir is missing FieldAccessMap content — `dotnet build` or reinstall." Use AppContext.BaseDirectory not Assembly.Location (Single-file deploy safe).

(5) "AppID parse" probe — replace the current AppID probe with one that distinguishes (a) AppIdStore credential/file ABSENT (current Fail "not persisted"); (b) raw value present but `Guid.TryParse` fails (NEW Fail "persisted value is not a valid GUID — run `lacerte-mcp register --reset` to re-mint"). Requires either exposing `AppIdStore.GetRaw()` returning the raw string, or adding `AppIdStore.GetDiagnostic()` returning a tri-state enum {Absent, ParseFailed, Ok(Guid)}.

(6) "LACERTE_DATA_ROOT" probe — same shape as (3) but for LACERTE_DATA_ROOT.

Test additions: add probes to DoctorCommandTests covering (1) mode-resolution warn-on-conflict via env-var test fixture; (2) ProgID Skipped off-Windows; (3) DATA_PATH fail-when-set-but-missing; (4) FieldAccessMap fail when probe directory empty (use a TempDir + AppContext-relative resolution helper that's overridable for tests); (5) parse-fail vs absent distinguished via LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE + writing a config.json with `"AppId": "not-a-guid"`.

Also: update the DoctorCommand XML doc (lines 22-27) to list all 13 probes, and update README quick-start which currently lists 7.

title: App.config missing/corrupt produces no detectable error path or doctor probe
description: The App.config is load-bearing for the live SDK COM activation (`useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy=true` + supportedRuntime v4.0) — without it `new LacerteSDK_Access.LacerteAccess()` throws on construction per the file's own header comment. However: (a) nothing in code verifies the file is present or well-formed at startup, (b) doctor has no probe for it, (c) if the file is missing the operator sees a raw COM exception at first wire call instead of a clear 'App.config missing' diagnostic, (d) if an operator copies just the .exe to a different dir without the .exe.config the first live-mode register() will throw a COM HRESULT that the BridgeUnavailable mapper will translate to a generic 'reason: ex.Message' (Registration.cs line 105). The project relies entirely on the file existing in the output dir; there is no copy-time check, no startup check, and no operator-readable error.
recommendation: Add a doctor probe `App.config runtime shim`: check that `Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule.FileName + ".config"` exists, read it, confirm the `useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy=true` attribute and supportedRuntime element are present. FAIL with remediation 'App.config is missing or has been edited — restore the runtime shim per ARCHITECTURE.md Build & Runtime'. Optionally add a Program.cs startup check that emits a single ILogger.LogError if the resolved AppDomainSetup.ConfigurationFile is null/missing on Windows.
rationale: App.config is silently load-bearing and the failure mode (raw COM construction throw) is one of the worst possible operator experiences. The file's own comment says 'Do not remove' but offers no enforcement. Round-1 lenses audited the COM bridge correctness but did not surface the App.config-missing UX hole.

verdict.reasoning: Verified real: (1) App.config is load-bearing per its own header comment — mixed-mode LacerteSDK_Access requires useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy. (2) Grep across all .cs files returns zero reads of App.config / .exe.config / ConfigurationFile — nothing probes for it. (3) DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes (lines 124-234) has 8 probes (build version, Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install, LACERTE_DATA_PATH, AppID GUID) — no App.config shim probe. (4) The failure path is genuinely silent: LacerteAccessClient.cs:67-72 catches all construction exceptions and reduces them to `_comInstance = null`, which surfaces as `BridgeUnavailable` with `reason: ex.Message` per Registration.cs:99-106 — the operator sees a raw COM HRESULT, not "App.config missing." (5) Phase-14 P14-062 only documents env-only convention; it explicitly leaves App.config alone and does not add a probe. No Phase-14 task addresses this UX hole. Actionable off-Windows: probe logic uses File.Exists + XML parsing of `Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule.FileName + ".config"` — all cross-platform APIs; can be unit-tested with synthetic paths. The probe can be authored + tested on Linux/Mac just like the existing ComputeExitCode pure function (P14-071 pattern).
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `ProbeAppConfigShim()` to `DoctorCommand.cs` (slot it after probe #2 "x64 process" since it's a build-output check, not a Windows-only check — the file ships with the .exe regardless of OS). Logic: (a) resolve `var configPath = AppDomain.CurrentDomain.SetupInformation.ConfigurationFile` (cross-platform, returns the .exe.config path even on Linux/Mono); fallback to `Process.GetCurrentProcess().MainModule.FileName + ".config"` if null/empty; (b) if file missing → Fail "App.config not next to LacertMCP.Server.exe" with remediation "Restore App.config per ARCHITECTURE.md 'Build & Runtime' — the file is load-bearing for the mixed-mode CLR shim and must ship next to the .exe"; (c) if present, parse XML and assert both `/configuration/startup[@useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy='true']` AND `/configuration/startup/supportedRuntime[@version='v4.0']` exist → Fail "App.config runtime shim has been edited — useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy or supportedRuntime missing" with remediation pointing at the canonical 14-line file in the repo; (d) pass with detail `runtime shim present (useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy=true, supportedRuntime v4.0)`. Add 3 xUnit tests against a helper `ProbeAppConfigShimAt(string path)` that takes the config path as an arg (pure function — testable off-Windows like ComputeExitCode): missing-file → Fail, malformed-xml → Fail, valid-shim → Pass. Skip the startup-Program.cs ILogger check from the original recommendation — it's redundant once doctor covers it and would noise up server stdout on every launch; the doctor probe is the single source of truth. Also append a one-line note to README's Troubleshooting section entry "(d) shim removed (restore App.config)" already queued in the Phase 14 troubleshooting task: "→ `lacerte-mcp doctor` will flag this as red."

title: Program.cs Main has zero env validation; bad env values fail at first tool call
description: Main() builds a Host, adds the LacerteSessionManager singleton, and calls RunAsync. There is no startup validation pass. Concrete failures the operator hits LATE rather than early: (a) LACERTE_DATA_ROOT set to a malformed path — PathValidation will reject it on FIRST tool call instead of startup; (b) LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH set to an inaccessible dir — silently falls back to ./logs (per WireLog ResolveConfig line 583-584) with no startup signal that the override was discarded; (c) LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=true (not '1') — silently disabled because ResolveConfig does strict '== "1"'; the operator who used 'true' or '1 ' (trailing space) sees no logs and no warning. None of these surface in the MCP stdio protocol's startup phase; the agent only learns at first call.
recommendation: Add an `EnvironmentValidator.RunAtStartup(ILogger)` step between AddSingleton and AddMcpServer. Walk each LACERTE_* env var, parse/validate it (int for years, dir-exists for paths, '1' vs 'true'/'yes'/'on'), log warnings to stderr for any rejected value, and exit non-zero on hard-incompatible combinations (e.g. LACERTE_LIVE=1 on non-Windows with no LACERTE_DATA_PATH). Print a single startup banner line listing the resolved mode + effective config values so the operator sees what the server thinks the world looks like.
rationale: Startup is the only point the operator is watching the terminal. After the MCP handshake completes, errors are buried inside JSON-RPC envelopes the agent surfaces inconsistently. A 12-line StartupBanner that prints {mode, dataPath, defaultYear, debugWire, appIdSource} converts dozens of 'why doesn't my config work' support questions into a copy-paste.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by direct read. Program.cs Main (lines 18-44) is exactly as described: it builds the host, wires LacerteSessionManager + AddMcpServer, and calls RunAsync with zero env validation or banner. WireLog.ResolveConfig at WireLog.cs:561-562 does strict `flag != "1"` — `LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=true` silently disables logging. LacerteSessionManager.ReadEnvFlag at line 1441-1444 also does strict `== "1"` so the same trap applies to LACERTE_LIVE, LACERTE_SIMULATION, LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC, LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE. The LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH silent-fallback path the finding cites (WireLog.cs:583-584) is confirmed: if PathValidation.ValidateLogDir returns null the operator gets the default ./logs dir with no stderr signal that their override was discarded. Phase-14 search across Todo.md (P14-001 through P14-071) and audit-findings.json finds NO startup-validation or startup-banner task: P14-016/033 added env docs to README but the code surface is unchanged. P14-049 added defensive path validation but left the silent-fallback behavior in place (deliberately, per the comment). DoctorCommand exists in the CLI but only runs when the operator types `lacerte-mcp doctor` — when Claude Desktop spawns the MCP stdio binary directly, doctor output never appears. Fix is pure C# in Program.cs + a new small EnvValidator class, fully sim-actionable. Useful: this is the operator's only debugging touchpoint before the agent absorbs all output into JSON-RPC envelopes; the 'why doesn't my LACERTE_LIVE=true work' failure mode is real. Minor: the finding's example 'LACERTE_LIVE=1 on non-Windows with no LACERTE_DATA_PATH' as a hard-exit case is too aggressive — that's actually the documented sim-fallback path (line 133-135), so warn-not-exit is correct there.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `src/LacertMCP.Server/Startup/EnvValidator.cs` invoked from Program.cs:Main BEFORE `builder.Build().RunAsync()`. Single public method `Validate(TextWriter stderr)` returns `(bool exitNow, int exitCode)`. Checks (all writing one-line warnings to stderr, none throwing):  (1) Boolean-shaped vars (LACERTE_LIVE, LACERTE_SIMULATION, LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE, LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC, LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE) — if value is non-null AND not exactly "1" AND not exactly "0" AND not exactly empty, warn `[startup] LACERTE_X='<value>' is not '1' — treated as disabled (this server uses strict '1'-means-on semantics).` Lower-case 'true'/'yes'/'on' specifically called out. Whitespace-trimmed compare for the warning so '1 '/' 1' both warn AND remain disabled (preserves existing semantics; warn only). (2) LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR — if set, `int.TryParse` and require 2018 <= y <= DateTime.UtcNow.Year+1; warn-and-ignore on reject. (3) LACERTE_DATA_ROOT — if set, run through PathValidation.ValidateDataRoot (factor out from existing PathValidation) — warn-and-ignore on reject (do NOT fail-fast; sim mode doesn't need it). (4) LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH — if set AND LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE='1', run through the same PathValidation.ValidateLogDir the WireLog uses and warn `[startup] LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH='<value>' rejected — wire log will write to ./logs instead.` on null return. Then print exactly one banner line to stderr: `[startup] LacerteMCP <assemblyVer> mode=<sim|live> dataPath=<value-or-unset> defaultTaxYear=<value-or-current> debugWire=<on|off> wireLogDir=<resolved-dir-or-NA> appIdSource=<credman|file|none>`. Wire-up: call EnvValidator.Validate AFTER `builder.Logging.ClearProviders/AddConsole` so the banner uses the same stderr stream the rest of logging will. Do NOT hard-exit anywhere — Boundary Invariant #4 (sim works off-Windows) means we cannot block startup on missing platform features. Tests: pure xUnit against EnvValidator with a `Dictionary<string,string>` env injection (mirror existing LacerteSessionManager ctor's `env` parameter pattern) — assert 8 warning scenarios + 1 happy-path banner; no Windows or Lacerte dependency.

title: FieldAccessMapLoader fails-open silently on missing/empty shards — every write becomes Unknown
description: LoadModule (line 247-250) returns an empty Dictionary when the per-module JSON shard is missing from the build output. LoadOverlay (line 288-291, 318-324) does the same on missing or malformed JSON, with the explicit doc comment 'A shipping typo in an overlay should fail open to base-map behavior, not nuke the write path.' Combined with AssertWritable's Unknown branch (line 219), this means: if the entire FieldAccessMap directory fails to copy to output (e.g. operator runs from a partially-published dir, or csproj Content include is broken), EVERY write returns synthetic 9012 UnknownFieldAccess with 'Refusing to write. Pass force:true to override.' The operator has no way to distinguish 'this field is genuinely unknown' from 'the access-map directory is empty'. There is no doctor probe, no startup log, and no SessionStatus field that surfaces 'access-map loaded 0 modules / 0 overlays'.
recommendation: Add a one-shot startup self-check (called from Program.cs OR lazily on first AssertWritable call): enumerate Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json next to the assembly, count modules + overlays loaded, log warning if zero modules loaded ('FieldAccessMap directory empty — every write will report UnknownFieldAccess. Verify build copied Schema/FieldAccessMap/**/*.json to output.'). Add a doctor probe `Field-access map shards` that counts module shards and FAILs if zero. Optionally surface the count in lacerte_session_status so the operator can see {accessMapModules: 9, accessMapOverlays: 4} or {accessMapModules: 0} at a glance.
rationale: Round-1 caught the JSON-throw-poison fix (catch JsonException to avoid re-throw per call) but the broader 'fail-open with no diagnostic' UX gap was not surfaced. The map is the only write-safety boundary; an operator running from a broken build directory gets uniform 9012 errors with no signal that the access map itself is the problem. This is one of the hardest support tickets to diagnose remotely because the symptom (refuses to write) and the cause (empty map) look unrelated.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct read of FieldAccessMapLoader.cs and cross-checked against Phase-14 tasks in Todo.md + audit-findings.json. The finding is REAL: LoadModule (line 247-250) returns empty on missing file, LoadOverlay (line 290-291, 318-323) returns empty sentinel on missing file or JsonException — both by design. Combined with AssertWritable's Unknown branch (line 218-224) emitting 9012 UnknownFieldAccess, an empty Schema/FieldAccessMap/ directory makes every WriteField uniformly refuse with no diagnostic distinguishing 'map empty' from 'field genuinely unknown.' This is the same as today's state (shards ship as {} per v1) — WriteParityTests confirms the gate fires for known fields.

NOT a duplicate of any Phase-14 task:
- P14-024 added try/catch on overlay JsonException + test coverage for malformed overlays. Does NOT add a startup self-check or doctor probe for empty shards.
- P14-020 (Modules consolidation) routed LoadModule through Modules.FileBasenameFor but added no diagnostics.
- P14-040 (BuildInfo doctor probe) added a 'Build version' probe — different surface, not shard counts.
- P14-release-script verifies Schema/FieldAccessMap/{manifest,base,overlays} at stage time (release.ps1 lines 4, 46, 58-60) — but only catches build-side breaks. An operator running from a hand-copied bin/ or a custom-extracted single-exe still gets silent fail-open with zero runtime signal.

Verified no existing surface counts shards: DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes has 8 probes (Build version + 7 install probes), none enumerate Schema/FieldAccessMap. SessionStatusSnapshot.cs has no accessMap fields. Program.cs has no FieldAccessMap startup log.

Fix is 100% off-Windows actionable: file enumeration + log + 1 doctor probe + 2 SessionStatusSnapshot fields. No Lacerte/COM/ODBC touch.

Severity is fairly medium — the release script catches the most common operator path, but the runtime diagnostic gap remains a real support-ticket trap (described symptom 'refuses to write' has no causal connection to actual cause 'access map directory empty/missing').
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three narrow additions, all sim-only:

(1) Add `FieldAccessMapLoader.GetShardCounts()` public static helper returning `(int modules, int overlays)` — scans `{assemblyDir}/Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json` and `overlays/ty*-not-supported.json` and returns counts WITHOUT loading them. Pure file enumeration; no JSON parse cost; safe to call from hot path / startup.

(2) Add a Doctor probe `Field-access map shards` in DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes (insert after Build version): probe Pass if modules > 0, Warn if modules == 0 (text: "0 module shards found under {SchemaRoot}/base — every WriteField will return 9012 UnknownFieldAccess. Verify build copied Schema/FieldAccessMap/**/*.json to output."). Do NOT Fail — the v1 shards ship empty by design (Phase-9 introspection pending per Todo.md #13), so Fail would break the green doctor today; Warn is the right severity. When Phase-9 lands and shards actually populate, upgrade to Fail at zero. Output format: "Pass: 9 modules, 4 overlays loaded".

(3) Add `accessMap` to SessionStatusSnapshot with shape `{ modules: 9, overlays: 4, root: "{SchemaRoot()}" }` (root for triage — operator can see whether the lookup directory is where they expect). Surface in `lacerte_session_status` output. Two new fields, ~6 lines.

Skip the "startup log warning" piece from the original recommendation — Program.cs ships clean today (no startup banners) and a warning-to-stderr on first AssertWritable call would be noisy and order-dependent. The doctor probe is the explicit "operator runs this when confused" surface; the SessionStatusSnapshot field is the "operator pastes status into a bug report" surface. Together they cover the diagnostic gap without adding any stdout noise.

Tests: (a) DoctorCommandTests asserts the new probe appears and Warns when SchemaRoot points to an empty temp directory (use AccessMapTestFixture-style reflection to redirect or just point at an empty temp); (b) SessionStatusSnapshot test asserts the accessMap counts are reflected when shards are seeded vs absent; (c) FieldAccessMapLoader test asserts GetShardCounts returns (0,0) for empty dir, (N,M) for seeded dir.

title: WrapToolHandler.Run wraps unknown exceptions as StatusCodes.Error (0) which carries a useless userMessage
description: The fallback path turns any non-LacerteSDKError into LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.Error). The Error(0) StatusInfo is "Lacerte returned a generic error with no further detail." with remediation "Re-run with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 to capture the bridge call args; check Windows Event Viewer for SDK traces." Both lie when the underlying exception is a NullReferenceException, ArgumentException, OdbcException, FileNotFoundException, JsonException — none of those came from Lacerte at all. The LLM is told to look in Windows Event Viewer for an SDK trace that doesn't exist. With rawError redacted to "***" (P14-019), even the exceptionType (which IS preserved) is the only signal — and "InvalidOperationException" is not actionable on its own. The userMessage should depend on whether the exception is bridge-origin or MCP-origin.
recommendation: Reserve StatusCodes.Error (0) for actual SDK code 0 returns. Add SyntheticStatusCodes.InternalError = 9200 (or relocate within 9200-range) with userMessage "The MCP server itself raised an unexpected exception — not a Lacerte SDK error." and remediation "Capture the exceptionType from context, re-run with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1, and file an issue with the wire log line." Have WrapToolHandler's catch-Exception branch route to this new code. Keep exceptionType in context (already done). Optionally classify well-known types — OdbcException → DBFNotAccessable, FileNotFoundException → InvalidDataPath — but the default should not lie about the error's origin.
rationale: Misattributing a server-side bug as an SDK error degrades both LLM autonomy (it'll try SDK remediations that can't help) and operator triage (Windows Event Viewer is the wrong place to look for a NullRef in the C# server). This is the silent failure mode that grows worse as the tool surface expands.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:67-79 (catches every non-LacerteSDKError as StatusCodes.Error=0), src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/StatusCodes.cs:76-80 (Error(0)'s userMessage literally claims "Lacerte returned a generic error with no further detail" and the remediation points the operator to "Windows Event Viewer for SDK traces"), and src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/SyntheticStatusCodes.cs (the 9200-9299 range is reserved for "COM bridge / runtime failures" with only 9201 BridgeUnavailable and 9202 SimulationOnly populated — 9203 is unused and a natural slot). The misattribution is genuine: an in-server NullReferenceException or JsonException becomes a wire envelope that pretends the SDK answered and tells the LLM/operator to look in Event Viewer. After P14-019 redacted rawError to "***", only exceptionType remains as a signal, which the audit correctly identifies. Searched Todo.md and audit-findings.json for all 71 P14 task IDs — P14-019 touched WrapToolHandler only for redaction, P14-022/031 fixed unrelated int.Parse placeholders in the session manager, and no other P14 task re-classifies the catch-Exception fallback's status code or message. Existing test Run_GenericException_FallsThroughToStatusCodeZero in WrapToolHandlerTests.cs:50-72 pins the current (wrong) behavior — that single test needs to update with the fix. OdbcException is already routed via OdbcErrorMapper at call sites that use it, but any OdbcException that escapes (or a bridge ArgumentException, FileNotFoundException, etc.) still hits this fallback. Fully sim-implementable: zero Lacerte/Windows surface, pure C# code + one test rewrite + StatusInfo entry.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Three-file fix, all sim-testable, ~25 LOC + 4 tests: (1) src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/SyntheticStatusCodes.cs — add `public const int InternalServerError = 9203;` in the 9200-9299 block (slot is open after BridgeUnavailable=9201, SimulationOnly=9202) and a StatusTable entry: name "InternalServerError", Severity.Error, userMessage "The MCP server itself raised an unexpected exception — this is not a Lacerte SDK error.", remediation "Capture the exceptionType from context, re-run with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1, and file an issue with the wire log timestamp." Update the file's range-layout XML doc comment to note that 9203 covers in-server faults (distinct from 9201 bridge-process unavailability). (2) src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:67-79 — change the wrapped status from `StatusCodes.Error` to `SyntheticStatusCodes.InternalServerError`. Keep the existing context dict shape (rawError + exceptionType) untouched so P14-019 redaction still applies. Optional but cheap classifier in the same catch: if `ex is System.Data.Odbc.OdbcException`, route via `OdbcErrorMapper.Map(ex)` so SQLSTATE telemetry isn't lost — that path already exists in src/LacertMCP.Server/Odbc/OdbcErrorMapper.cs and converts to proper TAPIStatus codes (DBFNotAccessable/CodeBaseError/NotExposed). Skip the FileNotFoundException → InvalidDataPath mapping from the original recommendation; InvalidDataPath (9013) is specifically about lacerte_set_context payload validation per its docstring, and conflating runtime IO failures into it would create a new misattribution. (3) src/LacertMCP.Tests/Errors/WrapToolHandlerTests.cs:50-72 — rewrite `Run_GenericException_FallsThroughToStatusCodeZero` as `Run_GenericException_WrapsAsInternalServerError`: assert statusCode == 9203, statusName == "InternalServerError", userMessage starts with "The MCP server itself", context.exceptionType contains "InvalidOperationException", context.rawError == "***" (P14-019 still holds). Add 3 more tests: (a) OdbcException → DBFNotAccessable when routed through the new classifier (using OdbcErrorMapper.MapSqlState since the OdbcException ctor is internal — fabricate via SqlStateMapping comparison or inject a stub), (b) NullReferenceException → 9203 (most damaging misattribution), (c) preserve LacerteSDKError passthrough unchanged (regression guard). Update Todo.md adding this as P15-001 (or P14 follow-up), and add a one-line entry to DECISIONS.md noting the semantic split: StatusCodes.Error (0) is reserved for actual SDK code-0 returns; SyntheticStatusCodes.InternalServerError (9203) signals server-side faults so LLM remediation paths don't waste cycles on Event Viewer / SDK trace dead-ends.

title: DBxError remediations (16-23) say "check the table file on disk" but never name the file
description: All eight DBxError entries (DB1Error..DB8Error) share the remediation "Check the table file on disk; run Lacerte's index-repair on the affected module/year." — but the only context the LLM has at this point is the integer code (e.g. 16). The mapping DB1Error=DATA1, DB2Error=DATA2 is documented only as a comment after the userMessage suffix "(DATA1)". The remediation doesn't tell the LLM or operator the filename to repair — they have to know that DATA1+module-char+2-digit-year forms the DBF basename and that the active context.module determines the char. None of the eight throw-sites in the codebase actually emit these codes today (they come from the SDK), so the context dict on raise is empty by default.
recommendation: Two-part: (1) Update the DBxError remediation to include the concrete file path template: "Check ${dataPath}/DATA<N><module><YY>.DBF on disk; run Lacerte File → Repair Indexes for the affected module/year." — formatting via a templated remediation requires either string.Format placeholder substitution at GetStatusInfo time, or the tool-layer code that propagates the SDK code substitutes via context before raising. (2) When LacerteSessionManager catches a DBxError from the bridge, enrich context with {dataPath, module, year, expectedDbf} computed from the active SessionContext so the LLM has the actual filename to suggest the operator open.
rationale: Eight near-identical remediations all telling the operator to "check the file" without naming the file is a useful-on-paper / useless-in-practice pattern. The LLM has the data needed to substitute the path; the wiring just isn't there.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/StatusCodes.cs lines 175-221: the 8 DBxError StatusInfo entries do share an identical generic remediation "Check the table file on disk; run Lacerte's index-repair on the affected module/year." that names no file. The finding is a real, observable property of the code. No Phase-14 task (scanned all 71, P14-001..P14-071) touches DBxError remediations — closest neighbors are P14-031 (pre-TY21 row-num), P14-053 (CreateClient required fields), and P14-061 (EditionDetection caching), none of which overlap. Two factual corrections to the finding's rationale, however: (a) the claim "None of the eight throw-sites in the codebase actually emit these codes today" is wrong — SimulationStore.cs:248-258 has _dbErrorByTable[] and ErrorForTable() that emits DB1Error..DB7Error at lines 335 and 338 inside SimulateFieldWrite for the "row lookup failed" branch (this is the dominant emission path in the off-Windows sim mode this project runs in by default). (b) Because the sim emits these for "row not found", the remediation "check disk / repair indexes" is doubly misleading there — it's not a file-on-disk problem at all, it's a missing row. The right fix is sharper than the original recommendation: (1) Split the semantics: SimulationStore should throw a "RowNotFound"-style synthetic status (or reuse OutOfIndex=4) with context {table, clientNumber, subClientID?, stateAbbrev?} when the row isn't found, NOT DBxError. Reserve DBxError for the live-bridge path where it actually comes from the SDK on a real DBF I/O failure. (2) For the live path, enrich context at the bridge catch site in LacerteSessionManager/Writer/Reader with {dataPath, module, year, expectedDbf=DATA<N><M><YY>.DBF} so the existing WrapToolHandler context echo gives the LLM the filename to repair. (3) Either rewrite the remediation to be useful when context IS present ("Check ${expectedDbf} under ${dataPath}; run Lacerte File → Repair Indexes for ${moduleName} ${year}.") via a templated substitution at GetStatusInfo time, or leave the string generic and rely on the context dict + WrapToolHandler serialization to surface the file. Useful: medium — the LLM-facing remediation is currently un-actionable for these 8 codes, and the wires are cheap. Actionable: yes, sim-only (string edits + sim throw-site refactor + context enrichment helper, all under net48 + xunit).
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Three-part fix, all sim-only: (1) Stop conflating "row not found" with "DBF disk error" in the sim path — in SimulationStore.cs:335,338, replace `ErrorForTable(table)` with `throw new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.OutOfIndex, new Dictionary<string,object?>{["op"]="WriteField",["table"]=table,["clientNumber"]=clientNumber,["subClientID"]=subId,["stateAbbrev"]=state,["reason"]="Row not found for the given identifiers"})`. OutOfIndex (TAPIStatus 4) is the spec-correct code for this and already has remediation guidance. Reserve DB1Error..DB8Error for the live bridge path where the SDK itself returns them on a real DBF I/O failure. (2) When the live bridge actually surfaces a DBxError from the SDK (Writer.cs / Reader.cs / LacerteSessionManager), enrich the LacerteSDKError context dict with `{dataPath=ctx.DataPath, module=ctx.Module, year=ctx.Year, expectedDbf=$"DATA{N}{ctx.Module}{ctx.Year%100:D2}.DBF", moduleName=Modules.GetByChar(ctx.Module)?.Name}` so the WrapToolHandler-serialized context tells the LLM exactly which file to name to the operator. The substitution belongs at the throw site (operator's session knows N from the table arg), not in StatusInfo templating — keeps StatusCodes.cs pure. (3) Update each of the 8 DBxError remediation strings in StatusCodes.cs:175-221 to point at the expectedDbf key the live path now populates: "If context.expectedDbf is set, check that file under context.dataPath; run Lacerte File → Repair Indexes for the affected module/year. If expectedDbf is empty, this is a sim 'row not found' that should not normally surface as DBxError — file an issue." Tests: SimulationStoreTests.cs:328 (which the grep showed already references DB1Error) will need updating to assert OutOfIndex + the new context keys; add a parity test that pins the new sim contract.

title: Synthetic vs SDK code distinction is buried in source comments, never documented for LLM consumers
description: The wire envelope returns `statusCode` as a bare integer with no marker for whether it came from the SDK (0-204 range) or was minted by MCP (9001-9202 range). The distinction matters because: SDK codes can be looked up in Intuit documentation, synthetic codes cannot. SDK codes signal real Lacerte-side state, synthetic signals pre-flight rejection that the LLM may be able to fix without re-talking to Lacerte. Today the only way the LLM disambiguates is by knowing 9xxx is synthetic — and that convention is in a code comment, not in the tool descriptions, not in README.md, not in the error envelope itself.
recommendation: Add a `"origin": "sdk" | "synthetic"` field to WrapToolHandler.SerializeError's envelope (derive from StatusCode >= 9000). Document the convention in README.md's "Errors" section. Update DECISIONS.md with a short "Why both number-ranges exist" entry. Consider exposing a tool `lacerte_explain_status_code(code)` that returns the StatusInfo for any code without going through a real operation — cheap LLM self-help.
rationale: An LLM seeing `statusCode: 9202 SimulationOnly` will react differently than `statusCode: 14 TaxModuleMismatch` — the first means "flip a server config flag", the second means "call set_context with the right ReturnType". Without a documented origin marker, the LLM either has to memorize ranges or treat both classes identically (which defeats the synthetic-code design).

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct read of src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs (lines 82-95) and SyntheticStatusCodes.cs. The SerializeError envelope is fixed at {success, statusCode, statusName, severity, userMessage, remediation, context} with NO origin marker — Phase-14 P14-019 only added WireLog.Redact() over the JSON, didn't touch the field set. README has no Errors section (verified via section list); the only synthetic-vs-SDK reference is one tool-row at line 154 and one troubleshooting line at 245. DECISIONS.md 2026-05-30 documents the range allocation for designers, not the LLM-consumer distinction. So the docs gap and envelope gap are both real and NOT a Phase-14 dupe.

Partially mitigated: MetadataTools.LacerteReturnCodes (line 141, 155) already emits an `origin` field in the catalog with values TAPIStatus/TPSDKStatus/Synthetic — so an LLM can resolve any code by calling that tool. This makes the proposed lacerte_explain_status_code(code) tool redundant and that part of the recommendation should be dropped. The remaining real wins: (a) add `origin` to the error envelope so the LLM doesn't have to round-trip through the catalog mid-failure, and (b) document the convention in README + DECISIONS.

Also: StatusName itself is partial signal (e.g. "SimulationOnly" vs "TaxModuleMismatch") but not normalized — many SDK codes have terse names ("DBError") whose origin isn't obvious. An explicit one-token `origin` field beats name-pattern matching.

Actionable off-Windows: pure C# + 2 markdown edits, fully unit-testable (assert envelope JSON contains "origin":"synthetic" when StatusCode>=9000, "sdk" otherwise). ~15 LOC + 3 tests + 2 doc edits.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-part fix, all sim-only, ~30 minutes:

(1) src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:82-95 — add one field to the SerializeError envelope after `statusName`: `["origin"] = err.StatusCode >= 9000 ? "synthetic" : "sdk",`. Derivation lives at the serialization boundary (not on LacerteSDKError itself) so the existing ~25 throw-sites and constructors stay untouched. Test in src/LacertMCP.Tests/Errors/ (new file or extend WrapToolHandlerTests if it exists): (a) throw LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.SimulationOnly) → envelope.origin=="synthetic"; (b) throw LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.ExposedForRead /*8*/) → envelope.origin=="sdk"; (c) generic Exception wrapper at line 67-79 wraps with code 0 (StatusCodes.Error) → envelope.origin=="sdk" (since 0 < 9000).

(2) README.md — add a new `## Errors` subsection after `## Prompts` (line 156-167 area) before `## CLI`. ~15 lines: "All tool errors return `{success:false, statusCode, statusName, severity, userMessage, remediation, context, origin}`. The `origin` field is either `"sdk"` (codes 0-204, real Lacerte SDK TAPIStatus/TPSDKStatus state — look up the code in Intuit's SDK documentation; remediation is operator-side) or `"synthetic"` (codes 9001-9299, minted by this MCP before any SDK call — pre-flight validation, auth gate, or bridge runtime; remediation is usually MCP-side config). Call `lacerte_return_codes` for the full code catalog with names + remediation." Link to DECISIONS.md "Synthetic statusCode range" 2026-05-30.

(3) DECISIONS.md — append a short "Why the wire envelope carries `origin`" paragraph under the existing "Synthetic statusCode range" 2026-05-30 entry (don't make a new dated entry — same decision lineage). Two sentences: "The 9000+ numeric threshold is a load-bearing convention, so we surface it explicitly in the envelope rather than asking LLM consumers to memorize the range. Derived at SerializeError time (not on LacerteSDKError itself) so existing throw-sites need no change."

SKIP the originally-proposed `lacerte_explain_status_code(code)` tool — the existing `lacerte_return_codes` tool (MetadataTools.cs:121-165) already returns the full StatusInfo catalog including an `origin` discriminator, so a per-code tool would be redundant. Mention `lacerte_return_codes` in the new README Errors section so consumers know it exists.

title: Tax-organizer / CSV-intake flow has no helper; LLM rebuilds mapping per row
description: REQUIREMENTS §1.3 names "Bootstrapping new clients from a CSV or Tax Organizer responses" as a primary operator flow. The only support is the `lacerte_client_intake` prompt, which is single-client (no CSV iteration), and the `lacerte_client_create` tool, which takes ONLY the minimum-required {clientID, taxType, firstName, lastName, emailID} — every other field (address, SSN, DOB, dependents, W-2 totals) must be wired one at a time via separate `lacerte_field_write` and `lacerte_detail_write` calls with no canonical mapping from common CSV column names → Lacerte field codes. The model has to relearn the mapping ("address line 1 = C1_?", "DOB = C1_?", "first dependent's name = which Series in detail?") per session and per row, and there's no metadata tool that returns "the canonical address+demographic field set for module I". CSV intake is the most common new-client workflow at tax-prep firms and is essentially DIY today.
recommendation: Two concrete additions: (1) extend `lacerte_client_create` with a `seedFields: Dictionary<string,object>` optional param so a single tool call creates the row AND seeds the basic address/demographic fields atomically (one idempotency key covers both). (2) Add a `lacerte_field_codes` metadata tool (or extend `lacerte_field_access_map`) that returns a human-friendly map `{ "firstName": "C1_1", "lastName": "C1_2", "email": "C1_3", "addressLine1": "C1_?", "city": "C1_?", ... }` for the active module. Doc the canonical Tax-Organizer column-name → Lacerte-field mapping in `WorkflowPrompts.ClientIntake` so the LLM doesn't have to introspect per row. Optional but high-impact: a `lacerte_client_create_batch(rows[], idempotencyKeyPrefix)` that loops, mirroring the bulk-write proposal in finding 1.
rationale: Without the mapping helper, CSV-to-Lacerte costs the LLM dozens of `field_access_map` probes per row and is fragile to schema variants between modules. The named flow is fundamentally unergonomic at scale.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed real and uncovered by Phase 14. REQUIREMENTS.md line 13 verbatim names "Bootstrapping new clients from a CSV or an upstream system (Tax Organizer responses)" as a primary operator flow — yet (a) `lacerte_client_create` (CreateClientTools.cs:50-225) accepts only the 5-field minimum set and exposes no `seedFields` param, (b) no `lacerte_client_create_batch` exists, (c) `WorkflowPrompts.ClientIntake` (lines 42-93) explicitly walks a single client only — Step 4's only guidance is "C1_1 (first name), C1_2 (last name), C1_3 (email). Use `lacerte_field_access_map` if unsure", with NO canonical CSV-column → Lacerte-field map, and (d) `lacerte_field_access_map` (MetadataTools.cs) returns only access enums (ReadOnly/ReadWrite) keyed by raw field codes like C1_5, not human-friendly aliases — and the comment at MetadataTools.cs:69-71 admits the base JSON shards are "mostly {} pending the introspection follow-up F5", so even the access map is sparse today.

Phase-14 scan: P14-053 made the existing 5 fields required (orthogonal — doesn't add seeding). No P14 task covers CSV intake, batch creation, seedFields, or canonical column mapping. Grep of audit-findings.json for CSV/batch/seedField/canonical-mapping returns zero matches in this domain. So the finding is genuinely new.

Actionability: (1) seedFields param is fully sim-implementable — wrap CreateClient + N WriteField calls inside a single idempotency body in LacerteSessionManager. (2) `lacerte_client_create_batch` is fully sim-implementable (loop with shared idempotencyKeyPrefix). (3) Doc canonical mapping in WorkflowPrompts is pure docs. (4) The `lacerte_field_codes` human-alias map has a constraint the finding glosses: the underlying field-access shards are empty pending live introspection (F5). The well-documented C1_1/C1_2/C1_3 (name + email) and a handful of address fields from Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md §4 ARE knowable off-Windows, but a full demographic map is gated on F5. So the recommendation for (2) should ship a curated, spec-sourced starter alias map that documents its provenance + gaps rather than promising a complete one.

Usefulness: REQUIREMENTS §1.3 names this flow as one of five top-level operator capabilities and ARCHITECTURE/HANDOFF/Todo.md offer no support for it. Today every row costs 1 CreateClient + dozens of FieldWrite + an unknown number of field_access_map probes, with no canonical column name → field code translation — fragile across modules and across sessions. Closing this gap unblocks the named flow at meaningful cost-savings to the LLM. Not bikeshedding.

Confidence high — direct file reads of all cited files plus REQUIREMENTS.md, MetadataTools.cs, and the FieldAccessMap base shards confirm every premise.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three landed, scoped changes — all sim-doable, no Lacerte/Windows needed; defer the live-introspection-dependent piece behind F5.

(1) **Add `seedFields` to `lacerte_client_create`** — extend CreateClientTools.LacerteClientCreate with `Dictionary<string,string>? seedFields = null`. On success, after the CreateClient call returns the new ClientNumber, the tool loops the dictionary and calls WriteField for each (table=1, key=clientNumber, field=k, value=v). Wrap CreateClient + the seed-writes inside ONE call to `LacerteSessionManager.ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock(idempotencyKey, payload, body)` so a single key covers the whole atomic unit per the existing idempotency contract. On any seed-write failure, throw with a structured error that names {clientNumber, failedField, partialSeedCount}; do NOT attempt rollback of the CreateClient (the sim store has no transaction; the live SDK doesn't either) — the operator can retry with the same idempotencyKey and the cached partial state will be surfaced. Add tests in CreateClientToolsTests covering: empty dict (no-op), 3-field happy path, mid-loop failure surfaces structured error, idempotency replay returns cached result. Touch: CreateClientTools.cs, LacerteSessionManager.cs (small payload-shape extension), SimulationStore.cs (none needed — calls already route through WriteField), CreateClientToolsTests.cs.

(2) **Add `lacerte_client_create_batch(rows[], idempotencyKeyPrefix)`** — new tool on CreateClientTools (or a new BatchTools class). Accepts a `List<CreateRowArgs>` where each row carries `{clientID, taxType, firstName, lastName, emailID, seedFields?}`. Loops rows; per row builds idempotencyKey = `{idempotencyKeyPrefix}-{clientID}` and calls the existing seeded-create path from (1). Stop-on-first-error by default with `{continueOnError: bool = false}` escape hatch that collects per-row results instead of throwing. Mirror the bulk-write-prompt's structured response shape: `{requested, created, skippedDuplicate, failed, details[]}`. Tests cover: 3-row happy path, mid-batch DuplicateClient surfaces stop, continueOnError=true returns per-row report. Touch: CreateClientTools.cs (or new BatchTools.cs), CreateClientToolsTests.cs.

(3) **Document the canonical Tax-Organizer column → Lacerte-field mapping** — add a new section to WorkflowPrompts.ClientIntake (Step 4 expansion) AND a `## CSV intake → Lacerte field mapping` subsection in README.md citing what is canonical today. Concretely list the spec-sourced module-I fields confirmed in Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md §4 (firstName=C1_1, lastName=C1_2, emailID=C1_3 — already used in the prompt today). Mark every other commonly-asked field (addressLine1, city, state, zip, DOB, SSN, homePhone) as "field code to be confirmed via FieldAccessDumper run on Windows (gated on F5)" — DO NOT invent codes that aren't in the spec. Add a new prompt `lacerte_csv_intake(columnMap: dict)` whose body walks: validate session/context → enumerate rows → for each row call lacerte_client_create with seedFields → report per-row outcomes. title: FullFlowTests covers only happy-path single-client; bulk/CSV/EF-poll flows untested
description: The integration directory contains ONE test class (FullFlowTests.cs) with ONE method that exercises Register→SetContext→ListClients→ReadClient→Write(failing)→CreateClient→re-list. Four of the five named operator flows in REQUIREMENTS have no end-to-end coverage: (1) bulk-update across many clients, (2) CSV → CreateClient bootstrapping (multi-row create loop), (3) EF status review (no test calls `ReadEFStatus` end-to-end, asserts the join shape, then drills into specific buckets), (4) detail-row review (no test calls `ReadDetail` and asserts the operator can find a W-2 row by Series). Even the one test that exists asserts a failing write (UnknownFieldAccess) rather than the happy path. The integration layer therefore proves the plumbing compiles but does not prove the operator's workflows actually compose.
recommendation: Add four sibling files: `FullFlow_BulkUpdate.cs`, `FullFlow_CsvIntake.cs`, `FullFlow_EfStatusReview.cs`, `FullFlow_DetailReview.cs`. Each scripts the prompt's documented happy path end-to-end against the sim store, asserts the final visible state from a read-back, and runs in both sim and live modes via the same `ParitySessionFactory.For(mode)` pattern as the parity tests. These are the highest-leverage tests in the suite: they fail loudly when any tool's response shape drifts or any cross-tool data-flow assumption breaks (e.g. ClientNumber casing between list output and read input).
rationale: The CLAUDE.md operating system says "works flawlessly on the operator's box" is the bar. With four of five named flows untested at the integration layer, regressions in any cross-tool boundary will only surface in the operator's first real session.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed real: src/LacertMCP.Tests/Integration/ contains exactly one file (FullFlowTests.cs) with one [Fact] method that scripts a single happy-path single-client sequence. REQUIREMENTS.md lines 11-15 names five operator flows; only flow #1 (read clients) has integration coverage. EFileToolsTests.cs is a 2-method tool-shape probe (not a flow), DetailsToolsTests touches a single read, and there is no end-to-end test composing ReadClient -> WriteField (happy path) -> re-read across many rows, no CSV->CreateClient loop, no ReadEFStatus drill-into-bucket, no Detail W-2-row-by-Series lookup. Confirmed actionable: the existing test already runs sim-only off-Windows using SeedData.DataPathIData2024; ParitySessionFactory.For(mode) exists at src/LacertMCP.Tests/Parity/BothModes.cs:36 (live leg auto-skips off-Windows), so the both-modes claim is accurate. Confirmed useful: these flows are exactly where Phase-14 touched cross-tool plumbing without integration proof — P14-022 (EFStatus SQL projection columns), P14-055 (Detail Series numeric-string), P14-005 (idempotency lock helper around bulk writes), P14-019 (sim CreateClient gate parity around CSV bootstrapping). A regression in any of these will land first in the operator's session because nothing composes them today. Confirmed not a duplicate: Phase-14 task #84 was the ORIGINAL creation of FullFlowTests.cs; grep of audit-findings.json for bulk/csv/FullFlow/integration/BulkUpdate/CsvIntake/EfStatusReview/DetailReview returns no Phase-14 task proposing additional integration files. P14-022, P14-055, P14-019 fixed the underlying contracts but added unit/tool-level tests, not integration-flow tests.

All four should use ParitySessionFactory.For(mode) + [Theory][BothModesData] like Parity/RoundTripTests does, so the live leg auto-skips today but flips on once the Windows operator box exists.
