title: No request/correlation ID threads through WireLog records
description: Every WireLog record carries `{ ts, op, args, durationMs, result|error }` but no correlation field. A single MCP tool call like `lacerte_write_field` produces a NESTED stack of log lines: outer `WriteField` (line 689), inner `CanUseNewApis` it triggers (line 432), the AutoReconnect retries on the live path (currently silent — see finding #1), and any sub-ops in the bridge. When the operator opens `lacerte-20260530.log` with two concurrent tools running, there is no way to group these lines back to one logical request. The MCP transport itself receives a JSON-RPC request ID per tool call (the SDK has it); WireLog never sees it. Without a correlation column, multi-line forensics ("what wire calls did request 42 actually make?") requires guessing by interleaving timestamps. On Windows where the stdio MCP could face message-pump interleaving across two concurrent tools, this is materially harder than on a strict request/response transport.
recommendation: Add an optional `correlationId` to `WireLog.Record<T>(string op, object? args, Func<Task<T>> work, string? correlationId = null)`. Stamp it on the JSON line as `"cid"`. In `WrapToolHandler.Run`, generate a short cid (e.g. `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N").Substring(0,8)`) at handler entry and propagate it via an `AsyncLocal<string?>` so nested calls (CanUseNewApis, AutoReconnect.retry once finding #1 lands, ReadTableCore) inherit it. Cost: ~10 bytes per record, zero behavioral change, full backtrace recovery. Also include cid in the structured error envelope so the LLM client can echo it back when reporting a failure.
rationale: When a 2 AM Friday call comes in saying "tool X failed at roughly 14:32" you need to be able to grep one ID and see the full causal chain. Plain timestamps don't cut it for interleaved async.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading WireLog.cs lines 398-410 (WriteRecord dict) and WrapToolHandler.cs: the record dictionary has exactly {ts, op, args, durationMs, result|error} — no correlation field. Greppped src/ for correlation|correlationId|cid|requestId|traceId|AsyncLocal — only one hit, an unrelated comment in LacerteSessionManager.cs:65. Greppped audit-findings.json, Todo.md, and HANDOFF.md for the same keywords — no Phase-14 task addresses request correlation. Confirmed the nested-emit claim: a single lacerte_write_field tool call routes through WrapToolHandler.Run (no record) -> LacerteSessionManager.WriteField (would emit a session-level WireLog.Record if instrumented) -> LacerteSessionManager.CanUseNewApis (emits WireLog at line 432) -> Bridge.CanUseNewApis (line 95) -> Bridge.WriteField (line 169) -> potentially WireLog.RecordSync inside Writer.WriteToDBFDatabase. That's up to 4 records per single tool call, plus any ODBC.Query records that interleave with another concurrent tool's records. With no cid, multi-line forensics requires guesswork by timestamp interleaving. The proposed fix (AsyncLocal<string?> set at WrapToolHandler entry, threaded through WireLog.WriteRecord, stamped as a "cid" field) is small, non-behavioral, fully sim-implementable with no Windows/Lacerte dependency, and tests can assert it by reading the temp log file (test infra already exists via EnableForTests/FlushForTests). One minor tightening: the recommendation's "MCP SDK has the JSON-RPC request ID" angle is shakier — ModelContextProtocol 0.3.0-preview.4 may or may not expose it on a usable seam, so the safe, in-scope move is to generate the cid locally at WrapToolHandler entry. Including cid in the error envelope (so the LLM client can echo it in bug reports) is a real bonus.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add request-scoped correlation IDs in two coordinated changes: (1) WireLog.cs — add `public static AsyncLocal<string?> CurrentCorrelationId = new AsyncLocal<string?>();` (or a small `WireLogScope` class). In `WriteRecord`, after the `["durationMs"]` line, do `var cid = CurrentCorrelationId.Value; if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(cid)) record["cid"] = cid;` so the field appears only when set (keeps disabled-path cost zero and existing JSON shape unchanged when no scope is active). (2) WrapToolHandler.Run — at entry, generate `var cid = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N").Substring(0,8);` set `WireLog.CurrentCorrelationId.Value = cid;` and include `["cid"] = cid` in both the success envelope and SerializeError envelope so the LLM client can echo it in failure reports. Use a try/finally to clear the AsyncLocal slot at scope end (defensive against handler exceptions on threadpool reuse). Do NOT try to thread the JSON-RPC request ID from ModelContextProtocol 0.3.0-preview.4 — the SDK seam isn't guaranteed and a locally-generated 8-char Guid suffix is sufficient for grep-by-id forensics. Tests (off-Windows): (a) WireLogTests — call WireLog.Record from inside a scope and assert the written JSON line contains the expected `"cid":"..."` token; (b) WireLogTests — call WireLog.Record outside any scope and assert the line has NO `cid` key; (c) WrapToolHandlerTests — assert both the success and error envelopes carry a `cid` field with an 8-hex shape and that the same cid value appears in the log file lines emitted during the handler body; (d) concurrency test — two parallel WrapToolHandler.Run invocations each emit nested WireLog records, then assert each tool's records share their own cid and the cids differ across the two tools. Total cost ~25 LOC + ~80 LOC tests, zero behavioral change to wire path, full multi-line forensic recovery.

title: Stderr logging is set to Trace — production wire shows verbose framework chatter
description: `Program.cs` clears all logging providers, then adds a console provider with `options.LogToStandardErrorThreshold = LogLevel.Trace`. This means EVERY Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting / ASP.NET-pipeline / MCP-SDK internal log line at Trace level or above hits the operator's stderr. The MCP SDK preview-4 emits per-request framing trace logs; the Hosting subsystem emits per-DI-resolve trace lines on startup. For an MCP server whose only real signal channel is stderr (stdout is the JSON-RPC wire), drowning the operator in framework Trace noise means they will tune the entire stream out and miss the AutoReconnect warnings (finding #1) and the rotation warnings (finding #2) when they DO start firing. The intent here was probably "don't suppress anything," but `LogToStandardErrorThreshold = Trace` is the wrong knob — it just controls which-level-routes-to-stderr-vs-stdout. The actual `MinimumLevel` is still the host default (Information). The result is harmless today only because the framework happens not to emit floods of Trace; the moment SDK 1.x lands with debug telemetry, the change in noise floor will surprise.
recommendation: Switch to explicit level config: `builder.Logging.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Information)` and let `LogToStandardErrorThreshold = LogLevel.Information` (so everything that survives the filter routes to stderr, never stdout — that part is correct). Add an env var `LACERTE_LOG_LEVEL` (Trace|Debug|Information|Warning|Error) so a debugging session can opt into verbose without code change. Document the env var in README's env-var matrix. The current setup will get noisy the moment the MCP SDK matures, with no operator-side knob to dial it back.
rationale: The signal-to-noise ratio on the only real telemetry channel matters. Trace-by-default plus no explicit MinimumLevel is a future regression waiting for the next SDK bump.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the cited file at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Program.cs lines 23-27: builder.Logging.ClearProviders() + AddConsole with LogToStandardErrorThreshold = LogLevel.Trace, and NO explicit SetMinimumLevel call. The finding's read of the API is correct — LogToStandardErrorThreshold is a routing knob (which-level-goes-to-stderr-vs-stdout), and setting it to Trace means "everything routes to stderr," which is actually the CORRECT routing for an MCP stdio server where stdout is the JSON-RPC wire. So the loud-sounding "stderr logging is set to Trace" framing is misleading — operators don't see Trace today because MinimumLevel filters first, and that defaults to Information via Host.CreateApplicationBuilder. The real, narrower issues underneath are: (1) no explicit MinimumLevel — relies on host default (no appsettings.json ships, so the implicit Information is benign today but invisible to readers); (2) no operator-side env-var to toggle verbosity without a rebuild — confirmed by grep of README.md env-var matrix (lines 87-102) which lists LACERTE_LIVE/SIMULATION/DATA_PATH/DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR/APP_NAME/APP_ID/DEBUG_WIRE/DEBUG_LOG_PATH/SIM_EXPIRED/DATA_ROOT/MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE/PARITY_RECORDING — no LACERTE_LOG_LEVEL. Cross-checked audit-findings.json and Todo.md Phase 14: P14-012 / P14-018 / P14-019 / P14-037 / P14-057 / P14-067 all touch the custom WireLog subsystem, not the Microsoft.Extensions.Logging pipeline in Program.cs. No Phase-14 task touched Program.cs logging. Confidence is medium not high because the "this will explode when SDK 1.x lands" is speculative — today's behavior is fine and the change is a small hygiene + DX win rather than a bug fix.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In src/LacertMCP.Server/Program.cs, replace the AddConsole block (lines 23-27) with: (a) read LACERTE_LOG_LEVEL env var once, parse to LogLevel via Enum.TryParse (case-insensitive); default to LogLevel.Information when unset / unparseable; (b) builder.Logging.SetMinimumLevel(parsed); (c) keep AddConsole with options.LogToStandardErrorThreshold = LogLevel.Trace — that is the CORRECT routing for an MCP stdio server (every surviving log line goes to stderr, never stdout) and the finding's suggestion to change it to Information would actually break this guarantee for sub-Information levels (Debug/Trace would route to stdout and corrupt the JSON-RPC wire). Keep stderr-routes-everything; the MinimumLevel is the operator knob, not LogToStandardErrorThreshold. Add the env var to README's env-var matrix table with values "Trace|Debug|Information|Warning|Error|Critical|None" (default Information) and a one-liner noting it tunes the host/SDK log floor only — LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE is independent. Add one unit test in LacertMCP.Tests verifying Enum.TryParse handles a known-good and known-bad value (the bind happens in a static helper extractable from Program.cs).

title: No liveness/readiness check — an external watcher can't tell if MCP is alive
description: `LacerteHealth` is the only health surface and it's an MCP-tool — invokable ONLY through the MCP JSON-RPC stdio transport. To call it, a watcher must implement the MCP client handshake (initialize → list_tools → call_tool → parse envelope). No external process supervisor (Windows Task Scheduler, NSSM, an operator's `task list` script, a sidecar log-tail script) has a way to ask "is the server process alive AND has it completed the 24h Intuit auth?" without writing a full MCP client. The Lacerte 24h auth window is the single most operationally critical state — the operator MUST re-register before it expires or all writes fail at 9009. Today they have to manually run `lacerte-mcp status` (CLI subcommand spawns a separate process, separate manager → can't see the live server's auth state at all — its `IsRegistered` is its own). There's no signal file, no PID file with last-heartbeat-mtime, no `--health` flag on the server exe, no UDP heartbeat, no `MinutesUntilExpiry` exposed on disk.
recommendation: Add a heartbeat-file mechanism: when WireLog is enabled, also touch `{LogDir}/.heartbeat` every N seconds (or on every tool call) with mtime = now and contents = `{pid, mode, isRegistered, minutesUntilExpiry, buildVersion}`. A watcher script can `Get-Item .heartbeat | %{ $_.LastWriteTime }` to detect staleness and `Get-Content .heartbeat | ConvertFrom-Json` to read auth state. Zero new dependencies, zero new ports, zero change to MCP semantics. Document in README. This closes the "operator runs the server in the background and never knows the auth quietly expired 6 hours ago" failure mode that today requires noticing 9009 errors after the fact.
rationale: The operator runs this unattended; the single most important state (24h auth countdown) is invisible to anything that isn't an MCP client. A 200-byte file solves it.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading HealthTools.cs (lines 30-41 — confirmed it's an MCP-tool surface only, status is a hardcoded constant), StatusCommand.cs (lines 40-70 — confirmed the CLI's status is a separate-process view of disk state only; it reports `registered = appId.HasValue` but never consults the live server's in-memory ExpiresAt/MinutesUntilExpiry), LacerteSessionManager.cs (lines 74-293 — confirmed RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt/MinutesUntilExpiry live only in the running server's process memory and are exposed only through the MCP `lacerte_session` tool), and grepping for heartbeat/.heartbeat/liveness/readiness/signal-file/pid-file/watcher across src/, Todo.md (P14-001..071), audit-findings.json, and HANDOFF.md — zero hits. Phase 14 had no observability-category fix; the 10 prior-audit categories explicitly listed don't include observability. P14-001 (LacerteHealth WrapToolHandler envelope) and P14-040 (buildVersion stamp in status) are adjacent but don't close the gap: the running server's auth countdown is invisible to any external supervisor that isn't a full MCP client. The finding's claim that `lacerte-mcp status` can't see the live server's auth state is confirmed — it reads AppIdStore directly, a separate-process snapshot. Off-Windows actionable: a heartbeat-file writer + sim tests + README doc need zero Lacerte/Windows. The fix is small (~80 LOC + tests) and high-leverage because the 24h auth expiry is the single operationally critical state per CLAUDE.md.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add an unconditional (not WireLog-gated) heartbeat-file writer in `LacerteSessionManager`. Concrete plan, all off-Windows actionable: (1) Add `src/LacertMCP.Server/Diagnostics/HeartbeatWriter.cs` — a small class started by `LacerteSessionManager` ctor that writes `{HeartbeatDir}/.heartbeat` (single canonical path, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%/LacertMCP/.heartbeat` on Windows, `~/.local/share/LacertMCP/.heartbeat` elsewhere; override with `LACERTE_HEARTBEAT_DIR`; disable with `LACERTE_HEARTBEAT=0`). File contents = single-line JSON `{pid, mode, isRegistered, registeredAt, expiresAt, minutesUntilExpiry, lastToolCallUtc, buildVersion}` written atomically (write to `.heartbeat.tmp` then `File.Replace`). (2) Trigger: a 30-second `System.Threading.Timer` (idle keepalive) PLUS a hook in `WrapToolHandler.Run` finally-block (so the file mtime jumps on every tool call — easy "is anyone home" signal for a watcher). Both call the same `HeartbeatWriter.Touch(snapshot)` method; the writer dedupes so back-to-back calls within ~500ms don't thrash the disk. (3) Pass the existing `SessionStatusSnapshot` directly — no new state plumbing. (4) Sim tests in `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Diagnostics/HeartbeatWriterTests.cs`: assert (a) file is created on Touch, (b) JSON parses to expected shape, (c) mtime advances on subsequent Touch ≥1s later, (d) honors `LACERTE_HEARTBEAT=0` opt-out, (e) honors `LACERTE_HEARTBEAT_DIR` override, (f) atomic write doesn't leave `.tmp` behind, (g) writer doesn't throw if the dir is read-only (operator must never see an MCP error because heartbeat IO failed — wrap in try/catch, log to wire log if enabled, swallow). (5) README: new "Operator monitoring" subsection with a 6-line PowerShell snippet showing `Get-Item .heartbeat` (mtime staleness) and `Get-Content .heartbeat | ConvertFrom-Json` (auth countdown) — single example, no NSSM/Task-Scheduler boilerplate. (6) Drop the "tie to WireLog" coupling from the original recommendation — heartbeat is independent observability and should not require enabling debug logging to function. (7) Out of scope and explicitly NOT in this fix: a `--health` exe flag, UDP/named-pipe heartbeat, Windows service registration — the file approach is sufficient for a single-operator tool and stays zero-dependency.

title: Idempotency lock map (_idempotencyLocks) is genuinely unbounded; only the cache evicts
description: P14-005 added per-key SemaphoreSlim serialization via ExecuteWithIdempotencyLock, and P14-013/P14-064 added a 10k-entry + 24h-TTL eviction policy to _idempotencyCache. But the eviction logic in StoreIdempotent (lines 1374-1395) only prunes _idempotencyCache — it never touches _idempotencyLocks. Every unique idempotencyKey ever seen contributes one permanent SemaphoreSlim entry to the lock dictionary. With LacerteSessionManager being a process-lifetime singleton (per CLAUDE.md), a long-running MCP session that processes (say) 50k unique idempotent writes over a week leaves 50k SemaphoreSlims pinned in memory, all GC-rooted via the static-ish dictionary, even though _idempotencyCache itself stayed at 10k. The HANDOFF.md note "cheap to leak (one SemaphoreSlim per unique key)" assumes a short-lived session — this is an MCP stdio server that runs for the operator's full session. The P14-005 refinedRecommendation specifically suggested "or add a periodic compaction tied to session lifetime"; neither happened.
recommendation: When StoreIdempotent evicts an entry from _idempotencyCache (either expired or oldest-when-over-cap), also TryRemove the matching key from _idempotencyLocks and Dispose the semaphore. Guard against the race where another thread is currently holding the lock: only remove if `sem.CurrentCount == 1` (no one waiting AND no one holding) at the moment of eviction; otherwise let the next eviction cycle catch it. Add a test that creates 100 unique idempotency keys, forces eviction, and asserts _idempotencyLocks count is bounded.
rationale: Phase-14 audit P14-013 and P14-064 explicitly closed cache leaks, but missed the parallel lock-map leak created by P14-005. The fix is asymmetric: cache bounded, locks unbounded. Easy to fix in-session.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by direct read of LacerteSessionManager.cs. _idempotencyLocks (line 105-106) is a ConcurrentDictionary populated via GetOrAdd at line 1324 with no removal path anywhere except Dispose() at line 1465 (process exit). The eviction logic in StoreIdempotent (lines 1374-1395) operates only on _idempotencyCache and never touches _idempotencyLocks. This is the exact asymmetry described: cache is bounded at 10k entries with 24h TTL, locks grow forever. Grepping audit-findings.json confirms no Phase-14 task addresses lock-map eviction — P14-005 explicitly chose to leak ("cheap to leak ... or add a periodic compaction tied to session lifetime") and the compaction half was never delivered; P14-013/P14-064 only covered the cache. No existing test exercises lock-map bounds. The fix is fully sim-actionable: ~10 lines in StoreIdempotent + an xUnit test that creates 100 unique keys, triggers eviction, and asserts _idempotencyLocks.Count is bounded (needs internal-visible-to-test exposure of the field count, or a debug accessor). Severity caveat: for a single-operator MCP tool (CLAUDE.md), 50k unique keys/week is implausible; SemaphoreSlim is ~80-100 bytes + key string ~50 bytes; realistic leak is single-digit MB over months. But the asymmetry is a real code-quality defect — the cache has rigorous bounded-memory invariants that the lock map silently violates, and the fix is one block in StoreIdempotent. Worth landing as a follow-up to P14-005/013/064.

title: EFStatus sim/live divergence: SQL uses LEFT OUTER JOIN, sim uses INNER JOIN
description: P14-053 rewrote SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin to use `left outer join [EFilings] ... left outer join [EFStatuses]` so live results include clients with no eFiling rows (with null EFId/Status). But the sim path in LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus (lines 604-615) is `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId` — a LINQ INNER join that EXCLUDES clients without eFilings AND EXCLUDES eFilings without statuses. Net effect when Phase 9 wires live: sim returns N rows, live returns N+K rows (K = clients with no eFilings yet) — the exact "two-mode discipline observationally identical for the happy path" invariant the audit was closing. The audit verdict for P14-053 caught the column projection drift but not the JOIN-type drift. SqlTemplatesTests verify column names but not JOIN semantics; no parity test seeds a client without eFilings.
recommendation: Rewrite the sim's ReadEFStatus to be a LEFT OUTER JOIN (LINQ's `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId into gj from s in gj.DefaultIfEmpty() select ...`) AND to start from `module.Clients` (so clients without eFilings also appear, matching the SQL's `from ci ... left outer join ef ...` shape). When the join misses, emit nulls for EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId/Status/StatusDate. Add a parity test that seeds (a) one client with eFiling+status, (b) one client with eFiling but no status, (c) one client with no eFiling — assert all three appear in the result with the right null fields.
rationale: P14-053 fixed the column-projection half but introduced/left a JOIN-semantics divergence. The CLAUDE.md "observationally identical" invariant is exactly the thing this audit promised to enforce; the silent miss will only surface on a real Lacerte box (after Phase 9), too late to catch cheaply.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED. Direct code reading of LacerteSessionManager.cs:604-615 shows sim path is `from f in module.EFilings join s in module.EFStatuses on f.Id equals s.EFilingId` — a LINQ inner join starting from EFilings. SqlTemplates.cs:208-213 (post P14-021) is `from [DATA1-Client Info] as ci left outer join [EFilings] as ef on ci.C1_0 = ef.ClientId left outer join [EFStatuses] as s on ef.Id = s.EFilingId` — outer join starting from Clients. The two return DIFFERENT row sets when (a) a client has no EFiling, or (b) an EFiling has no status. Sim drops both; live includes both with NULLs. This is a clean violation of CLAUDE.md's "Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path" invariant — exactly the rule P14-021 was meant to enforce.

DUPLICATE CHECK: P14-021 (the only EFStatus-related Phase-14 task) explicitly addressed *column projection* parity. Its verdict reasoning says "Fix is a pure string edit in a const" — the entire framing was column names. The SqlTemplatesTests P14-021 added (lines 228-235, 246-259) verify column names and join-clause presence, but never assert ROW-SET parity. No Phase-14 task touched the sim's LINQ inner join. The two parity-leg tests for ReadEFStatus run sim-against-itself (the live leg isn't wired), so a divergence cannot be caught today even with parity tests in place. The current seed always creates EFiling+EFStatus together, so even a future round-trip parity test would miss case (c) "client with no EFiling" without an explicit seed.

ACTIONABLE OFF-WINDOWS: yes — pure LINQ rewrite + seed-extension + sim-only assertion. No COM, no ODBC, no Windows.

USEFUL: yes — this is the exact silent-divergence trap the audit was meant to close; will only surface post-Phase-9 on a real Lacerte box, the most expensive place to catch it. Also fixes a latent doc/code mismatch since SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin's xml-doc explicitly cites the parity invariant against ReadEFStatus.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-part fix, all in sim land:

1) `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs` ReadEFStatus (604-615): rewrite to start from `module.Clients.Values` (DATA1) and outer-join EFilings then EFStatuses, so the row set matches the SQL's `from ci left outer join ef left outer join s` shape exactly. Concrete LINQ:
```
var joined = from c in module.Clients.Values
             from f in module.EFilings.Where(x => x.ClientId == (string)c.Fields["C1_0"]).DefaultIfEmpty()
             from s in module.EFStatuses.Where(x => f != null && x.EFilingId == f.Id).DefaultIfEmpty()
             select (IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?>)new Dictionary<string, object?>
             {
                 ["ClientId"]   = c.Fields["C1_0"],
                 ["EFilingId"]  = f?.Id,            // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["EFId"]       = f?.EFId,          // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["InstanceId"] = f?.InstanceId,    // null when client has no eFiling
                 ["Status"]     = s?.Status,        // null when eFiling has no status
                 ["StatusDate"] = s?.StatusDate,    // null when eFiling has no status
             };
```
Key-name ordering should match the SQL SELECT alias order (ClientId, EFilingId, EFId, InstanceId, Status, StatusDate) so the dictionary's insertion-ordered enumeration matches what an ODBC reader would yield.

2) `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/SimulationStore.Seed.cs` (115-128): currently `if (c.EFStatus != null)` seeds BOTH an EFiling and a Status. Extend the seed so at least one fixture client has an EFiling with no status (push an EFiling, skip the EFStatuses add) and at least one has no EFiling at all (the path already exists — any client with `EFStatus == null` qualifies, but verify at least one such Individual + Corp client is present in the canonical TY24 seed). Document the three cases inline so future contractors don't "helpfully" delete them.

3) `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Parity/RoundTripTests.cs` ReadEFStatus_ReturnsRowsWithEfilingId (141-150): split into three assertions — (a) at least one row with non-null EFilingId/Status (full join hit), (b) at least one row with non-null EFilingId but null Status (EFiling-without-Status case), (c) at least one row with the seeded "no-eFiling" client's ClientId and null EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId/Status (client-without-eFiling case). Without (b)+(c) the parity contract is unenforceable.

Do NOT touch SqlTemplates.cs — the post-P14-021 SQL is correct; the bug is sim-side only. Also: while you're in ReadEFStatus, the leading XML doc-comment still says "TY19+ EFilings JOIN EFStatuses" — update it to "DATA1 LEFT OUTER JOIN EFilings LEFT OUTER JOIN EFStatuses" to match the SQL template's docstring style and remove the "INNER JOIN" mental model.

title: WireLog redaction will not match SDK-echoed sensitive keys that arrive in alternate casings or with embedded patterns
description: P14-024 expanded redaction key list. Two gaps in the implementation: (1) The sensitive-keys HashSet uses Ordinal*IgnoreCase* (good), but the lookup happens only when JSON is well-formed. When JsonNode.Parse fails the fallback regex (line 137) is alternation-only — it has no embedded-value detection, no value-shape detection (e.g., SSN pattern XXX-XX-XXXX in a non-listed key like `notes` or `comment` would slip through). (2) The wildcard-style fields like `PhoneNumber` are listed but actual Lacerte field codes (C1_15 SSN, C1_27 HomePhone, etc.) only get the field-code-driven scrub when the JSON shape is the literal `{"field":"C1_15","value":...}` pair. Any other shape — e.g. the row dict returned by ListClients that contains `{"C1_15":"111-22-3333"}` directly — has NO redaction, because the regex doesn't know C1_15 is sensitive and the walker doesn't recurse for known-PII column codes outside the explicit field/value pair shape. ListClients returns DbfRow dicts straight into the success envelope — every C1_X PII column ships unredacted.
recommendation: (a) Add a second JsonNode pass that, when the value of any key matches a PII pattern (SSN/EIN/phone/email regex), redacts it regardless of key name — catches the `notes` / `comment` / `description` echo case. (b) Extend the walker to also scrub VALUES of any property whose KEY is in _piiFieldCodes when the dict shape is row-flat (not just `{field, value}` pair). Concretely: at every JsonObject, for each property, if `name` matches `^C[1-7]_(\d+|G\d+)$` AND that exact code is in _piiFieldCodes, replace `obj[name]` with `***`. (c) Add tests for: SSN inside a `notes` value; ListClients-style flat-dict with C1_15 column containing an SSN.
rationale: The audit P14-024 closed the keyset-driven redactor but the redactor's coverage is shape-dependent — it works for log-line emission patterns but leaks row-flat PII through the success envelope, which is now also redacted via WrapToolHandler (P14-018). Two layers of redaction, both still leaking the same row-flat shape.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading WireLog.cs (lines 89-138), LacerteSessionManager.cs (ListClients line 451-479, CloneRow line 1292-1305), WrapToolHandler.cs (lines 61, 94), and WireLogRedactionTests.cs. The audit is correct on all three angles: (1) _sensitiveKeys is keyed by friendly names like "TaxpayerSSN" — but CloneRow emits flat dicts with raw Lacerte codes ("C1_15", "C1_27", etc.) as keys, which the walker does NOT match; (2) ScrubFieldValuePairs only triggers on the literal {"field":"<code>","value":...} write-shape pair (line 357-365), it does NOT scrub a property whose KEY is itself a PII field code; (3) the fallback regex (line 137) has no C1_X codes and no value-shape detection. End result: ListClients/ReadClient/ReadTable success envelopes ship rows like {"C1_15":"111-22-3333","C1_27":"555-1234"} unredacted through both WireLog.Redact disk write AND WrapToolHandler envelope to the MCP client. Phase 14 explicitly covered P14-018 (expanded keyset), P14-019 (error context redaction), P14-057 (arrays/nested/whitespace), and P14-024 (FieldAccessMapLoader tests) — none touched the row-flat C1_X shape. No existing test exercises a row-flat dict with PII column codes; WireLogRedactionTests confirms only the write-shape pair is covered (line 109-125). The fix is mechanically straightforward, sim-only, off-Windows verifiable.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In WireLog.cs RedactNode (line 303-345), add a third condition inside the JsonObject branch that checks if the property NAME is itself a PII field code in _piiFieldCodes — independent of the parent shape. Concretely, before the existing `_sensitiveKeys.Contains(name)` check, add: `if (_piiFieldCodes.Contains(name)) { obj[name] = JsonValue.Create("***"); continue; }`. This covers the row-flat shape that ListClients/ReadClient/ReadTable returns via CloneRow (LacerteSessionManager.cs:1292). Also expand _piiFieldCodes to cover the FULL set of PII codes from Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md DATA1-Individual (currently only 10 codes — at minimum add C1_2 LastName, C1_3 FirstName, C1_4 MiddleInitial, and any address codes C1_22/23/24/25), and add the same expansion to the fallback regex via a `C[1-7]_(\\d+|G\\d+)` alternation gated by a per-code membership filter in the MatchEvaluator. New tests in WireLogRedactionTests.cs: (a) Redact_RowFlatDict_RedactsRawFieldCodeKeys — feeds {"ClientNumber":"1001","C1_15":"111-22-3333","C1_27":"555-1234"} and asserts the SSN+phone are gone but ClientNumber is preserved; (b) integration test that calls ListClients via WrapToolHandler against a seeded sim row containing PII in C1_15/C1_29 and asserts the serialized envelope contains no PII. Skip the (a) value-shape SSN regex from the original recommendation as a separate follow-up — it would catch the `notes`-prose case but is higher false-positive-risk and not load-bearing for the primary leak (which is the row-flat dict).

title: WireLog _piiFieldCodes only covers DATA1-Individual; entity-module PII leaks
description: The PII field-code set hard-codes 10 codes from DATA1-Individual only (C1_14, C1_15, C1_19, C1_21, C1_27, C1_28, C1_29, C1_32, C1_71, C1_72). The Corporate (C), Partnership (P), SCorp (S), Fiduciary (F), and Estate (E) modules also expose SSN/EIN columns: officer SSNs in DATA1-Corp (officer compensation), K-1 recipient SSNs in DATA1-Partnership, beneficiary SSNs in DATA1-Fiduciary, bank-account columns across all modules. The current set covers `Bridge.UpdateTaxReturn` writes against an Individual module only — a `WriteField` against `module='C', field='C1_5'` (officer SSN) logs the value verbatim because C1_5 is not in the set.
recommendation: Replace the hand-curated set with a generator: at startup, walk `Schema/base/*.json` (the field-access map shards) and extract every `FieldEntry` whose Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md classification marks it as PII (or whose name in the spec contains `SSN|EIN|TIN|BankAccount|Routing|DOB|BirthDate|Phone|Email`). Land it as a static `Lazy<HashSet<string>>` populated from the schema so the redactor inherits new PII codes whenever the maps expand. Until the spec mining lands, expand the hard-coded set to cover the entity-module equivalents: add C1_5 (Corp officer SSN), C1_NN for K-1 partners (per spec), and the BankAccount columns across all modules. Add a unit test asserting `{field:'C1_5', value:'111-22-3333'}` redacts under module C, not just module I.
rationale: P14-018 explicitly cited 'DATA1-Individual' as the source spec but did not enumerate the parallel codes on entity modules. WireLog claims module-agnostic redaction; today it's module-I-only.

verdict.reasoning:
Real, but narrower than the finding claims. Confirmed at WireLog.cs:117-130: the _piiFieldCodes set is explicitly labeled "DATA1 (module 1, Individual)" and contains only 10 Individual-module codes. The ScrubFieldValuePairs pass (line 351) matches against this set with no module awareness — the WriteField args at LacerteSessionManager.cs:689-690 do include `module` context but WireLog never inspects it. So a WriteField against a non-Individual module using a code NOT in the set will log the raw value. Real concern. Not a duplicate of P14-018, which expanded key-name regex coverage and added the WriteField second pass against this DATA1-Individual set — the entity-module gap was carried forward unaddressed.

However the finding's specifics are weak:
1. The recommended "walk Schema/base/*.json" generator is non-actionable — those 9 shard files are all literally `{}` (3 bytes each). The field-access map isn't populated yet.
2. Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md does NOT enumerate entity-module PII codes; line 172 explicitly says "A complete per-module field catalog ... is needed". The spec mining the finding proposes has nothing to mine.
3. The "C1_5 = Corp officer SSN" example is fabricated. C1_5 is not in the spec under any module, and in this codebase's SimulationStore.Seed.cs:84 it represents `Dependents` (count). The finding hallucinated specific entity-module codes.
4. Blast radius is bounded to the {field, value} WriteField shape — bare-key PII (SSN, BankAccountNumber, EmailID, etc.) is still caught by the key-name _sensitiveKeys set regardless of module.

Lower confidence because the core observation is correct but the spec/schema sources for a proper fix don't exist yet, and the finding's concrete examples are unsupported. The pragmatic fix below (denylist semantics on the {field, value} pair) is real, useful, and sim-testable.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two-part fix in src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs + Tests/Logging/WireLogTests.cs (no Windows/SDK dependency):

1) Switch ScrubFieldValuePairs from allowlist to denylist semantics for the WriteField {field, value} shape. Rationale: the curated _piiFieldCodes set covers only DATA1-Individual and there is no spec source for entity-module PII codes yet (Schema/FieldAccessMap/base/*.json are all empty stubs, and Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md line 172 explicitly defers "complete per-module field catalog"). For a debug log, over-redacting WriteField values is strictly safer than guessing per module. Concretely: whenever an object has a "field" string AND a "value" sibling, redact "value" — regardless of the field code or module. This costs zero in production (LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE off by default) and a debug operator can re-derive the value from their input payload if needed; the field code + module + dryRun + result remain visible for diagnosis.

2) Add three WireLogTests.cs cases (mirroring the existing P14-018 WriteField test at the same pattern):
   (a) `{"args":{"module":"C","field":"C2_99","value":"111-22-3333"}}` → value redacts (entity-module unknown code).
   (b) `{"args":{"module":"P","field":"P3_47","value":"acct-12345"}}` → value redacts (Partnership unknown code).
   (c) Existing Individual-module test still passes (regression guard for the allowlist→denylist shift).

Delete the now-dead _piiFieldCodes HashSet (or convert it to documentation comment listing the originally-curated DATA1-Individual codes for reference). Update the XML doc on ScrubFieldValuePairs and the class-level redaction blurb (line 47-53) to describe the new "any field/value sibling pair" semantics. Do NOT pursue the schema-walking generator from the original finding — the schema shards are unpopulated and the spec lacks the data. If/when the field-access map fills in, that work can be a separate task.

Defer: separately consider redacting the top-level WriteField args.value at the call site in LacerteSessionManager.cs:689-690 by emitting a logged-arg shape that explicitly tags the value as PII (e.g., wrap with {"valueRedacted":true} when LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE_VALUES is not set) — out of scope for this fix.

title: TaxType alias list includes synthetic aliases the live SDK does not accept
description: Spec §2 explicitly lists the 9 valid ReturnType strings: `Individual, Corporate, Partnership, SCorporate, Fiduciary, Exempt, Estate, Gift, Benefit` — that's the ONLY accepted alphabet the ODBC connection string and the SDK's IClient(TaxType, ...) constructor recognize. Modules.cs ships an alias-list with 5 extra non-spec aliases per module: `"1040"`, `"1120"`, `"1065"`, `"1120S"`, `"S-Corporation"`, `"SCorp"`, `"1041"`, `"990"`, `"706"`, `"709"`, `"5500"`. These are colloquial form numbers, not SDK-accepted ReturnType strings. AcceptsTaxType returns true for every alias and CreateClientTools forwards the value verbatim into LacerteSessionManager.CreateClient → live `clientList.IClient(taxType, ...)`. On the live SDK, passing `"1040"` instead of `"Individual"` will likely return TaxModuleMismatch (14) — but the simulator returns Success because ModuleAcceptsTaxType passes. Sim and live therefore diverge on a happy-path create when the operator uses any non-spec alias, violating CLAUDE.md's two-mode discipline ('observationally identical for the happy path').
recommendation: Decide explicitly: (a) tighten Modules.TaxTypeAliases to ONLY the 9 spec strings, dropping the form-number aliases — operators who want 1040 ergonomics can build that translation in the tool layer with a clear warning; OR (b) keep aliases but have CreateClientTools and SimulateCreateClient NORMALIZE the incoming TaxType to the canonical spec string before any downstream call, so the live SDK only ever sees a spec-accepted ReturnType. Option (b) preserves operator ergonomics without breaking the two-mode invariant. Add a test asserting that passing `"1040"` or `"S-Corporation"` to lacerte_client_create produces the same response shape in sim and live (mock bridge) — today that test would fail because the normalized string never reaches the bridge.
rationale: Round 1 covered the 'CreateClient required-set' (firstName/lastName/emailID gating) but no round-1 finding examined whether the TaxType ALPHABET matches spec. P14-020 hoisted the alias list onto Modules but did not question whether the entries match what the SDK actually accepts. This is exactly the kind of sim-live divergence the audit was asked to look for.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in code: Modules.cs lines 45-53 ship per-module TaxTypeAliases that include form-number strings ("1040", "1120", "1065", "1120S", "S-Corporation", "SCorp", "1041", "990", "706", "709", "5500"). The spec (Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md §2) explicitly lists only 9 canonical ReturnType strings — these form-number variants appear nowhere. Bridge.CreateClient (LacerteAccessClient.cs:232) forwards `taxType` verbatim into `clientList.IClient(taxType, ...)` with no normalization. ODBC is fine because ConnectionStringBuilder receives `m.ReturnType` (SessionTools.cs:135), but CreateClient's SDK-facing IClient call does NOT — it passes whatever alias the operator sent. CreateClientTools.cs:154-175 only validates that the alias is in the accept-list; it never canonicalizes. Result: sim AcceptsTaxType returns true for "1040", DbfRow gets created with TaxType="1040" — but the live SDK's IClient(TaxType,...) likely rejects with TaxModuleMismatch since "1040" is not in the documented ReturnType alphabet. Sim/live divergence on the happy-path create violates CLAUDE.md's two-mode discipline. Phase-14 dupe check: P14-020 hoisted the alias list to Modules.cs and P14 added several CreateClient gates (lines 421/580/641/1152 in audit-findings.json) but none questioned whether the alias *alphabet* matches what the SDK accepts — they preserved the existing colloquial aliases as-is. Confidence is medium (not high) because the empirical "SDK rejects '1040'" claim cannot be verified off-Windows; however, spec evidence is strong enough that this should be addressed defensively.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Pick option (b) — preserve operator ergonomics, fix divergence. Concrete steps: (1) Add `Modules.CanonicalizeTaxType(char module, string taxType) -> string?` returning `info.ReturnType` when the input matches any alias case-insensitively (or null when no match). (2) In CreateClientTools.cs after the AcceptsTaxType gate at line 163, replace the verbatim `taxType` used downstream with `var canonical = Modules.CanonicalizeTaxType(moduleChar, taxType)!;` and pass `canonical` into `new CreateClientArgs(... TaxType: canonical ...)` at line 194. (3) Same canonicalization in SimulationStore.SimulateCreateClient and in LacerteSessionManager.ApplySimCreateClient so the simulator stores the canonical ReturnType in the DbfRow (today it stores "1040", which is itself a sim/live divergence in any subsequent read that exposes TaxType). (4) Tests in Schema/ModulesTests.cs: assert `Modules.CanonicalizeTaxType('I', "1040") == "Individual"`, `'S', "1120S" == "SCorporate"`, `'S', "S-Corporation" == "SCorporate"`, case-insensitive on all. (5) Tests in CreateClientToolsTests: assert that creating with TaxType="1040" yields the same response shape AND the same persisted TaxType ("Individual") as creating with TaxType="Individual" — currently this would fail because the persisted value differs. (6) Document in DECISIONS.md: "Form-number aliases (1040/1120/etc.) are accepted at the tool boundary as operator ergonomics but normalized to the canonical spec-mandated ReturnType before any SDK or DBF write." Pure C# change, no Windows or live SDK required, ~30 lines net.

title: Idempotency cache uses absolute expiry — silent surprise re-execution at 24h boundary
description: P14-013/P14-064 added a 24h TTL on idempotency entries 'matching the 24h Intuit auth window'. The implementation in TryReplayIdempotent uses absolute creation time (`DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - entry.CreatedAt > IdempotencyTtl`) — never refreshed on a cache hit. Symptom: an operator passes idempotencyKey='K1' for WriteField at t=0 (entry stored). At t=23.5h they pass the same key+payload (cache hit, no SDK call — correct). At t=24.1h they pass the same key+payload — the entry is evicted as expired, the write executes AGAIN against the SDK, and a successful first-execution side effect (a row already written) is now potentially DOUBLED. The user-facing contract was 'same key + same payload returns cached result' (CreateClientTools.cs:57 description); the silent eviction violates it. Worse, the 24h auth-window framing was the original justification — but auth re-registration doesn't actually invalidate the side effect of a prior write, so coupling these two TTLs is conceptually muddled.
recommendation: Two options: (a) Switch to sliding-window TTL — on cache HIT, refresh entry.CreatedAt (or store LastAccessedAt as a separate column). The semantic becomes 'same key+payload stays valid as long as you keep replaying it within 24h'. (b) Keep absolute TTL but on eviction-by-expiry, throw a NEW synthetic 9103 IdempotencyEvicted (the verdict on P14-064 actually suggested this naming) so the caller sees an explicit signal instead of a silent re-execute. Either way, add a test where a key+payload pair stored at t=0 is replayed at t=23h59m (must hit cache), then a fresh replay at t=24h01m (must throw 9103 — or hit cache if sliding). Update the audit-findings P14-013/P14-064 reasoning + DECISIONS.md to document which semantic was chosen.
rationale: Round-1 audit refined the cache to add 24h TTL but neither finding nor refined recommendation explicitly addressed sliding-window vs absolute semantics, nor surfaced the silent-re-execute risk. The 24h boundary is exactly the threshold most operators will hit in normal use (overnight pause + next-day replay), so the surprise is high-probability. Pure sim-actionable, ~10 lines + one test.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336-1396. The TTL implementation is absolute (entry.CreatedAt vs UtcNow), never refreshed on hit. Tool [Description] attributes on CreateClientTools.cs:57, FieldWriteTools.cs:49, and DetailsTools.cs:97 still advertise "Same key + same payload returns the cached result" with no mention of the 24h expiry — so the contract documented to the model is now silently inaccurate post-P14-013/P14-064. No test in the test tree exercises the TTL boundary (grep for IdempotencyTtl, CreatedAt, backdate, etc. in test sources returns zero hits — only build artifacts). The behavioral change the finder proposes (sliding-window OR new 9103 IdempotencyEvicted code) was already explicitly considered and rejected during round 1: P14-064's refined recommendation says "skip the new synthetic code... a never-stored key and an evicted-then-replayed key are observationally identical to a well-behaved caller and adding a new code for it just expands surface area." So the agent's core recommendation duplicates the rejected branch of P14-064's analysis. What is genuinely NEW: (a) the docstring/[Description] string is now stale relative to actual behavior, and (b) the chosen absolute-TTL semantic was decided but never pinned by a test, so a future refactor to sliding-window won't trip any guardrail. Severity is honestly low — single-operator stdio tool, write volumes per session are dozens not 10k, and overnight-pause-replay-next-day is a niche pattern. Confidence medium because the behavior question itself was already adjudicated; only the docs+test slice is undisputedly new.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Drop the behavioral-change ask (sliding-window OR 9103 IdempotencyEvicted) — P14-064's verdict already chose absolute TTL with silent miss-on-expiry and rejected the new synthetic code as surface-bloat. Limit the work to two doc+test patches: (1) Update the three tool [Description] strings to surface the TTL bound — change CreateClientTools.cs:57, FieldWriteTools.cs:49, DetailsTools.cs:97 from "Same key + same payload returns the cached result" to "Same key + same payload returns the cached result for up to 24h after the first call; replays after that re-execute (treated as a new key)." (2) Pin the chosen absolute semantic with one xUnit test in LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs using a test-only seam — either an internal `internal void SetIdempotencyEntryCreatedAtForTest(string key, DateTimeOffset)` exposed via InternalsVisibleTo, or reflection on `_idempotencyCache` to backdate CreatedAt on a stored entry. Two facts: (a) entry backdated to 23h59m ago → replay returns the cached result; (b) entry backdated to 24h01m ago → replay re-executes (observable via the same signal WriteParityTests uses: row count grows by 1 again, or a counter on a test bridge). Add one short DECISIONS.md entry titled "Idempotency cache TTL is absolute, not sliding" recording the round-1 decision and pointing at the tool [Description] strings + test as the pinning artifacts. Single PR, ~30 lines net, no behavior change. Skip the muddled-coupling critique in the original — the 24h-matches-auth-window framing is a reasonable mnemonic even if the two TTLs aren't causally linked, and rewriting it has no functional benefit.

title: BridgeInputValidation.ValidateValue does not reject NaN/Infinity on numeric value writes
description: P14-050 added `ValidateWriteDetailArgs` which explicitly rejects `double.NaN` / `double.IsInfinity` on `row.Amount` (lines 464-479) — but the generic field-write paths `ValidateWriteToDBFDatabaseArgs` and `ValidateUpdateTaxReturnArgs` call `ValidateValue(value, op)` which only branches when `value is string s` (line 289). A caller passing `double.NaN`, `double.PositiveInfinity`, or `int.MinValue` as the value for a numeric C{t}_n field (e.g. `C2_15` Amount) sails through unchecked and reaches the COM marshaller. The Lacerte SDK's late-bound COM dispatch will either marshal NaN as a junk DBF value (silent corruption of a tax field) OR throw a generic COM HRESULT that the bridge wraps as BridgeUnavailable — losing the precise reason. The asymmetry — defended at row.Amount, undefended at WriteField value — is exactly the kind of half-fix the audit was asked to look for.
recommendation: Add a `double`/`float` branch to ValidateValue: if value is double d, reject when double.IsNaN(d) || double.IsInfinity(d) with reason 'value must be a finite real number'. Same for float. Optionally also reject `decimal.MinValue` / `decimal.MaxValue` as sentinel-ish edge cases. Add unit tests for each numeric-edge case asserting DetailWriteInvalid before any COM call is attempted. The fix is ~6 lines + 3 tests, mirrors the existing row.Amount check, and closes the gap consistently across the three Write entry points.
rationale: Round 1's P14-050 was specifically about adding BridgeInputValidation. The verdict was 'real, actionable, useful' but only listed Writer/Reader entry points — the audit task explicitly asks to evaluate 'Quality of the 71 new fixes — bugs introduced, half-fixes, weak tests'. This is a half-fix: detail-row Amount is defended, generic value is not, the asymmetry creates a stealth corruption path on numeric field writes.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly against the cited code. BridgeInputValidation.ValidateValue (lines 287-293) has exactly one branch: `if (value is string s) EnsureSafeText(...)`. Every other CLR type — double, float, decimal, int, JsonElement — falls through unchecked. ValidateWriteToDBFDatabaseArgs (line 400) and ValidateUpdateTaxReturnArgs (line 417) both call ValidateValue, so numeric NaN/Infinity on a `C{t}_n` Amount-style field (e.g. C2_15) bypasses bridge validation entirely. The asymmetry the finding flags is real: ValidateWriteDetailArgs (lines 464-479) explicitly rejects NaN/Infinity on row.Amount, ValidateValue does not. Grep confirms NaN/IsInfinity exists in *only* one place in the entire Server tree (BridgeInputValidation.cs lines 462-476, the row.Amount guard), and tests cover only WriteDetail's row.Amount — no test exercises NaN as the `value` argument to WriteField/UpdateTaxReturn. Also confirmed that P14-050's refinedRecommendation step 2 (NormalizeFieldWriteValue in LacerteSessionManager.WriteField with a CLR type whitelist + JsonElement gating) was NOT shipped — grep for NormalizeFieldWriteValue/JsonElement/ValueKind in the Server source returns zero hits. So the upstream layer the auditor expected to also catch NaN never landed either; ValidateValue is the only gate, and it has the hole. Fully sim-actionable: pure CLR numeric check, no Windows/COM required, mirrors the existing row.Amount pattern, and BridgeInputValidationTests already has the harness shape. Not a duplicate — P14-050 covered the strings + the row.Amount carve-out but not the generic numeric value path.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Extend BridgeInputValidation.ValidateValue (BridgeInputValidation.cs:287-293) with three additional branches before the existing string branch returns:

1. `if (value is double d && (double.IsNaN(d) || double.IsInfinity(d)))` → throw LacerteSDKError with SyntheticStatusCodes.DetailWriteInvalid, payload `{op, field:"value", value:d, reason:"value must be a finite real number (no NaN / Infinity)."}` — mirrors lines 467-477 verbatim so the error shape stays consistent across row.Amount and generic value.
2. `if (value is float f && (float.IsNaN(f) || float.IsInfinity(f)))` → same shape. (Cast f to double in payload so JSON serialization is stable.)
3. Optional but cheap: `if (value is JsonElement je)` — reject ValueKind == Array/Object with reason "value must be a scalar (string, number, bool, or null)". This closes the related half-fix where P14-050 step 2 (JsonElement type whitelist in LacerteSessionManager.WriteField) was specified in the refinedRecommendation but never actually shipped — grep confirms zero JsonElement/ValueKind references in Server/. Belt-and-suspenders since FieldWriteTools.value is typed `object?`.

Skip decimal.MinValue/MaxValue sentinels — those are valid finite decimals; an over-eager reject would surprise operators legitimately writing large dollar amounts. Stick to NaN/Infinity only.

Add 3-4 tests to src/LacertMCP.Tests/Bridge/BridgeInputValidationTests.cs alongside the existing WriteDetail_NaNAmount tests (lines 318-340):
- WriteToDBFDatabase_NaNValue_ThrowsBeforeBridge
- WriteToDBFDatabase_PositiveInfinityValue_ThrowsBeforeBridge
- UpdateTaxReturn_NaNValue_ThrowsBeforeBridge
- (optional) WriteToDBFDatabase_JsonArrayValue_ThrowsBeforeBridge

Each asserts SyntheticStatusCodes.DetailWriteInvalid raised before any bridge call. Total diff: ~12 lines of production code + 3-4 unit tests. Touches: src/LacertMCP.Server/Bridge/BridgeInputValidation.cs, src/LacertMCP.Tests/Bridge/BridgeInputValidationTests.cs.

title: No tests for idempotency cache TTL + size-cap eviction
description: Phase-14 tasks P14-013 / P14-064 added cache size cap (IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries) and TTL eviction (IdempotencyTtl) at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336+. The TryReplayIdempotent path explicitly evicts on expiry and StoreIdempotent does opportunistic over-cap eviction by oldest CreatedAt. A grep for 'IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries|IdempotencyTtl|cache.*evict' across LacertMCP.Tests returns zero matches. The 'expired entry treated as miss' branch and the 'over cap drops oldest' branch are untested; a regression that flips the inequality (>= vs >) or skips the cleanup pass would not be caught.
recommendation: Add a test that exposes IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries via reflection / internal const, fills cache to N+1 entries, and asserts only N entries remain after the last StoreIdempotent call. Add a second test using a manipulated DateTimeOffset (or a test-only IClock seam) that asserts an expired key triggers a re-execute rather than returning the stale cached result. The TTL test is non-trivial without a clock seam — at minimum add an internal helper to force-expire an entry for tests.
rationale: Cache eviction logic is exactly the class of code where off-by-one bugs (>= cap vs > cap) and timing assumptions silently corrupt state. Zero coverage is unusual for a Phase-14 lens-9 (perf) hardening.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. P14-013 + P14-064 shipped the eviction code at LacerteSessionManager.cs:1336-1395 (TryReplayIdempotent expires via `> IdempotencyTtl`, StoreIdempotent over-caps via `> IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` with expired-first then oldest-by-CreatedAt prune). The Phase-14 refined recommendation for P14-013 EXPLICITLY listed the three tests as required deliverables ("(a) expired entry on TryReplay returns miss + re-executes, (b) over-cap StoreIdempotent prunes oldest entries, (c) replay-with-same-payload within TTL still hits"), but only (c) actually shipped — confirmed by Grep across LacertMCP.Tests for `expir|evict|MaxEntries|TTL|CreatedAt` returning zero matches in any idempotency test. The two existing idempotency tests in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs:262-310 cover only the hit-same-payload short-circuit and the conflict-on-different-payload throw. The eviction code has subtle inequality boundaries (strict `>`) where an off-by-one flip would silently break the contract and not fail any test. Actionable off-Windows: pure in-process data-structure logic, InternalsVisibleTo("LacertMCP.Tests") is already wired in AssemblyAttributes.cs:11 so reflection can reach `_idempotencyCache` and the private const/static-readonly fields. Useful: this is a known-risky code class (cache eviction with caller-supplied keys) on a hardening lens that the Phase-14 reviewer themselves flagged as test-required. Not a duplicate — P14-013 closed the implementation but its own refinedRecommendation's test asks are unfulfilled.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add three xUnit tests to src/LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs in the existing "Idempotency cache state machine" region. Use reflection (InternalsVisibleTo is already configured) on the private `_idempotencyCache` ConcurrentDictionary<string, IdempotencyCacheEntry> field. (1) `WriteDetail_IdempotencyKey_ExpiredEntry_ReExecutes`: do a first WriteDetail with idempotencyKey "exp1"; reflect into _idempotencyCache, retrieve the entry, and replace it with `new IdempotencyCacheEntry(entry.PayloadFingerprint, entry.Result, DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(-25))` (older than the 24h TTL); record the detail count, call WriteDetail again with the same key+payload, and assert the count INCREASED by 1 (re-executed, not replayed). (2) `StoreIdempotent_OverCap_DropsOldest`: rather than writing 10_001 rows, use reflection to read `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` (or hardcode a sentinel based on the known const), then directly populate _idempotencyCache via `TryAdd` with `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` entries staggered by CreatedAt (oldest = "k_old", newest progressively newer), then call a single real WriteDetail with a fresh idempotencyKey to trip the over-cap branch; assert `_idempotencyCache.Count == IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` AND `_idempotencyCache.ContainsKey("k_old") == false` AND the newest pre-seeded keys are still present. (3) `StoreIdempotent_OverCap_PrunesExpiredFirst`: seed `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` entries where half have CreatedAt > 24h ago and half are fresh; trigger one write; assert all expired entries are gone AND no fresh entry was evicted. As a follow-on tiny refactor (optional, only if reflection is judged too brittle), bump `IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries` from `private const` to `internal const` and add an `internal void ForceExpireForTests(string key)` helper that rewrites the entry's CreatedAt to UtcNow - IdempotencyTtl - 1s — cleaner than reflection and signals test-supported surface. Either path keeps the work purely off-Windows in the sim manager.

title: EnsureWritableFieldSeeded reflection helper triplicated across three test classes
description: WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs (lines 36-62), SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs (lines 38-83), and Resilience/SessionManagerAutoReconnectTests.cs (lines 26-52) each carry a near-identical 30-line copy of the static EnsureWritableFieldSeeded helper that reflects on FieldAccessMapLoader._moduleCache to inject I|1|C1_15 as ReadWrite. The three copies have subtle differences: SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests tracks a dead _seeded bool with an explicit '_ = _seeded;' suppression comment (line 81) that misleadingly suggests state matters when the actual idempotency comes from the cache.ContainsKey check above. A bug in one copy (e.g. wrong field source string, missed lock contention case) won't propagate to the other two. The behavior is also a poor fit for AccessMapMutationCollection — that collection serializes the three classes, but a stray test class outside the collection that touches the loader cache would race.
recommendation: Extract to a shared test helper (e.g. LacertMCP.Tests/Tools/AccessMapSeedHelpers.cs) with one canonical EnsureWritableFieldSeeded(char, int, string) method. Wire all three callers through it. Drop the dead _seeded field in SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests and its '_ = _seeded;' suppression comment. Optionally convert to an ICollectionFixture so the seed runs once per collection lifecycle instead of per-test under a lock.
rationale: Code duplication in tests is the same hazard as in production: drift, divergent bugs, and noise around the actual assertion. The handoff notes 'EnsureWritableFieldSeeded' as part of the integration test wiring — it should be shared infrastructure, not copy-paste.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three files (WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:36-62, SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs:38-83, SessionManagerAutoReconnectTests.cs:26-52) carry a near-identical reflection-based seed helper into FieldAccessMapLoader._moduleCache for entry I|1|C1_15. The bodies differ in trivial cosmetics (the BridgeWireup copy uses BuildKey() and tracks a `_seeded` bool with the misleading `_ = _seeded;` suppression on line 81 — confirmed dead; the other two just inline the key string). An existing AccessMapTestFixture exists but uses the on-disk reset-then-write approach, which is exactly what the in-memory triplicate was written to avoid (per the BridgeWireup comment on lines 49-55 calling out disk-write races with Stream B). Phase-14 deduped production duplication (P14-024-ish entries for module-name maps, FieldWriteTools/UpdateReturnTools shared helpers) but explicitly did not touch this test triplicate — confirmed via grep of Todo.md, audit-findings.json, and HANDOFF.md. The fix is pure test-code refactor: trivial in-session, no Windows/Lacerte needed. Useful: low-risk drift hazard (a tampered seed key in one copy could mask a real test failure in the other two), and removes a comment-trap (`_ = _seeded;`) that future contractors will waste a beat on.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `src/LacertMCP.Tests/AccessMapInMemorySeed.cs` (root `LacertMCP.Tests` namespace — keeps it visible to the three callers in Tests/Logging, Tests/Bridge, Tests/Resilience without an extra using) exposing one static method `EnsureWritableFieldSeeded(char module = 'I', int table = 1, string field = "C1_15", string source = "test-seed")` that performs the additive-only in-memory mutation under a private static lock — KEEP additive semantics (do not reset like AccessMapTestFixture; that class is the wrong tool here, as the BridgeWireup comment explicitly explains). Replace the three local copies with calls to the helper. Delete the dead `_seeded` field and `_ = _seeded;` suppression from SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests. Do NOT promote to ICollectionFixture — the three classes already share `[Collection(AccessMapMutationCollection.Name)]` which serializes them with the on-disk Tools/ tests; an ICollectionFixture would either duplicate the existing fixture's lifecycle or fight it. Add a one-line XML-doc on the helper that points readers to AccessMapTestFixture for the on-disk-reset variant so the next contractor doesn't reinvent the choice.

title: Dry-run 'does not persist' tests assert null == null and pass for wrong reason
description: FieldWriteToolsTests.FieldWrite_DryRun_DoesNotPersist (lines 96-122) and UpdateReturnToolsTests.UpdateReturn_DryRun_DoesNotPersist (lines 124-147) both read field C1_15 from BROW client 1001 before and after a dryRun write, then assert Assert.Equal(origValue, afterValue). But the simulation seed only populates C1_0 (ClientNumber), C1_1 (FirstName), C1_2 (LastName), C1_3 (TaxType) — see SimulationStore.Seed.cs:80. Field C1_15 is not seeded, so origValue is null AND afterValue is null. The assertion passes regardless of whether dry-run actually short-circuited the write — even a broken dry-run that DID persist would still leave afterValue as the new value 'dry-run-only' which is unequal to null, so this catches THAT regression — but a dry-run that wrote to the WRONG field (a SimulationStore bug where the field name was ignored) would also pass null==null. The test is brittle and over-relies on the empty-seed assumption.
recommendation: Either (a) extend the seed to include a non-null value for AccessMapTestFixture.WritableField in the BROW client, then assert origValue != null && origValue == afterValue, OR (b) write twice in succession (first with dryRun:false to establish a known value, then dryRun:true with a different value) and assert the read returns the FIRST written value. Option (b) is closer to the real-world property under test: dry-run does not mutate observable state.
rationale: A test that passes via null==null gives false confidence in dry-run correctness — a class of bug (silently writing to the wrong sim-store key) would slip past.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly against the cited code: SimulationStore.Seed.cs:75-87 (SeedIndividualClient) seeds only C1_0, C1_1, C1_2, C1_3 (Email — finding mislabels as TaxType), C1_4, C1_5, and ClientID into DATA1 for individual clients. AccessMapTestFixture.WritableField is "C1_15" (AccessMapTestFixture.cs:28). Both tests (FieldWriteToolsTests.cs:96-122 and UpdateReturnToolsTests.cs:124-147) use BROW client 1001 in TY24 IData via SetContext(SeedData.DataPathIData2024, 2024, 'I'), then read C1_15 → null, dry-run write "dry-run-only", read again → still null, assert origValue == afterValue (null == null). The assertion is satisfied by the empty-seed coincidence rather than by dry-run semantics. The finding is precise about the residual coverage too — a broken dry-run that DID persist would still be caught (afterValue would be "dry-run-only" ≠ null), but a SimulationStore bug that routes the write to a *different* field key (or to the wrong client row, or to the wrong table key) would be invisible. No Phase-14 task addresses this. In fact P14-025 explicitly cloned FieldWriteToolsTests.cs into UpdateReturnToolsTests.cs and so propagated the same tautological assertion. P14-043 reworked the dry-run snapshot mechanism (per-op undo closures replacing full module clone) — that refactor is exactly the kind of change where a tautological test gives false confidence: a regression in the undo replay path that mis-keys the restore would still pass null==null. The fix is sim-only, pure-test, ~10 lines per file.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Apply option (b) from the original recommendation — it's the property-under-test ("dry-run leaves observable state unchanged") and avoids coupling to the brittle seed-shape assumption. Concretely, in BOTH FieldWriteToolsTests.FieldWrite_DryRun_DoesNotPersist (FieldWriteToolsTests.cs:96-122) and UpdateReturnToolsTests.UpdateReturn_DryRun_DoesNotPersist (UpdateReturnToolsTests.cs:124-147): (1) Before the dry-run call, perform a real write to establish a known sentinel: `var seedJson = await tool.Lacerte{FieldWrite|UpdateReturn}(table: AccessMapTestFixture.Table, clientNumber: "1001", field: AccessMapTestFixture.WritableField, value: "seed-value-before-dryrun");` and assert seedJson reports success — this also exercises ApplySimFieldWrite, so the test now pins both the persist and the don't-persist sides of the same code path. (2) Re-read and capture origValue; assert `Assert.Equal("seed-value-before-dryrun", origValue)` to lock the seed. (3) Issue the dry-run with a DIFFERENT value ("dry-run-only"). (4) Re-read; assert `Assert.Equal("seed-value-before-dryrun", afterValue)` — this catches mis-routing (afterValue would be null), silent-persist (afterValue would be "dry-run-only"), AND row-loss (afterValue would be null). Do NOT use option (a) — extending the seed couples test fixtures to production seed data and contaminates every other test in the suite that walks IData 1001. Caller-side seeding via a real write keeps the fixture pristine and makes the test's intent explicit. While in the file, audit the two sibling idempotency-replay tests (FieldWriteToolsTests.cs:125+ and UpdateReturnToolsTests.cs:151+) for the same null==null pattern — at a glance they look OK because they compare structured envelopes, but worth a 60-second scan.

title: doctor's Unicode glyphs mojibake on default Windows console codepage
description: `ProbeResult.Glyph` returns the Unicode chars U+2713 (✓), U+26A0 (⚠), and U+2717 (✗). The default Windows console code page on most operator boxes is 437 or 850, neither of which contains these glyphs — they render as `?` or replacement boxes unless the operator has run `chcp 65001` or is in Windows Terminal. The XML comment shows the author knows the glyphs are special but there is no ASCII-only fallback. There is also no `--no-color` / `--ascii` flag anywhere in the CLI surface (the brief asked specifically about this).
recommendation: Detect support before printing: if `Console.OutputEncoding.CodePage != 65001 && Console.OutputEncoding.WebName != "utf-8"`, fall back to ASCII (`[OK]`/`[WARN]`/`[FAIL]`/`[--]`). Alternatively set `Console.OutputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8` once in Program.Main (works on net48 since Vista). Add a `--ascii` global option as a manual override and document it. Same fix applies to any future color use.
rationale: Operators running on cmd.exe or older PowerShell will see garbled output from the very first diagnostic command they run — first impression of a 'fresh install' surface. Cheap to fix and the audit brief explicitly asked about --no-color.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/DoctorCommand.cs:48-55: Glyph returns literal U+2713/U+26A0/U+2717 characters. Program.cs (src/LacertMCP.Cli/Program.cs:28-44) never sets Console.OutputEncoding. On default Windows cmd.exe/legacy PowerShell consoles the OEM codepage (CP437 in US-English, CP850 in many EU locales) does not contain these glyphs — they render as `?` unless the operator has run `chcp 65001` or is using Windows Terminal/PowerShell 7 (which default to UTF-8). The grep confirms these glyphs are ONLY used in DoctorCommand, and there is no `--ascii` or `--no-color` global option anywhere. Searched audit-findings.json + Todo.md Phase-14 for related keywords (doctor, glyph, ascii, unicode, codepage, OutputEncoding, no-color, chcp): Phase 14 touched DoctorCommand (P14-040 build-version probe, P14-046 unregister/tools verbs, P14-071 ComputeExitCode refactor, P14-017 quick-start exit-code wording) but did NOT address the rendering/encoding issue. Confirmed not a duplicate. Severity is low (cosmetic on first-touch tool) but the fix is trivial and isolated to one file plus optionally a one-line Program.cs change. The recommendation to set `Console.OutputEncoding = Encoding.UTF8` once in Program.Main is the cheapest reliable fix on net48 (supported since Vista); the ASCII fallback inside Glyph is a robust belt-and-suspenders.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-line fix, both in-session: (1) In src/LacertMCP.Cli/Program.cs Main, before constructing the root command, add `try { Console.OutputEncoding = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8; } catch { /* redirected stream — leave alone */ }`. This handles the common case (cmd.exe, legacy PowerShell) without operator action and is a no-op on already-UTF-8 terminals. (2) Keep a defensive fallback inside DoctorCommand.ProbeResult.Glyph: change return type to `string` and return ASCII tags when `Console.OutputEncoding.CodePage != 65001` (Pass=`[OK]`, Warn=`[WARN]`, Fail=`[FAIL]`, Skipped=`[--]`). Update the existing format string at line 77 from `{r.Glyph}  {r.Name}` to `{r.Glyph} {r.Name}` (string already carries its own spacing). Add a unit test in DoctorCommandTests that constructs ProbeResult instances and asserts the rendered text contains no `?` and no chars > 0x7E when CodePage != 65001 (mock by wrapping the encoding check in an internal seam). Skip the proposed global `--ascii` option — it adds CLI surface complexity for a problem the auto-detect already solves; document the auto-detect behavior in one line in the doctor section of README.md instead. Total diff: ~25 lines + one test, no Windows or Lacerte SDK needed.

title: tools has no filtering — operator must grep ~30+ entries for the one they want
description: `tools` enumerates every registered MCP tool but offers only `--json`. There's no `--name` regex filter, no `--module` (e.g. only e-file tools), no `--phase` grouping. The CLI table in README lists 6 categories of tools (read / write / create / metadata / e-file / session) but the `tools` output has no grouping or filter to match. With ~30 registered tools an operator wanting to check what 'lacerte_field_*' looks like has to pipe to `Select-String` (PowerShell) or grep — fine, but the CLI advertises itself as 'useful for sanity-checking the tool surface before pasting into a Claude Desktop config' (XML doc line 30-32) where filtering would matter most. Also no --names-only / --short output for quick listing.
recommendation: Add `--filter <regex>` (matches against tool name), `--name <exact>` (single tool deep-print including all parameter descriptions), and `--names-only` (just print one tool name per line, no descriptions — perfect for shell pipelines and CI smoke). Tests: assert `tools --filter ef` returns only entries whose names contain 'ef', and `tools --names-only` returns at least N lines with no `:` separator.
rationale: Round-1 added the tools verb but stopped at the minimum surface. The brief explicitly asked about filtering. Cheap to add and matches the documented use case.

verdict.reasoning: Verified C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/ToolsCommand.cs (lines 42-59): the `tools` verb only registers `--json`. No `--filter`, `--name`, or `--names-only`. Verified C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Tests/Cli/ToolsCommandTests.cs: no filter tests. Verified Phase-14 P14-046 in Todo.md and audit-findings.json — the original spec only required `--json`, nothing about filtering. So the finding is genuinely new, not a Phase-14 dupe. Actual tool count is ~23 across 15 *Tools.cs files (finding claim of "~30+" overstates, but order-of-magnitude correct). The XML doc comment on lines 28-32 does claim "sanity-checking the tool surface before pasting into a Claude Desktop / Cursor MCP config" which is exactly the workflow filtering would help — operator would want to grep for "ef" or "client" subsets. The fix is pure off-Windows CLI work (no Lacerte/Windows dependency), small (≈30 lines), and adds test coverage cheaply. However, this is genuinely low-severity quality-of-life — `lacerte-mcp tools | Select-String ef` already works fine in PowerShell; the upgrade is mainly about `--names-only` for shell pipeline composition and `--name <exact>` for deep-print of one tool's full parameter spec. Borderline bikeshedding but on the useful side since the deep-print mode is meaningfully different from the current "every tool, every param" dump.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add three options to ToolsCommand.Build(): (1) `--filter <regex>` — case-insensitive regex matched against ToolEntry.Name; filter applied after DiscoverTools() in Run(). Wrap the Regex constructor in try/catch and return exit code 2 with a clear stderr message on invalid pattern. (2) `--names-only` — bypass the description/parameter block entirely; print one tool name per line, sorted ordinal. Pairs cleanly with shell pipelines and CI smoke (`lacerte-mcp tools --names-only | measure-object -line` for a count assertion). Mutually compatible with `--filter`; mutually exclusive with `--json` (or `--names-only` wins — document and test). (3) `--name <exact>` — print ONE tool's full surface (including all parameter descriptions, currently truncated to one line per param), or exit code 1 with "no tool matched" if absent. Tests in ToolsCommandTests.cs: assert `Run(filter: "ef", ...)` returns only entries whose name contains "ef" (lacerte_ef_status, lacerte_ef_*); assert `Run(namesOnly: true, ...)` output line count equals DiscoverTools().Count and no line contains ':' or '-'; assert `--name lacerte_health` returns exactly one tool block; assert invalid regex returns exit 2. Skip `--module`/`--phase` from the original recommendation — those would require categorization metadata we don't have on the [McpServerTool] attribute today, so they'd need a parallel registry that drifts. Filter-by-name-prefix subsumes the grouping use case (`--filter ^lacerte_ef_` gives the e-file subset).

title: FieldAccessCommand RunList/RunSet write errors to Console.Error, bypassing writer parameter
description: RunList(char, int, int, TextWriter) accepts a writer for its happy-path output but writes the 'Unknown module' error directly to `Console.Error.WriteLine` (line 81). Same pattern in RunSet (lines 166, 171) and in the SetHandler closures (lines 65, 143). UnregisterCommand by contrast correctly takes both `stdout` and `stderr` as TextWriter parameters and uses them. The inconsistency means: (a) tests that pass a StringWriter for stdout silently miss the error message because it goes to the real Console.Error, (b) any future wrapper that wants to capture combined output (e.g. for a `--json` mode) can't, (c) the public `RunList`/`RunSet` API contract is half-honored. Sub-commands in System.CommandLine don't help here because Run* is public for testing.
recommendation: Add a `TextWriter stderr` parameter to `RunList` and `RunSet`, default Console.Error from the SetHandler, and route all current `Console.Error.WriteLine` calls inside those methods through it. Mirror the UnregisterCommand signature. Update existing tests to pass a separate stderr StringWriter and add one assertion that error messages flow through it (regression-pinning the contract).
rationale: Round-1 introduced UnregisterCommand with the clean stdout+stderr separation, but didn't backfill the older FieldAccessCommand which had the inconsistency. Minor but worth fixing while the testability pattern is fresh — keeps a single convention across the CLI surface.
