The finding's line citations are correct: RunList(line 77) accepts a TextWriter writer but writes the "Unknown module" error to Console.Error.WriteLine at line 81; RunSet(line 160) accepts a TextWriter writer but writes "Unknown module" + "Invalid --access" errors to Console.Error at lines 166, 171. The SetHandler closures (lines 65, 143) also directly use Console.Error.WriteLine for the "--module must be a single character" pre-check, which is OK in the closure (Console.Error is the default there) but RunList/RunSet should accept a stderr parameter rather than reaching for the static. UnregisterCommand.Run(bool, TextWriter stdout, TextWriter stderr) at line 55 is the clean reference pattern, introduced as part of Phase-14 P14-046. No RunList/RunSet tests exist today, so the testability hole the finding identifies is latent (will bite the first test that tries to assert error messages). Searched audit-findings.json + Todo.md Phase 14: no duplicate. The only Phase-14 touch on this file was the Modules.FileBasenameFor extraction (dedup refactor), which didn't address stderr routing. Pure CLI refactor — no Windows/SDK needed. Severity is correctly tagged low, but the fix is ~30 lines and locks in a single convention across the four CLI command files.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Change RunList(char, int, int, TextWriter) -> RunList(char, int, int, TextWriter stdout, TextWriter stderr) and RunSet(...) similarly, mirroring UnregisterCommand.Run(bool, TextWriter, TextWriter). Replace the three Console.Error.WriteLine calls inside RunList/RunSet (FieldAccessCommand.cs:81, 166, 171) with stderr.WriteLine. In the two SetHandler closures (BuildListCommand line 60, BuildSetCommand line 138), pass Console.Out + Console.Error explicitly to the Run* call so the default is visible and grep-able rather than buried in the method (the pre-check Console.Error.WriteLine at lines 65 + 143 can stay in the closure since it runs before Run* is called — or move it into RunList/RunSet so all validation lives in one place). Add a regression-pinning test: call RunList('Z', 1, 2024, new StringWriter(), new StringWriter()) with the unknown-module sentinel and assert (a) exit code 1, (b) stderr StringWriter contains "Unknown module", (c) stdout StringWriter is empty. One test for RunSet's invalid --access path mirrors it. Total diff ~40 lines incl. tests; no behavior change in production paths.

title: StatusInfo.UserMessage and Remediation strings are English-baked with no localization seam
description: Every userMessage and remediation in StatusCodes.StatusTable and SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable is a hardcoded English string. Lacerte ships localized installs (notably Canadian-French and Spanish-speaking US markets per Intuit's international rollouts). When the SDK echoes localized text into ex.Message (preserved in context.reason / rawError per Bridge/* and Writer.cs:67/122/190), the wire envelope will mix English MCP-layer strings with localized SDK-layer strings — confusing for both LLM (lower NER precision on mixed-language text) and human operators reading the same log. No CultureInfo plumbing exists.
recommendation: Either (a) commit to en-US in the spec/REQUIREMENTS.md and document it as a known limitation — operators on localized installs accept English MCP messages; or (b) introduce a StatusInfo localization seam: StatusInfo.UserMessage becomes StatusInfo.UserMessage(CultureInfo) with a fallback to en-US, and the StatusTable values become {key → {culture → string}} dictionaries. (a) is a 1-line README change + a DECISIONS.md entry; (b) is a deeper refactor. Pick (a) for now and revisit if the operator's install ever surfaces non-English SDK text.
rationale: Low severity (the operator is single-user English speaker per CLAUDE.md "Single operator") but the assumption is invisible. Without a documented decision, the next contractor may waste a session trying to internationalize — or worse, an LLM may try to translate the SDK's localized exception text and re-trigger known mojibake bugs.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the factual claim by reading StatusCodes.cs, SyntheticStatusCodes.cs, and StatusInfo.cs — every UserMessage and Remediation is a hardcoded English literal, StatusInfo has no CultureInfo overload, and GetStatusInfo returns a single en-US fallback for unknown codes. Grepped audit-findings.json, Todo.md, REQUIREMENTS.md, DECISIONS.md, and README.md for any localization/CultureInfo/en-US/language keyword — zero hits. Phase 14 did not touch this surface, so the finding is NOT a duplicate. The useful question is borderline: per CLAUDE.md the project is explicitly a single-operator personal tool ('Bar is works flawlessly, not ships to customers') and the operator is the English-speaking US user per the memory file, so the actual i18n risk is essentially zero. However, the recommendation's option (a) — document the en-US assumption — has real meta-value in a heavily AI-driven workflow: without it, a future audit (round 3) or an LLM auto-fix pass will re-surface this same finding and waste session time, and CLAUDE.md+REQUIREMENTS.md is exactly where 'invisible assumptions' should be made visible. Option (b) refactor to a CultureInfo-keyed dictionary would be over-engineering and rightly rejected. Net: confirm as a docs-only, low-effort fix.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Docs-only fix in two locations, no code change:

1. DECISIONS.md — append a new dated entry:
```
## 2026-05-30 — Status messages are en-US only (no localization seam)

StatusCodes.StatusTable, SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable, and the
GetStatusInfo unknown-code fallback emit hardcoded English UserMessage
and Remediation strings. StatusInfo has no CultureInfo overload.

Rationale:
- Single-operator English-speaking US deployment per CLAUDE.md "Single operator".
- The wire envelope already mixes our en-US strings with whatever the
  SDK echoes into context.reason / rawError. Localizing only the MCP
  layer would not produce a fully-localized response; we would still
  emit mixed-language output. Either fully translate (out of scope for
  a personal tool) or accept en-US for both layers (what we do).
- LLMs handle en-US technical strings reliably; routing through a
  CultureInfo plumbing layer would add complexity for zero current
  operator benefit.

Revisit only if the operator deploys against a non-en-US Lacerte install
and observes context.reason text the LLM mishandles.
```

2. REQUIREMENTS.md — add a one-line bullet under the operator-environment / scope section:
`* **Locale:** All MCP-layer UserMessage and Remediation strings are emitted in en-US. SDK-echoed text in context.reason is passed through unmodified.`

No source, test, csproj, or workflow changes. Verify with a grep that the new DECISIONS entry is the only mention of "localization" or "CultureInfo" in the repo (so a future audit hits this decision before re-raising the finding).

title: FieldAccessMapLoader.AssertWritable for FieldAccess.Unknown buries the remediation in context.reason
description: When a field isn't in the access map, AssertWritable throws SyntheticStatusCodes.UnknownFieldAccess (9012). The StatusInfo remediation is good: "Run `lacerte-mcp field-access discover` to populate the map, or pass force:true to override." — but the throw-site ALSO stuffs a near-duplicate ~120-char remediation into context["reason"] ("Refusing to write. Pass force:true to override, or run 'lacerte-mcp field-access discover'"). After the round-1 fix runs WireLog.Redact, context.reason becomes "***" — but the standalone remediation in the envelope is still correct. So this is a duplication that wastes payload, doesn't change behavior, but creates a maintenance trap: future edits to one copy won't track the other. Also the throw doesn't include the suggested next-step args (force:true is mentioned but the *current* call args aren't echoed so the LLM can rebuild the call easily).
recommendation: Drop the duplicated remediation from context["reason"]. Replace with a structured context: {module, table, field, taxYear, suggestedRetryArgs: {force: true}, suggestedCli: "lacerte-mcp field-access discover"}. The LLM gets one source of truth (remediation), plus typed handles to either retry the same call with force:true or run the suggested CLI. Apply the same pattern to the read-only case (line 206) and the not-exposed case (line 211).
rationale: Single-copy remediation is the lower-maintenance shape, and giving the LLM machine-readable retry hints (suggestedRetryArgs) lets it construct the retry call without re-parsing prose. Cheap fix that pays compounding dividends as more error paths add structured retry hints.

verdict.reasoning: Verified. Real issue with high confidence.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Drop context.reason in all 5 AssertWritable branches and replace with typed keys.

title: _newApisCache and _edition not cleared on Register() — re-auth doesn't refresh per-process derivatives
description: Register() updates IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt on success but does NOT clear _newApisCache or _edition. After a long-running session the operator re-runs Register() (because the 24h ticket expired and they want a fresh session) — but if a prior CanUseNewApis probe failed transiently and got cached (via the AutoReconnect.WithRetrySync wrapping in CanUseNewApis at line 432-435, which still propagates final-failure exceptions through GetOrAdd — actually GetOrAdd's factory exception does NOT cache, so transient probe failures DON'T pollute _newApisCache; this is the saving grace), then for _edition specifically (cached on first failure as 'Unavailable' per P14-061) the re-Register does nothing to refresh it. Compound with finding 'EditionDetection cached as Unavailable forever': re-registering after a Lacerte version bump shows the wrong (or 'Unavailable') edition until process restart.
recommendation: In Register() on the AccessGranted branch, clear the derived caches: `_edition = null;` (with _editionLock held). Optionally clear _newApisCache too — the (year, module) → useNewApis answer is technically stable across re-auth so this is defensive, but free. Document the contract: 'A successful Register() invalidates EditionInfo so the next SessionStatus re-probes.'
rationale: Pair fix with the EditionDetection issue above. Without clearing on re-auth, the operator's only path to refresh the edition is process restart, which defeats the purpose of having Register() as a re-auth surface. Low severity because today's wire-disconnect cache pollution is only the edition string, not anything functional — but lifecycle correctness matters for the documented re-auth workflow.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 85-94 (field declarations), 186-256 (Register), and 311-349 (EnsureEditionProbed). Both caches are confirmed:

(1) _newApisCache is a ConcurrentDictionary<(int,char), bool> populated via GetOrAdd at line 418-438. The finding's claim that GetOrAdd does NOT cache factory exceptions is correct — Microsoft documents that an exception in the valueFactory propagates and the key is NOT added — so transient CanUseNewApis probe failures do NOT poison the cache. Successful answers persist for process lifetime.

(2) _edition is a single nullable field. EnsureEditionProbed (P14-061) explicitly caches the 'Unavailable' sentinel on probe failure (line 345) so the docstring's 'never re-probed for the lifetime of the process' contract holds.

(3) Register() AccessGranted branch (lines 226-231 live, 242-247 sim) updates only IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt. Neither _edition nor _newApisCache is touched.

(4) Cross-checked Phase-14 task list (P14-001..P14-071 in Todo.md): P14-061 added the cache-failure-as-sentinel behavior but did NOT add cache invalidation on Register(). The audit-findings.json EnsureEditionProbed entry's refinedRecommendation explicitly stops at 'cache the failure'; it never mentions clearing on re-auth. This finding is genuinely new and is the natural follow-on to P14-061.

(5) Real-world impact is low — the dominant operator workflow is start → use → stop, and a fresh process re-probes from scratch. The 24h Intuit auth window plus stdio MCP lifetime mean mid-process Register() is rare. But the CLI does expose `lacerte-mcp register` as a re-auth surface, and after P14-061 the edition string can semantically lie until process restart, which contradicts the documented intent of having Register() as a refresh point. Fix is ~6 lines + a sim-only unit test using the test ctor with a throwing fake bridge that flips to non-throwing on second probe.

(6) The finding's own analysis of _newApisCache being a defensive (not strictly necessary) clear is correct — the (year, module) → useNewApis answer is a property of the Lacerte install, not the auth ticket, so it's stable across re-auth. Clearing it is cheap insurance for the case where a future Lacerte upgrade changes TY21+ support mid-process.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
In LacerteSessionManager.Register() on AccessGranted (both sim path line 247 and live path line 231), invalidate the derived per-process caches so a successful re-auth refreshes them:

```csharp
// After setting IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt on AccessGranted:
lock (_editionLock) { _edition = null; }
_newApisCache.Clear();
```

Rationale per cache:
- _edition: REQUIRED after P14-061. Without it, a transient first-probe failure (e.g. live bridge BridgeUnavailable during a pre-Phase-9 startup, or a slow COM probe timing out once) sticks 'Unavailable/Unavailable/Unavailable' to the snapshot for process lifetime — the operator's documented escape hatch (`lacerte-mcp register` re-auth) does not refresh it, only process restart does. That defeats the point of Register() being a re-auth surface.
- _newApisCache: DEFENSIVE / cheap insurance. The (year, module) → bool answer is a property of the installed Lacerte build, not the auth ticket, so it survives re-auth correctly today. Clearing it costs ~9 entries max (1 per module) and protects against a future Lacerte version-bump mid-process; not strictly required.

Add one sim-only xUnit test in LacerteSessionManagerTests using the internal test ctor with an ILacerteBridge fake whose first probe throws and second succeeds: assert SessionStatus().Edition returns 'Unavailable' before Register(), then after a second Register() call returns the success triple. Document the contract in the Register() XML doc: 'A successful Register() invalidates the cached EditionInfo and CanUseNewApis answers so the next SessionStatus()/CanUseNewApis() re-probes the bridge.' Add a one-line cross-reference comment at the _edition declaration site (line 93) pointing to Register() so a future contributor doesn't re-introduce the leak.

Do NOT clear IsRegistered/RegisteredAt/ExpiresAt or Context — Register() already manages those; only the derived probe caches need clearing on success. Do NOT touch the failure branches (lines 234-237, 251-253) — those already leave IsRegistered=false and a failed re-register correctly does not invalidate the prior successful probe state.

title: WireLog ProcessExit hook + AutoFlush ok for graceful exit but no flush on hard-kill; no rotation policy beyond per-day file
description: Two gaps in the WireLog lifecycle for long-running ops: (1) Rotation is per-UTC-day only — no per-file size cap, no compression, no retention. A debug-wire-on session that runs for a week produces 7 lacerte-YYYYMMDD.log files of unbounded size that accumulate forever in cfg.LogDir. Disk-full is handled by the swallow-and-drop-cached-writer path (lines 446-460), but there's no proactive pruning. (2) The midnight rollover works correctly (FilenameForToday produces a new path, GetOrOpenWriterLocked sees a cache miss and closes prior writers) — but only when a write happens AFTER midnight. If logs are quiet at midnight, the previous day's writer stays open holding an OS file handle until the next write. Combined with FileShare.ReadWrite this is benign but contradicts the stated 'rolls over at midnight' contract. (3) ProcessExit hook is correct for graceful shutdown but doesn't fire on TerminateProcess / SIGKILL / power loss; the AutoFlush=true mitigates this for content but the file remains open and may be marked as 'in-use' by Windows file-system trim on next boot.
recommendation: Add a max-files-per-dir or max-bytes-per-file cap with a simple rolling delete (e.g. keep last 14 days, or keep total under 500MB). Document LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS env var. The midnight-rollover contract should explicitly say 'on next write after midnight, not at midnight' OR a low-priority background timer could close stale writers (probably not worth the complexity). The TerminateProcess gap is fundamentally a Windows OS behavior — note in DECISIONS.md that AutoFlush guarantees content durability but the file remains open until next process start.
rationale: P14-007 in audit-findings moved WireLog to keep-file-open for perf but didn't add rotation. For an operator who runs the MCP server as a long-lived service with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 for ongoing diagnostics (the documented use case in README), the log directory grows without bound. Low severity because disk-full is handled defensively, but operationally noisy.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified all three sub-claims against the current WireLog.cs and the Phase-14 task list.

Sub-claim 1 (NO ROTATION/RETENTION POLICY) — REAL AND NEW. The file at lines 556-557 produces `lacerte-YYYYMMDD.log`, GetOrOpenWriterLocked at 465-495 only manages cross-day handle hygiene (not pruning), and there is zero size cap, zero file-count cap, zero retention. P14-012 (the prior round-1 fix that introduced the cached writer) explicitly says "rolling at midnight; per-UTC date" but never mentions retention. Greps across Todo.md, README.md, DECISIONS.md, HANDOFF.md show zero references to "retention/rotation/RETENTION_DAYS/prune". P14-018/019/037/057/067 all touch WireLog but none address growth policy. The README at line 95 markets LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE as an operator-toggleable diagnostic — exactly the use case that produces unbounded log directories. Genuinely useful for the documented operator workflow.

Sub-claim 2 (MIDNIGHT ROLLOVER "CONTRADICTS CONTRACT") — FALSE/BIKESHED. The code at lines 471-482 (added by P14-012) does close stale writers "on next write" — the XML doc at line 72 already says "naturally appears at midnight rollover and a new writer is opened then" which is honest about the lazy semantics. No real contradiction. Holding one FD overnight on an idle Windows process is not a real ops concern. Drop this from the recommendation.

Sub-claim 3 (TerminateProcess GAP) — REAL BUT NOT WORTH FIXING. AutoFlush=true (line 490) already pushes each WriteLine through the FileStream buffer to the OS write path before returning, so on hard-kill the only loss is whatever was in the OS page cache at SIGKILL — and Windows file-system journaling handles that. The DECISIONS.md note suggestion is doc-housekeeping with negligible value vs the retention gap. Drop this too.

Net: one real, useful, in-session fix (rotation/retention) + two bikeshed items to drop. Fully sim-actionable — pure C# Directory.GetFiles + DateTime arithmetic on filenames + File.Delete. Tests slot into existing WireLogTests temp-dir harness.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Scope this to the retention gap only — drop the midnight-wording and TerminateProcess bullets (the former is bikeshedding, the latter is OS-level and AutoFlush already covers content durability).

Single-file fix in src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs:

1) Add a `LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` env var resolved in ResolveConfig (default `14`, accepted range `1..365`, invalid → silent fallback to 14 — same "never break the operator path" rule as the existing path-validation fallback at line 583). Store on WireLogConfig as an int `RetentionDays`.

2) Add a `static int _lastPrunedDayOfYear = -1` sentinel guarded by `_writeLock`. Inside GetOrOpenWriterLocked's cache-miss branch (after line 482, before the FileStream open), if `DateTime.UtcNow.DayOfYear != _lastPrunedDayOfYear`, call `PruneOldLogsLocked(cfg.LogDir, cfg.RetentionDays)` and update the sentinel. This makes pruning a once-per-day O(N) directory scan that piggybacks on the natural rollover write — no background timer, no extra threads, no perf cost on the steady-state hot path.

3) PruneOldLogsLocked implementation: `Directory.GetFiles(logDir, "lacerte-????????.log")` → parse the 8-char `yyyyMMdd` segment via `DateTime.TryParseExact` (skip any name that doesn't match — defensive against operator-dropped files) → `File.Delete` everything older than `UtcNow.Date - RetentionDays`. Wrap each File.Delete in its own try/catch that swallows IOException (file may be held open by a tail viewer); never propagate.

4) Document `LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS` in README.md's env table (add row after line 96 entry for LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH).

5) Tests in WireLogTests.cs: (a) seed `lacerte-20250101.log` + `lacerte-20250102.log` + today's file in a temp dir, set RetentionDays=14 via EnableForTests (extend signature to accept retentionDays optional param, default 14), force a write that triggers the prune branch, assert the two old files are gone and today's survives; (b) seed a malformed `lacerte-notadate.log`, assert prune leaves it untouched (defensive); (c) seed today + yesterday with RetentionDays=1, assert yesterday's file IS pruned (boundary).

Skip the "size cap per file" and "total-dir-size cap" suggestions from the original finding — JSON-per-line records are tiny and a 14-day window with one-record-per-tool-call cap is already small enough to make per-file size irrelevant. Single env knob beats two.

Total scope: ~50 LOC + 3 tests + 1 README row. No DECISIONS.md entry needed — the policy is self-evident from the env var name and matches the project's existing "operator-toggleable, sensible default" pattern.

title: Read paths log args but not result-shape — no result-size telemetry
description: Read chokepoints (`ListClients`, `ReadTable`, `ReadEFStatus`, `ReadSubclients`, `ReadStates`, `ReadStatuses`, `ReadForms`, `ReadDetail`) wrap their bodies in `WireLog.Record` — but the `result` field in the log line is the FULL payload, then post-redacted. For `ReadTable(1)` against a 5000-client DBF this writes 5000 row dicts to disk per call (~2 MB per log line). Two issues: (1) the log balloons (contributes to finding #2), and (2) the operator looking at logs cannot quickly see "this call returned 5000 rows in 800ms" without parsing the entire JSON payload. There's no `resultCount` or `resultBytes` summary field. Compare to the write side which logs `result` as a single `int` TAPIStatus — that side is fine. The read side over-shares: the LLM client got the data, the log file doesn't need to re-store the entire payload to be debuggable.
recommendation: In `WireLog.WriteRecord`, when `result` is `IList`/`ICollection`/`IDictionary` or implements `IEnumerable` (and isn't already a small JsonNode), serialize as `{ "kind": "collection", "count": N, "sampleFirst": <first item only> }` instead of the full payload. Add an env var `LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1` that opts in to the current verbose behavior for the rare deep-debugging session. This is the right knob alongside the redact-all toggle (which is a separate gap) — it cuts the per-line size from MB to KB on the common large-read path without losing per-call duration/op/args/count signal. Bonus: makes finding-#2 rotation pressure much rarer for typical operator workflows.
rationale: Today the debug log doubles as a copy of every read payload. That's not observability — that's a full data export. The operator needs counts + samples, not the dataset.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED via direct read of LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 455-617 and WireLog.cs lines 145-462. Every read chokepoint (ListClients, ReadClient, ReadTable, ReadSubclients, ReadStates, ReadStatuses, ReadForms, ReadDetail, ReadEFStatus) wraps its body in WireLog.Record<T>(...) where T is IReadOnlyList<IReadOnlyDictionary<string,object?>>. WriteRecord at WireLog.cs:398-462 builds a dictionary with record["result"] = result and feeds the full payload to JsonSerializer.Serialize before passing it to Redact. There is no count/sample summarization, no size cap, and no opt-in switch — every read is mirrored to disk in full. For ListClients(limit=int.MaxValue-equivalent) or ReadTable(1) on a 5k-row DBF this produces multi-MB log lines per call.

NOT a Phase-14 duplicate. Phase 14 WireLog tasks were: P14-012 (file-handle reuse — orthogonal), P14-018/P14-019/P14-057 (redaction expansion + JsonNode walker — those harden WHAT is redacted, not how much is logged), P14-067 (drop dead ResetForTests). None of the 71 landed fixes address result-payload volume or add count/sample summarization. P14-013 caps the idempotency cache and P14-014 caps the SQL fetch — neither caps log-line size.

Fully actionable off-Windows: the entire change lives in WireLog.WriteRecord plus a unit test. No bridge, no COM, no Lacerte install. The existing WireLog tests demonstrate the test seam (EnableForTests / FlushForTests / Redact) already used by Phase-14 redaction tests.

IsUseful: yes. The sim store currently seeds modest fixtures but ReadTable is the same chokepoint live-mode ODBC reads will hit on real-world client rosters (the project's spec assumes thousands of clients per practice). Operators with LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 enabled for a few hours would see logs grow from KB to GB. The summary line {kind, count, sampleFirst} keeps every operationally useful signal (op, duration, count, shape).

Minor refinement to recommendation: the JsonNode walker added in P14-057 is the right place to plug this in — summarize JsonArray nodes assigned to the "result" key when length > N, rather than introducing a separate IEnumerable type-sniff path. This stays consistent with the post-P14-057 architecture (one structured walker, regex only as fallback). Also: the proposed env var should be named consistently with the existing LACERTE_DEBUG_* family.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In WireLog.WriteRecord, after JsonSerializer.Serialize but BEFORE Redact, post-process the parsed JsonNode to summarize large arrays under the top-level \"result\" key. Concretely: parse the serialized record back into a JsonNode (or build the record as a JsonObject from the start to skip the round-trip), and if the result value is a JsonArray with Count > LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_RESULT_SAMPLE (default 5), replace it with {\"kind\":\"collection\",\"count\":N,\"sample\":[first 1-5 items]}. Apply the same summarization recursively if any sampled item is itself a large array (depth cap = 2 to keep it bounded). Gate the summarization behind an opt-out env var LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1 (default: summarize) so deep-debugging sessions can still capture the full payload. Land three xUnit cases in WireLogTests: (1) sub-threshold result (e.g. 3 rows) logs as-is; (2) above-threshold result (e.g. 5000 fake DbfRow dicts) logs as a {kind,count,sample} object with sample.Length == 5 and count == 5000; (3) LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_FULL_RESULTS=1 disables summarization. Keep the existing redaction pipeline downstream of the summarization so sampled rows still pass through RedactNode + ScrubFieldValuePairs (the sampled rows are real DbfRow dicts and can carry SSN/EmailID/etc.). Add a one-line entry to the WireLog DECISIONS.md block landed in P14-037 explaining the summarization policy. No Bridge/ODBC/Windows dependency — entire change is in WireLog.cs plus tests.

title: Reader.cs bridge call bypasses WireLog while Writer.cs is wrapped — asymmetric debug coverage
description: P14-004 added Marshal.ReleaseComObject to both Writer.cs and Reader.cs in parallel, and Writer.cs also goes through WireLog.RecordSync<int> for each of its three entry points (WriteToDBFDatabase, UpdateTaxReturn, WriteDetail). Reader.cs's ReadFromDBFData has NO WireLog wrapping — so when an operator sets LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 to diagnose a live read issue, the introspection path through the COM reader produces zero log records. Inconsistent with the F11 invariant ("every chokepoint logs") and the audit's own note on Writer that says "F11 — wrap with WireLog" three times. The Bridge/Reader cold-fallback case (when ODBC DSN is broken but COM works) is exactly where WireLog observability is most needed.
recommendation: Wrap Reader.ReadFromDBFData's body in `WireLog.RecordSync<string>("Bridge.ReadFromDBFData", new { dbf, dataPath }, () => { ... })` mirroring Writer's pattern. Put it inside the validation (so it logs accepted calls only) but outside AcquireReader so failed acquisitions still surface in the log via the error-record path.
rationale: Minor but the Phase-14 hygiene push touched both files in parallel for COM-release; the WireLog asymmetry was missed. Low-effort copy of an established pattern.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by direct file reads. Reader.cs:35-78 has zero WireLog wrapping — the body goes straight to BridgeInputValidation, then AcquireReader, then dynamic invoke, then finally ReleaseComObject. Writer.cs's three entry points (WriteToDBFDatabase:45, UpdateTaxReturn:98, WriteDetail:160) all call WireLog.RecordSync<int>(\"Bridge.X\", ...) at the bridge boundary even though LacerteSessionManager ALSO wraps the higher-level Read*/Write* paths — so the project's established pattern is double-coverage at both session and bridge layers. The Todo.md F11 description (line 168) explicitly lists \"Bridge/LacerteAccessClient + Bridge/Writer methods\" but omits Bridge/Reader — an inherited gap that Phase 14's COM-release task (P14-004) touched in parallel without noticing. Grep across audit-findings.json for Reader/ReadFromDBFData/F11/chokepoint surfaces no Phase-14 finding that addresses the Reader WireLog wrap. Sim-friendly: WireLog.RecordSync is platform-neutral, runs the body inline, and Reader's off-Windows path (BridgeUnavailable throw) will be captured as an error record exactly as the finding requests. The fix is a 5-line copy of the Writer pattern. Useful because the Reader path is precisely the cold-fallback / schema-discovery case where observability matters most — without it, an operator setting LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 to diagnose a live-mode read failure gets zero records from the bridge layer for reads.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Mirror Writer.cs exactly in Reader.cs:35-78. Concrete edit: after the existing `BridgeInputValidation.ValidateReadFromDBFDataArgs(...)` call (which must stay outside the wrap so validation rejections don't pollute the log), wrap the rest of the body in `return WireLog.RecordSync<string>(\"Bridge.ReadFromDBFData\", new { dbf, dataPath }, () => { ... });`. Inside the lambda, keep the existing `var reader = AcquireReader(\"ReadFromDBFData\");` + try/catch/finally (ReleaseComObject) verbatim — both the BridgeUnavailable throw from AcquireReader and the LacerteSDKError wrap from the dynamic call will surface via WireLog's error-record path. Do NOT include `appId` in the args object (matches Writer.cs:46/99/161 which intentionally omit appId — it's a stable session identifier already known from Bridge.Register and noisy at per-call frequency). Add `using LacertMCP.Server.Logging;` at the top (Writer.cs:4 has it; Reader.cs currently does not). Optional: extend the existing Reader unit test (off-Windows BridgeUnavailable path) to set `WireLog.EnableForTests()` and assert one record is written with op=\"Bridge.ReadFromDBFData\" and an error block — mirrors WireLogTests pattern (~10 lines, no Windows needed). Skip the Todo.md F11 line edit unless doing a broader doc sweep — F11 is already checked off and adding Bridge/Reader to its description retroactively would muddy the changelog; the new task can stand on its own P14-followup line.

title: Idempotency cache: type-mismatch on cached Result misreports as 'different payload fingerprint'
description: In TryReplayIdempotent (lines 1349-1359): when the cached entry's PayloadFingerprint matches the new payload, the code tries `entry.Result is T match`. If the cast fails (e.g., somehow a CreateClientResult was cached under a key now being used by WriteField returning int), the code falls through to throw IdempotencyConflict with reason = 'Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint.' That message is FACTUALLY wrong in this branch — the fingerprint matched. This case can arise via developer error (operator reuses a key across tools) or via a future refactor that changes return types; the misleading error sends the diagnostician chasing a payload-canonicalization bug that isn't there. The actual cause (key reused across operations) is invisible.
recommendation: Split the throw into two branches: (a) when `entry.PayloadFingerprint != payload` → throw with reason 'Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint.' (the existing message). (b) when fingerprint matches but cached type != T → throw with reason 'Idempotency key reused across operations with different return types (cached: <cachedType>, requested: <T>).' Include both in the context dict so the operator can see exactly which keys collide. Add one test that primes the cache with an int result, then calls WriteDetail (also int) and CreateClient (CreateClientResult) under the same key to demonstrate the disambiguation.
rationale: Phase-14 P14-005 closed the TOCTOU race but left the error-message branch wrong for the secondary failure mode. Trivial fix, real DX win when (not if) the case fires.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 1349-1359: when entry.PayloadFingerprint == payload but `entry.Result is T match` fails, control falls through to the same `throw new LacerteSDKError(...IdempotencyConflict, { reason = "Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint." })`. The reason string is factually wrong on that branch — the fingerprint matched; the failure was a return-type mismatch. The inline comment at line 1352 ("Cached result type mismatch — treat as conflict.") even acknowledges this branch but reuses the wrong message. Phase-14 covered TOCTOU (P14-005), TTL/eviction (P14-013/P14-064), timing-safe compare (P14-064), and BuildPayload short-circuit (P14-042) but did NOT touch the error-shape disambiguation. Off-Windows actionable — pure C# change with a SimulationStore-backed unit test using existing WriteField (int) vs CreateClient (CreateClientResult) tools. Low severity (only fires on operator key reuse across tools or a future return-type refactor) but real DX win that prevents diagnostician misdirection.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In TryReplayIdempotent (LacerteSessionManager.cs ~1349-1359), split the conflict throw into two distinct branches so the error message matches the actual failure mode: (1) `entry.PayloadFingerprint != payload` → keep existing reason "Idempotency key reused with a different payload fingerprint." and include the cached + requested fingerprint prefixes (first 8 chars only — full base64 is noise) in the context dict. (2) Fingerprint matches but `entry.Result is T` fails → throw with reason "Idempotency key reused across operations with different return types." and include `cachedType = entry.Result?.GetType().FullName ?? "null"` and `requestedType = typeof(T).FullName` in the context dict (serialize as strings, not Type objects — Type does not round-trip through System.Text.Json). Keep the synthetic status code as IdempotencyConflict (9102) for both — no new status code needed. Add one Xunit fact in IdempotencyTests (or LacerteSessionManagerTests, wherever the P14-005 stress test landed) that: (a) calls WriteField with key "K1" (returns int), (b) calls CreateClient with same key "K1" (returns CreateClientResult), (c) asserts the second call throws LacerteSDKError with code 9102, reason containing "different return types", and context dict containing both type names. This is off-Windows-actionable via SimulationStore. ~15 LOC change + ~25 LOC test.

title: release.ps1 wipes the entire output directory and re-creates it — silently destroys prior artifacts
description: release.ps1 derives staging from -OutputDir if supplied (line 23), then unconditionally does `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $staging -Recurse -Force` (line 79) if it exists. If an operator runs `./scripts/release.ps1 -OutputDir C:/builds/lacerte` and that directory holds older release zips (LacerteMCP-v0.0.9.zip, etc.) or ANY other content, they are wiped without prompt or warning. Default OutputDir is `./dist` which is usually safe, but the parameter exists specifically so operators can redirect output — and pointing it at a shared artifact dir or git-tracked location is destructive. Also, the script does not validate that OutputDir is not a high-value path like the repo root, the user profile, or a system directory.
recommendation: Either (a) place the zip + staged tree under a versioned subdirectory (e.g. `$staging/LacertMCP-v$Version/`) and only wipe THAT subdirectory, leaving other content in OutputDir intact, OR (b) refuse to overwrite an existing OutputDir without a -Force flag (`if ((Test-Path $staging) -and -not $Force) { throw 'Output dir exists; pass -Force to overwrite.' }`). Also validate OutputDir is not equal to (or a parent of) the repo root before any Remove-Item. Add a one-line test that runs the script against a dir with a pre-existing dummy file and asserts the dummy is still present after a successful release.
rationale: P14-010 introduced the script as a new operator-facing surface. The destructive behavior is contrary to standard CLI build-tool conventions (e.g. msbuild, cargo, npm don't wipe arbitrary output dirs). Single-operator project so blast radius is bounded, but the workflow could easily land on the operator's shared C:/builds/ path.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading scripts/release.ps1: line 23 sets `$staging = $OutputDir` when provided; line 78-79 then unconditionally `Remove-Item -LiteralPath $staging -Recurse -Force` if the path exists. There is no -Force/-Clean opt-in flag, no versioned subdirectory isolation, no validation that OutputDir isn't a high-value path (repo root, $HOME, drive root). An operator running `./scripts/release.ps1 -OutputDir C:/builds/lacerte` would silently lose every prior artifact and any unrelated content in that directory. Phase-14 verification: P14-010 (Todo.md line 245) introduced this script and Phase-14 has no follow-up addressing the destructive behavior. Audit-findings.json shows P14-010 was the only release.ps1 entry and its refinedRecommendation never mentioned wipe safety. Severity is correctly low — default `./dist` is safe and the project is single-operator — but the fix is genuinely useful (matches msbuild/cargo/npm convention of never wiping operator-supplied output dirs) and trivially implementable off-Windows in pure PowerShell with no Lacerte/Windows-runtime dependency.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Restructure the staging layout to isolate the wipe: introduce a versioned subdirectory `$stageRoot = Join-Path $staging "LacertMCP-v$Version"` AFTER step 2 resolves $Version (currently line 43), and only `Remove-Item` that subdirectory, not `$staging` itself. Concretely: (a) delete the unconditional wipe at line 78-79; (b) after $Version is resolved, compute `$stageRoot` and `if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $stageRoot) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $stageRoot -Recurse -Force }`; (c) point `$serverStage`/`$cliStage`/$zipPath at `$stageRoot` instead of `$staging`. Add a `-Force` switch param that gates wiping a non-empty $stageRoot. Add a pre-flight guard before any Remove-Item: reject if `$staging` resolves to (or is an ancestor of) `$script:RepoRoot`, `$HOME`, or a drive root — `if ($resolved -eq $repoRoot -or $repoRoot.StartsWith($resolved, [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { throw "Refusing to wipe '$resolved' — equal to or parent of repo root." }`. Add a Pester-free smoke test (or a one-shot script under tests/) that creates a temp dir with a dummy file, runs release.ps1 -OutputDir $tempDir, and asserts the dummy file still exists alongside the new LacertMCP-v$Version/ subdir and zip. No CHANGELOG/LICENSE scope creep — those were P14-010 concerns; this is a focused destructive-behavior fix.

title: AppID GUID strings linger in the GC heap with no SecureString equivalent
description: TryCredRead allocates a managed `byte[]` from the credential blob, converts to a managed `string` via `Encoding.Unicode.GetString`, and returns it. The byte[] becomes GC-collectable but is not zeroed; the string is interned in the LOH/Gen2 heap and survives until the next compacting GC AT BEST. Same for CredWriteOrThrow: the input `value` is the GUID string already in caller memory, plus a new `blob = Encoding.Unicode.GetBytes(value)` and an unmanaged HGlobal allocation. Marshal.FreeHGlobal frees the unmanaged blob but the managed byte[] and string remain in the heap until GC. A memory dump (or a same-process info leak via a future bug) can recover the AppID GUID. The threat model is low — AppID is a GUID identifier the operator can mint freely via `register --reset` — but the symmetry with how DPAPI is meant to be used is broken.
recommendation: Convert the AppID storage and retrieval to use `SecureString` end-to-end: `TryCredRead` returns `SecureString`; the COM bridge dispatches via `SecureStringMarshal.SecureStringToCoTaskMemUnicode` only at the moment of the COM call, and frees the unmanaged buffer with `ZeroFreeCoTaskMemUnicode`. For the managed byte[] in TryCredRead, replace with `var bytes = new byte[blobSize]; ... try { value = Encoding.Unicode.GetString(bytes); } finally { Array.Clear(bytes, 0, bytes.Length); }` to at least zero the byte buffer (the GC-heap string still lingers but is shorter-lived). At minimum, zero the byte[] in both Read and Write paths in a finally block. Document the residual GC-heap exposure in DECISIONS.md.
rationale: Round 1 framed AppID as 'the secret' (DECISIONS.md) and added DPAPI storage but stopped at the persistence boundary. The in-process lifetime is the missing half of the threat model. Low severity given AppID is re-mintable but the symmetry matters for a security-audited codebase.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified the code at src/LacertMCP.Cli/Storage/AppIdStore.cs:221-283. The defect is real:
(a) TryCredRead allocates `var bytes = new byte[cred.CredentialBlobSize]` (line 238), Marshal.Copy's the credential blob into it, then GetString's it (line 240). The byte[] is never zeroed before falling out of scope — it sits on the managed heap holding plaintext UTF-16 bytes of the GUID until a GC collects it.
(b) CredWriteOrThrow (line 254) does `var blob = Encoding.Unicode.GetBytes(value)` and never zeros it either; only the unmanaged HGlobal copy is freed via Marshal.FreeHGlobal.
(c) The same pattern is mirrored in src/LacertMCP.Server/Bridge/Registration.cs:211-229 (Server's read-only duplicate).

Not a duplicate of any Phase-14 task. P14-065 only addressed channel leaks (CLI prints, error messages); no Phase-14 task touches in-process byte[]/string residency.

Two weaknesses in the finder's framing:
1. The "string is interned in the LOH/Gen2 heap" claim is technically wrong — Encoding.Unicode.GetString() produces a fresh non-interned string; LOH and string interning are unrelated concepts. The string does linger until GC but isn't pinned via interning.
2. SecureString end-to-end is over-engineering. Microsoft explicitly recommends against new SecureString usage; its guarantees on net48 are weak (data transits managed memory anyway), and the threat model is thin — the AppID is a re-mintable identifier (DECISIONS.md 2026-05-30 §"AppID GUID in Windows Credential Manager"), printed on stdout for backup, displayed via --show-app-id. Anyone who can dump this process's memory can also just call CredRead directly as the same user.

The cheap byte[]-zeroing piece is worth doing as defense-in-depth and is trivially safe; the SecureString rewrite is not justified by the threat model. Useful but low severity, as the finder concedes.

title: TaxYear floor enforced as 2018 but TY18 is documented support boundary — fence-post is silent
description: Spec §1: 'Lacerte TY18+ installed'. Spec §5 status code 25 InValidTaxYear remediation says 'Set LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR >= 2018'. The code in SetContext + SimulateCreateClient + SimulateFieldWrite uses `year < 2018` as the floor — TY2018 is accepted. But the spec also names TY21 as the schema-shift boundary and TY24 (or current year) as the upper edge of installed coverage. Three subtle holes: (1) No upper-bound check — a typo passing `year = 2098` is silently accepted and then misroutes to `GetOrAddModule` which creates a phantom in-memory cell. (2) `CanUseNewApis` returns `year >= 2021` unconditionally in sim, but a year >= 2026 still routes through that path even though no Lacerte module exists for it. (3) The Modules catalog has no per-module 'first supported year' field — e.g. Benefit (5500) shipped on a different timeline than Individual — so a 2018 Benefit context is accepted in sim and the operator only learns at live runtime that the module-year cell doesn't exist. Off-by-floor only, but worth flagging because it lights up as confusing live errors.
recommendation: Add an upper-bound sanity check: reject taxYear > (current calendar year + 1) with a clear synthetic 'TaxYearTooNew' error, since the SDK never has data for a year not yet released. Optionally extend ModuleInfo with `int FirstSupportedYear` (default 2018 for I/C/P/S, later for the specialized modules per spec's TY18 footnote) and validate per-module in SetContext. Either fix is sim-actionable; the spec-tightening is a half-day's work that closes a class of confusing live errors.
rationale: Round 1 found year-related issues (P14-009 covers ARCHITECTURE.md tax-year boundaries; P14-020 hoisted module catalog) but no finding addressed the upper-bound + per-module-floor combination. The audit task explicitly asked for 'TY18 vs TY21 vs TY24 boundaries: are off-by-one year boundaries correct in CanUseNewApis?' which this surfaces.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct file inspection. LacerteSessionManager.SetContext (line 378) and SimulateCreateClient inline check (line 907) both gate only on `year < 2018` with no upper bound. SyntheticStatusCodes.cs has TaxYearTooOld (9003) but no TaxYearTooNew counterpart. Meanwhile ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:77 ALREADY validates `taxYear > 2099` — but throws a raw `ArgumentException`, not a structured `LacerteSDKError`, so the two enforcement points are inconsistent: SetContext accepts year=2098, then a downstream Odbc.Query call would throw an unstructured ArgumentException that bypasses the LacerteSDKError envelope contract. This is a real fence-post + error-shape consistency gap.

Phase-14 duplicate scan: P14-009 (CI workflow — NOT year-boundary docs as the finding's rationale incorrectly claims), P14-020 (module catalog hoist), P14-032 (overlay per-year semantics) all touched adjacent areas but none added an upper-bound year gate, a TaxYearTooNew synthetic code, or per-module FirstSupportedYear. No Phase-14 task surfaces year-ceiling enforcement.

Caveats that tighten the recommendation: (a) the finding's "phantom in-memory cell" claim is weak — SetContext already validates module membership, so misrouting is bounded. (b) The CanUseNewApis claim (year >= 2026 routes through UpdateTaxReturn path "even though no Lacerte module exists") is technically true in sim but harmless since sim is a deterministic decision; live mode delegates to the bridge probe. (c) The per-module FirstSupportedYear half is speculative without spec citations naming which specialized modules (B/N/T/R/F) shipped on which timelines — should be deferred or dropped. The upper-bound gate is the high-value piece worth landing.

title: Single-logfile assertion races UTC midnight rollover
description: WireLog filenames are 'lacerte-' + DateTime.UtcNow.ToString('yyyyMMdd') + '.log' (Server/Logging/WireLog.cs:557). WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.FullSequence asserts Assert.Single(files) after the test writes 3 ops + 1 probe record over several seconds, and the same pattern is used by WireLogTests.WriteForTest_WritesOneJsonLine_RedactedFirst. If the test process happens to span UTC midnight (a real CI hazard for the upcoming GitHub Actions Windows runner, which the handoff notes is new in Phase 14), two files appear and Assert.Single fails. The prior audit (audit-findings.json) called this test out as flaky; the round-1 fix added FlushForTests/cache-handle plumbing to fix the FileShare race, but the date-roll race is independent and untouched.
recommendation: Replace Assert.Single(files) with a robust pattern: enumerate matching files, assert at least one exists, then pick whichever file contains the unique op tags the test emitted (e.g. the 'Redaction.Probe' marker). Or stub DateTime.UtcNow via an injectable IClock test seam. Lowest-effort fix: instead of asserting count, do `var line = files.SelectMany(f => File.ReadAllLines(f)).Last(l => l.Contains("Redaction.Probe"))` and assert on that single record.
rationale: Prior audit explicitly named this test as flaky. The round-1 fix addressed the file-handle race but left a different flake (date-roll) untouched. Likelihood is low per run but CI runs multiply odds.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed in source: WireLog.FilenameForToday() at src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs:557 uses DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyyMMdd") with no IClock seam, and the same Record/RecordSync chokepoints recompute the filename on every call — so a test that spans UTC midnight will produce two files and Assert.Single(files) fails. The finding undercounts the surface: in addition to WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:118 and WireLogTests.cs:67, the same Assert.Single(files) on Directory.GetFiles(dir, "lacerte-*.log") exists at WireLogRedactionTests.cs:219. Searched audit-findings.json for midnight/UtcNow/FilenameForToday/yyyyMMdd/date-roll — no Phase-14 finding addressed the date boundary; the round-1 fix (P14-012, FlushForTests + cached writer) only addressed the FileShare race. Real flake, low per-run probability, but the Phase-14 GitHub Actions Windows runner multiplies exposure. Fix is mechanical, requires no Windows/Lacerte, and is contained to test files.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Apply the fix to ALL THREE tests (finding missed WireLogRedactionTests.cs:219): WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:118, WireLogTests.cs:67, WireLogRedactionTests.cs:219. Replace `Assert.Single(files)` + `File.ReadAllLines(files[0])` with a date-roll-agnostic pattern: enumerate all "lacerte-*.log" files in the dir, assert at least one exists, then concatenate their lines (`files.SelectMany(File.ReadAllLines).ToList()`) before running the existing op/redaction assertions. This is preferable to an IClock seam because WireLog has no DI surface today and adding one for one test would be over-engineering. Keep the FlushForTests call before enumeration so the cached writer is closed regardless of which date's file it's pinned to. No new test required — the change strengthens existing assertions.
